boundary_rationale: The unit opens with the book's own first verse and its accession formula וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֛ק שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בֶן דָּוִ֖יד עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ ('Solomon the son of David was firmly established in his kingdom,' web:2Chr.1.1), which sets the עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ ('over his kingdom') theme that v.13 will later echo. Verses 2-6 narrate one continuous action — Solomon's summons to the nation's officials (web:2Chr.1.2) and the assembly's move to the Gibeon high place for sacrifice (web:2Chr.1.3-1.6), noting in passing why the ark at Jerusalem and the Gibeon tabernacle stood apart (web:2Chr.1.4-1.5) — closing on וַיַּ֧עַל עָלָ֛יו עֹל֖וֹת אָֽלֶף ('and offered one thousand burnt offerings on it,' web:2Chr.1.6). The next verse pivots on a temporal disjunction, בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא נִרְאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ('That night, God appeared to Solomon,' web:2Chr.1.7), switching register from public cultic action to private nocturnal theophany, so the sacrifice act is the natural close of this opening notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through v.7 to include the theophany would blur the sacrifice scene's own closure at 'a thousand burnt offerings' into an event the night-formula deliberately sets apart as a separate occasion.

boundary_rationale: בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא נִרְאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ('That night, God appeared to Solomon,' web:2Chr.1.7) opens a self-contained exchange: God's invitation to ask for anything (web:2Chr.1.7), Solomon's petition for wisdom over riches, honor, or long life (web:2Chr.1.8-1.10), and God's grant of both wisdom and the unrequested wealth (web:2Chr.1.11-1.12). It closes with the return notice, וַיָּבֹ֨א שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה לַבָּמָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר בְּגִבְעוֹן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל ('So Solomon came from the high place that was at Gibeon...to Jerusalem; and he reigned over Israel,' web:2Chr.1.13). A samekh follows v.10 (oshb:2Chr.1.10, samekh, single-witness), tier-3 evidence disclosed here that neither drives nor defeats this unit's boundary; it falls at the petition/answer hinge inside the span (petition 1:8-1:10, answer 1:11), and the question-and-answer exchange itself runs unbroken across it. The shared element between v.13's closing verb, וַיִּמְלֹ֖ךְ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and v.1's עַל מַלְכוּת֑וֹ is the root מלך (lemma citation, not itself an attested pointed form) -- מַלְכוּת is the -ut abstract noun built on that root, not the shared root, and remains the correct citation below for the noun's own recurrences, each attested with the 3ms suffix וֹ, but a book-wide check shows the same root recurring past this span, at oshb:2Chr.1.18 (= web:2Chr.2.1, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֨יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וּבַ֖יִת לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ) and again at oshb:2Chr.3.2 (וַ֠יָּחֶל לִבְנ֞וֹת בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי֙ בַּשֵּׁנִ֔י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֖ע לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ); the recurrence is a passing thematic thread running through the wider Solomon narrative, not an exclusive envelope confined to 1:1-1:13, so no inclusio claim rests on it here. A PE follows v.13 (oshb:2Chr.1.13, pe, single-witness), weak corroboration for the close. Verse 14 then opens an unrelated administrative topic, וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף שְׁלֹמֹה֮ רֶ֣כֶב וּפָרָשִׁים֒ ('Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen,' web:2Chr.1.14), so the reign-confirmation at v.13 is where this dialogue unit properly ends.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reassigning v.13 to the following wealth notice as its opening frame is the closest rival, but it would strip v.13 of its own return-and-reign-confirmation report and orphan the oracle from the narrative resolution that closes it.

boundary_rationale: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֣ף שְׁלֹמֹה֮ רֶ֣כֶב וּפָרָשִׁים֒ (web:2Chr.1.14) turns from the Gibeon oracle to a wealth-and-trade inventory -- chariots and horsemen (web:2Chr.1.14), silver, gold, and cedar made common as stone (web:2Chr.1.15), and the horse-and-chariot trade with Egypt and Kue (web:2Chr.1.16) -- running through the closing trade notice, וְ֠כֵן לְכָל מַלְכֵ֧י הַֽחִתִּ֛ים וּמַלְכֵ֥י אֲרָ֖ם בְּיָדָ֥ם יוֹצִֽיאוּ (web:2Chr.1.17), rendered by WEB as 'They also exported them to the Hittite kings and the Syrian kings.' rather than an unlabeled translator gloss. The next verse, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֨יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וּבַ֖יִת לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ (web:2Chr.2.1 = oshb:2Chr.1.18 (MT), 'Solomon decided to build a house for Yahweh's name, and a house for his kingdom'), is a 3ms wayyiqtol with Solomon as its explicit subject throughout and no independent first-person pronoun anywhere in it; the pivot from this row's third-person commercial reportage to that verse's third-person notice of royal building-resolve (a wayyiqtol plus an infinitive-of-purpose clause) is the register shift that marks the close, not a shift into first person -- the independent pronoun אֲנִי first stands three verses later -- the interval from oshb 1:18 running 2:1, 2:2, 2:3 -- at web:2Chr.2.4 = oshb:2Chr.2.3 (MT), הִנֵּה֩ אֲנִ֨י בֽוֹנֶה, which is decision M8-2Chr-005's own opening line; first-person reference has already entered Solomon's letter one verse earlier, however, at web:2Chr.2.3 = oshb:2Chr.2.2 (MT), whose כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ עִם דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֔י carries a 1cs suffix inside the direct speech opened by לֵאמֹ֑ר -- material that belongs to decision M8-2Chr-005's own span, not this row's, since it follows this row's own closing verse, web:2Chr.2.1 = oshb:1.18 (MT), by two verses. book_strategy_draft.md §6 lists this exact span, '1:14-17 (inclusio partner status),' among the campaign's roughly fifteen expected low-confidence regions, tied to the disputed 9:25-28 inclusio-partner identification; that identification is corroborating context from outside this part, not the primary boundary evidence, which rests on the in-part topic pivot on both edges (theophany-to-commerce at v.14, commerce-to-building-resolve at 2:1 = 1:18 MT).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 1:14-17 forward into the temple-decision notice as one long 'transition' unit ignores the sharp register switch from third-person commercial reportage to third-person building resolve that opens web:2Chr.2.1 (= oshb:1.18 MT), not a seam the strategy conceded doubt about -- book_strategy_draft.md §6 flags 1:14-17 only for its disputed 9:25-28 inclusio-partner status, a different question, so no strategy-level concession attaches to this register-switch seam itself.

boundary_rationale: web:2Chr.2.1 = oshb:2Chr.1.18 (MT), וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֨יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וּבַ֖יִת לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ ('Solomon decided to build a house for Yahweh's name, and a house for his kingdom'), opens the temple-preparation pericope with Solomon's own building resolve, immediately paired with the workforce count at web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT), וַיִּסְפֹּ֨ר שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ אִ֣ישׁ סַבָּ֔ל וּשְׁמוֹנִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ חֹצֵ֣ב בָּהָ֑ר וּמְנַצְּחִ֣ים עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת ('Solomon counted out seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand men who were stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them'). A PE follows this verse (web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT), pe, single-witness), weak corroboration for treating decision-plus-census as one opening notice. The next verse turns outward with a sending formula, web:2Chr.2.3 = oshb:2Chr.2.2 (MT), וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶל חוּרָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ צֹ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר ('Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying'), which begins direct diplomatic correspondence and so closes this internal notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 2:1-2 with the letter that follows into one undivided 'temple-preparation' block is the strongest rival, but it effaces the sending-formula boundary that opens direct correspondence only at web:2Chr.2.3.

boundary_rationale: The frame is explicit on both sides, satisfying the inset rule for isolating a letter as its own row: the internal decision-and-census notice closes at web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT) (with its PE), and the sending formula web:2Chr.2.3 = oshb:2Chr.2.2 (MT), וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶל חוּרָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ צֹ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר, opens direct first-person discourse — beginning at web:2Chr.2.4 = oshb:2Chr.2.3 (MT), הִנֵּה֩ אֲנִ֨י בֽוֹנֶה בַּ֜יִת לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֗י ('Behold, I am about to build a house for the name of Yahweh my God'), and continuing through the rhetorical question of God's greatness (web:2Chr.2.5-2.6), the request for a skilled craftsman (web:2Chr.2.7), and the timber and provisions request (web:2Chr.2.8-2.9) — that runs to web:2Chr.2.10 = oshb:2Chr.2.9 (MT), וְשֶׁ֕מֶן בַּתִּ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אָֽלֶף ('and oil, twenty thousand baths,' the last item Solomon promises), where a PE also falls (web:2Chr.2.10 = oshb:2Chr.2.9 (MT), pe, single-witness). The reply that follows, web:2Chr.2.11 = oshb:2Chr.2.10 (MT), וַיֹּ֨אמֶר חוּרָ֤ם מֶֽלֶךְ צֹר֙ בִּכְתָ֔ב וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה ('Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing...to Solomon'), reverses both the sending direction and the speaker, closing this request-letter as its own bounded unit within the census-framed pericope.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Combining Solomon's request and Huram's reply into a single 'letter exchange' row is plausible given their shared subject matter, but it erases the speaker-change and reply-marker (בִּכְתָ֔ב) that the text itself uses to hand the correspondence to a new voice.

boundary_rationale: Huram's own reply begins where Solomon's request left off: web:2Chr.2.11 = oshb:2Chr.2.10 (MT), וַיֹּ֨אמֶר חוּרָ֤ם מֶֽלֶךְ צֹר֙ בִּכְתָ֔ב וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה בְּאַהֲבַ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת עַמּ֔וֹ נְתָנְךָ֥ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֶֽלֶךְ, is itself a third-person narrative frame naming the responding king and marking the reply's written form with בִּכְתָ֔ב ('in writing'), reversing the sending direction against Solomon's own letter-opening at web:2Chr.2.3 = oshb:2Chr.2.2 (MT), וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶל חוּרָ֥ם; the doxology that follows at web:2Chr.2.12 = oshb:2Chr.2.11 (MT), בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ('Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel'), continues that frame as Huram's own quoted speech -- a book-wide check shows the identical phrase recurs verbatim in consonants, points, and accents at oshb:2Chr.6.4, בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, spoken by Solomon himself, so the doxology is not speaker-exclusive; the seam rests instead on the changed grammatical subject, the בִּכְתָ֔ב reply-marker, and the reversed sending direction. The commendation of Huram-abi and his lineage (web:2Chr.2.13-2.14) and the logistics for shipping the provisions (web:2Chr.2.15) run to web:2Chr.2.16 = oshb:2Chr.2.15 (MT), וְאַתָּ֛ה תַּעֲלֶ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם ('then you shall carry it up to Jerusalem,' web:2Chr.2.16), with a PE following (web:2Chr.2.16 = oshb:2Chr.2.15 (MT), pe, single-witness). Sustained third-person narrative action -- as opposed to the reply's own opening frame clause -- resumes only at the next verse, web:2Chr.2.17 = oshb:2Chr.2.16 (MT), וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כָּל הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הַגֵּירִים֙ ('Solomon counted all the foreigners'), whose opening verb וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר echoes the same verb's only other occurrence in this book, the opening census at web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT) rather than continuing Huram's letter, so this reply closes here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 2:11-16 as mere continuation of Solomon's own letter rather than an independent reply would require ignoring the explicit change of grammatical subject to Huram, the בִּכְתָ֔ב reply-marker, and the reversed sending direction, none of which depend on the doxology's wording.

boundary_rationale: The 70,000/80,000/3,600 figures from the opening census (web:2Chr.2.2 = oshb:2Chr.2.1 (MT)) recur almost verbatim at the close: web:2Chr.2.18 = oshb:2Chr.2.17 (MT), וַיַּ֨עַשׂ מֵהֶ֜ם שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ סַבָּ֔ל וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף חֹצֵ֣ב בָּהָ֑ר וּשְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת מְנַצְּחִ֖ים לְהַעֲבִ֥יד אֶת הָעָֽם ('he set of them seventy thousand to bear burdens, eighty thousand stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred overseers to assign the people their work'), closing the inclusio that frames the whole temple-preparation pericope. The bridge verse into this close, web:2Chr.2.17 = oshb:2Chr.2.16 (MT), וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה כָּל הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הַגֵּירִים֙ ('Solomon counted all the foreigners who were in the land of Israel'), drops the direct speech of Huram's letter for third-person narration opened by וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר, the same verb (וַיִּסְפֹּ֨ר) that opened the pericope's census. Beyond the pericope's end, the next verse launches construction with a different act-verb outside the offset zone, oshb:2Chr.3.1, וַיָּ֣חֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֤וֹת אֶת בֵּית יְהוָה֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם ('Then Solomon began to build Yahweh's house at Jerusalem on Mount Moriah'), whose opening וַיָּ֣חֶל ('began') decisively ends the preparatory frame and opens the construction catalog.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Absorbing 2:17-18 into Huram's reply as its logistical tail is the closest rival, but the return to third-person narration opened by וַיִּסְפֹּ֣ר and the near-verbatim repetition of the workforce figures mark an independent closing notice, not a continuation of direct speech.

boundary_rationale: 3:1 opens וַיָּ֣חֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לִבְנ֤וֹת אֶת בֵּית (gloss: "Solomon began to build the house of..."), naming site and etiology (Moriah, David's appointment, Ornan the Jebusite's threshing floor); 3:2 repeats the same inceptive verb and adds the date, בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי֙ בַּשֵּׁנִ֔י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת אַרְבַּ֖ע לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ (gloss: "in the second month, the second, in the fourth year of his reign"). The verb wayyahel ("he began") occurs only in these two verses across the whole 3:1-5:1 span (checked programmatically), so the doubled inceptive frame is a self-contained commencement notice: site, then date. It closes before 3:3, which pivots to the catalog's own header sentence, וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הוּסַ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לִבְנ֖וֹת אֶת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (gloss: "and these are [the foundations] laid for Solomon's building of the house of..."; הוּסַ֣ד is a Hophal perfect 3ms of the root ysd, a passive form, so Solomon is not this clause's grammatical agent -- WEB's own restructuring, 'Now these are the foundations which Solomon laid...,' likewise avoids treating him as the verb's subject), a list-opening device distinct in form from the narrative inceptive of 3:1-2. The opening edge continues the seam-out already fixed at Phase 0 for the part boundary following the temple-preparation chapter.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping 3:1-3 as one 'opening' unit is possible since v3 still names Solomon, but the shift from narrative notice to the list-header formula is a sharp enough genre change to seat the boundary between v2 and v3.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the catalog header וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הוּסַ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לִבְנ֖וֹת אֶת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (gloss: "and these are [the foundations] laid for Solomon's building of the house of..."; per M8-2Chr-008, הוּסַ֣ד is Hophal passive), giving foundation length/width (3), then two further named spaces: the porch, וְהָאוּלָ֡ם אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל פְּנֵ֨י הָאֹ֜רֶךְ (v4, WEB 'the porch'), and the great house/main hall, וְאֵ֣ת הַבַּ֣יִת הַגָּד֗וֹל (v5, WEB 'the larger room'), with its cypress ceiling and gold overlay and palm-tree ornament (5), precious-stone decoration with Parvaim gold (6), and full gold overlay of beams, thresholds, walls, and doors, closing וּפִתַּ֥ח כְּרוּבִ֖ים עַל הַקִּירֽוֹת (gloss: "and engraved cherubim on the walls"); a samekh follows v7 (weak corroboration, single-witness). Porch and great house are genuinely distinct named spaces, not one undifferentiated room, but both stay subordinate to the v3 header's single foundation-and-construction report, not because a fresh wayyiqtol-plus-subject test picks them out -- v4's וְהָאוּלָ֡ם and v5's וְאֵ֣ת הַבַּ֣יִת הַגָּד֗וֹל are waw-plus-noun openings, not verb-initial wayyiqtols, and 3:6's וַיְצַ֧ף and 3:7's וַיְחַ֨ף are themselves subjectless verb-initial wayyiqtols that continue the already-governing הַבַּיִת rather than opening a new unit, so 'subject' is not what the test turns on; the actual discontinuity arrives only at 3:8, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת בֵּֽית קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים (gloss: "and he made the house of the holy of holies"), a verb-initial wayyiqtol -- itself subjectless, like 3:6-3:7 -- that names בֵּֽית קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים, a space not previously governing this report -- not, as previously framed, a disappearance of house/great-house vocabulary, since a consonantal sweep confirms that root occurs in every verse from 3:3 through 3:8 (twice in 3:8's own construct chain and measuring phrase), missing only from 3:9.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The porch/great-house naming shift at vv4-5 is the genuinely strongest rejected alternative -- a real seam candidate, not the undifferentiated space this row once claimed -- but neither verse opens with its own wayyiqtol-plus-subject the way 3:8's fresh construct does, so both stay inside the v3 header's single foundation report.

boundary_rationale: Opens naming the room, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת בֵּֽית קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים (gloss: "and he made the house of the holy of holies"), reusing 3:4's עַל פְּנֵ֤י רֹֽחַב הַבַּ֨יִת֙ formula and its twenty-cubit width for this different space, though not 3:3's sixty-cubit length (שִׁשִּׁ֔ים), which is not repeated (8); v9's coda names the nail-weight, then a second, distinct location, וְהָעֲלִיּ֖וֹת חִפָּ֥ה זָהָֽב (gloss: "and the upper rooms he overlaid with gold") -- a brief aside inside the same report on Solomon's unnamed-subject construction work, not part of the holy-of-holies room itself. V10 resumes with the same room named again, now in a locative slot: v8's אֶת בֵּֽית קֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֔ים (accusative אֶת) becomes v10's בְּבֵֽית קֹ֤דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ (locative prefix בְּ) in וַיַּ֜עַשׂ בְּבֵֽית קֹ֤דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים֙ כְּרוּבִ֣ים שְׁנַ֔יִם (gloss: "and he made in the house of the holy of holies two cherubim") -- not a byte-identical rerun of v8's phrase, but the same room continuing to govern the unit rather than a fresh location -- the test that separates this from v15's pivot below, where the locative names a place not previously governing this unit -- and the two carved gold cherubim with their wingspans run 10-13. The unit closes with the veil, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ אֶת הַפָּרֹ֔כֶת (gloss: "and he made the veil"), which carries no locative of its own; its attachment here rests instead on the כְּרוּבִֽים catchword closing v14 answering the cherubim of 10-13, not on any stated location. It closes before v15, which relocates the action to a genuinely new place, וַיַּ֜עַשׂ לִפְנֵ֤י הַבַּ֨יִת֙ עַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֔יִם (gloss: "and he made before the house two pillars"), whose לִפְנֵ֤י הַבַּ֨יִת֙ never governs any verse in 8-14 and so cannot be read as continuing this report -- outside the interior entirely.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The mark cluster (samekh after 3:13, samekh after 3:14, both single-witness) could be read as favoring a split between the cherubim-images clause (10-13) and the veil notice (14), but both stay bound by the shared כְּרוּבִֽים catchword (v10's cherubim, v14's cherubim on the veil) with no subject change, and marks are tier-3 weak, never drivers.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the locative pivot וַיַּ֜עַשׂ לִפְנֵ֤י הַבַּ֨יִת֙ עַמּוּדִ֣ים שְׁנַ֔יִם (gloss: "and he made before the house two pillars"), moving the report outside the interior spaces catalogued in 8-14 for the first time since v3's foundation notice. The three verses form one action sequence on a single object-pair: fabrication with capital measure (15), chain ornament for the pillars (16 -- WEB 'chains in the inner sanctuary,' בַּדְּבִ֔יר, a term found only here and at 4:20 in chs 3-4; the pillars themselves remain the exterior objects named at v15 and set up 'before the temple,' עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַהֵיכָ֔ל, at v17, so this is read as a crux describing how, or in whose style, the chains were made, rather than relocating the pillars indoors -- flagged rather than resolved here), and erection-with-naming, closing וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם הימיני הַיְמָנִי֙ יָכִ֔ין (gloss: "and he called the name of the right-hand one Jachin"; הימיני is ketiv and הַיְמָנִי֙ is qere) -- Boaz follows for the left. Chapter 3 ends here; a samekh also follows this closing verse (oshb:2Chr.3.17, samekh, single-witness), alongside the samekh already disclosed after v15. It closes before 4:1, a fresh object opening chapter 4 with an explicit new material label, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח נְחֹ֔שֶׁת (gloss: "and he made an altar of bronze"), unseen in the gold-dominated report of chapter 3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A samekh follows 3:15 (single-witness, weak), which might tempt isolating v15 alone from the chain-and-naming notices in 16-17, but fabrication, ornament, and installation-with-naming form one uninterrupted action on the same referent and read better as a single installation report.

boundary_rationale: Opens the chapter on a freestanding object, וַיַּ֨עַשׂ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח נְחֹ֔שֶׁת (gloss: "and he made an altar of bronze"), then the molten sea (2-5), ten wash-basins (6), ten gold lampstands and ten tables set in the hall (7-8), the priests' court with bronze-plated doors (9), and the sea's placement, closing וְאֶת הַיָּ֗ם נָתַ֞ן מִכֶּ֧תֶף (gloss: "and the sea he set from the shoulder..."). Checked programmatically, no proper name (neither Solomon nor Huram) appears anywhere in 4:1-10, though Solomon is named as the subject governing this construction work two verses earlier, at both 3:1 (וַיָּ֣חֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה) and 3:3 (הוּסַ֣ד שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה); the construction verbs of 4:1-10 continue that same unnamed-in-context 3rd-person builder without renaming him, while the descriptive clauses at 4:3-4:5 take the sea and its oxen as grammatical subject instead -- סוֹבְבִ֣ים/מַקִּיפִ֥ים ('surrounding'/'encircling') at 4:3, עוֹמֵ֞ד ('standing') at 4:4, and מַחֲזִ֣יק/יָכִֽיל ('holding'/'could hold') at 4:5 -- before the construction verbs resume at 4:6. It closes before v11, where וַיַּ֣עַשׂ חוּרָ֔ם אֶת הַ֨סִּיר֔וֹת (gloss: "and Huram made the pots") switches the grammatical subject to a named craftsman for the first time in this catalog.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The material/location pattern near v7 is a real seam candidate, corroborated by samekh marks after 4:1, 4:5, 4:6, and 4:7 (single-witness, weak, all four now disclosed); but it does not run cleanly bronze-court(1-6)/gold-hall(7-10) as first framed -- gold appears only at 4:7-8 (the lampstands and tables set 'in the hall'), while bronze returns at 4:9's court doors, וְדַלְתוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם צִפָּ֥ה נְחֹֽשֶׁת, and 4:10 places the sea, itself a court object; the true pattern is a hall(7-8)/court(9-10) alternation, not a two-part material split. It is rejected in either form because book_strategy_draft.md §5 directs the construction chapters (3-4) be kept coarse as register-catalogs, and the subject-attribution seam at v11 -- corroborated by the zero-hit name-sweep above -- is the stronger, unambiguous divider.

boundary_rationale: Opens naming Huram as subject, וַיַּ֣עַשׂ חוּרָ֔ם אֶת הַ֨סִּיר֔וֹת (gloss: "and Huram made the pots"), with the items list, אֶת הַ֨סִּיר֔וֹת וְאֶת הַיָּעִ֖ים וְאֶת הַמִּזְרָק֑וֹת (gloss: "...the pots, the shovels, and the basins"), then the completion-plus-heading clause וַיְכַ֣ל חירם (ketiv) חוּרָ֗ם (qere) לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים (gloss: "and Huram finished doing the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God") -- the only finite כלה ('finish') form in chapters 3-5. What follows this clause is not a new independent report but an appositional itemization of 'the work' just named: pillars, bowls, capitals, networks, pomegranates, bases, basins, the sea and its oxen (12-15), and no wayyiqtol at all runs from v12 through v17 -- v16's עָשָׂ֞ה חוּרָ֥ם אָבִ֛יו ('Huram-abi ... made,' his remaining bronze tools) and v17's יְצָקָ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ ('the king cast them,' the Jordan-plain casting site) are full qatal predicates naming two distinct explicit agents, not appositional continuations of v11's heading, though still carrying no wayyiqtol of their own; a single-witness SAMEKH follows v11 itself, weak corroboration for treating v11 as its own closing unit, but the absence of any wayyiqtol through v17 argues instead that v11's clause is a heading caption for the recap rather than a self-contained completion report, so the seam is not adopted here. The unit's actual closing tally comes only at v18, וַיַּ֧עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה כָּל הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָרֹ֣ב מְאֹ֑ד כִּ֛י לֹ֥א נֶחְקַ֖ר מִשְׁקַ֥ל הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת (gloss: "Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance, for the weight of the bronze was not measured") -- not a subject-restoration, since v17's own subject, הַמֶּלֶךְ ('the king'), is already Solomon; the tally rests instead on v18's own summarizing כָּל הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָרֹ֣ב מְאֹ֑ד and the unmeasured-bronze coda, which nothing in 12-17 carries -- not, as previously framed, a lexical inclusio with v11, since bronze itself is named only at v16 and v18, never at v11; what the material sweep does support is gold's total absence across 11-18 against its presence in every verse of 19-22, and a PE follows v18 (single-witness). It closes before 4:19, where an almost identical 'made all the vessels' formula, וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֵ֚ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (gloss: "Solomon made all the vessels that were [in] the house of God"), reopens for a materially distinct, gold-only inventory.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v11 from 12-18 at the SAMEKH is the row's live internal rival -- v11's own וַיְכַ֣ל...לַעֲשׂוֹת֙ אֶת הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים clause could read as a stand-alone completion report -- but the list it introduces is entirely appositional (verbless or qatal, no new wayyiqtol subject until v18), so v11 functions as the recap's heading rather than its own closed unit; treating v18 instead as the opening line of the next unit (paired with 19-22 as one long 'all the vessels' summary) is tempting given the phrasal echo, but v18's own clause names bronze specifically as the closing tally's subject matter, tying it to Huram's recap rather than to the gold catalog that follows.

boundary_rationale: Opens with וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֵ֚ת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (gloss: "Solomon made all the vessels that were [in] the house of God"), a clause that shares its subject, verb form, and 'all the vessels' object with the immediately preceding v18, וַיַּ֧עַשׂ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה כָּל הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לָרֹ֣ב מְאֹ֑ד כִּ֛י לֹ֥א נֶחְקַ֖ר מִשְׁקַ֥ל הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת (gloss: "Solomon made all these vessels...") -- a formula doublet, not a subject-restoration, since Solomon is already the explicit subject of the identical wayyiqtol one verse earlier (a name-sweep across 3:1-4:22 confirms Solomon named at 3:1, 3:3, 4:11, 4:16, 4:18, and 4:19, with only 4:11 and 4:16 genuinely benefactive -- 'for king Solomon' -- and 4:18/4:19 sharing subject and verb). What separates the two is not the subject but the material: every verse from 19-22 names gold -- golden altar and show-bread tables (19), lampstands of pure gold (20), flowers, lamps, and tongs of purest gold (21), and closing וּפֶ֣תַח הַ֠בַּיִת דַּלְתוֹתָ֨יו הַפְּנִימִיּ֜וֹת לְקֹ֣דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁ֗ים וְדַלְתֵ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת לַהֵיכָ֖ל זָהָֽב (gloss: "and the entrance of the house, its inner doors for the holy of holies, and the doors of the house for the main hall, gold") -- while bronze, which closed the immediately preceding tally at v18 (מִשְׁקַ֥ל הַנְּחֹֽשֶׁת), never recurs; checked programmatically, every verse 19-22 contains the word for gold and none contains the word for bronze, the reverse of 19-22's gold saturation, not a symmetric mirror, since bronze within 11-18 is itself confined to only two of its eight verses (16 and 18), while gold is absent from all eight. The disclosed PE after v18 (single-witness) offers weak further corroboration for a seam at exactly this doublet. It closes before 5:1, where the discourse shifts from itemized 'he made X' clauses to a summary completion statement.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Appending 4:19-22 to the Huram unit (11-18) as one long inventory is possible, but the explicit renaming of Solomon as subject and the total absence of bronze vocabulary mark a fresh, materially distinct list rather than a continuation of Huram's bronze recap.

boundary_rationale: וַתִּשְׁלַם֙ כָּל הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה (gloss: "and all the work that Solomon did was completed") breaks the repeated wayyaas ("he made") item-notice pattern -- verified programmatically at sixteen occurrences across 3:8-4:19 -- with a feminine completion verb agreeing with 'the work' itself as grammatical subject: a discourse-level closure, not another manufacture clause. The same verse's deposit notice, וַיָּבֵ֨א שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אֶת קָדְשֵׁ֣י דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֗יו וְאֶת הַכֶּ֤סֶף וְאֶת הַזָּהָב֙ וְאֶת כָּל הַכֵּלִ֔ים נָתַ֕ן בְּאֹצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים (gloss: "and Solomon brought in the dedicated things of David his father... and put [them] in the treasuries of God's house"), belongs to the same closing unit, reporting Solomon's final act before the narrative reopens with the assembly summons. A samekh+pe double mark follows (single-witness; the doubling is disclosed, not treated as double-strength evidence). It closes before 5:2's assembly-summons opening, a fresh scene outside this part's range.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Appending 5:1 to the preceding gold-vessels row (4:19-22) as its capstone verse is the closest rival, but the shift from itemized 'he made' clauses to a summary completion-and-deposit statement is a strong enough genre change -- and the book strategy's Phase-0 crosswalk already seats the part boundary here -- for it to stand alone.

boundary_rationale: This unit opens on אָז֩ ('then'), immediately after the completion formula that closed the temple-construction section at 5:1 (וַתִּשְׁלַם֙ כָּל הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה...), a verse carrying one of the book's two double-mark verses (SAMEKH+PE, single-witness; the other is 13:3's SAMEKH+SAMEKH) -- weak corroboration only, since tier-3 marks in Writings neither drive nor confirm a boundary on their own. WEB's 'Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel... to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark' (v2, אָז֩ יַקְהֵ֨יל שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה...) is answered directly by v3's fulfillment, 'all the men of Israel assembled themselves to the king' (וַיִּקָּהֲל֧וּ אֶל הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ...), echoing the same root as v2's opening verb, and v3 closes on its own dated notice, 'at the feast, which was in the seventh month' (בֶּחָ֑ג ה֖וּא הַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִעִֽי). V4a, וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ כֹּ֖ל זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ('all the elders of Israel came'), still names the identical elders-of-Israel body summoned at v2 (אֶת זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל) and reads as the summons frame's own continuation rather than new material; the genuinely new action begins only at v4b, 'the Levites took up the ark' (וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ הַלְוִיִּ֖ם אֶת הָאָרֽוֹן), which starts the physical procession. The whole-verse cut at v3/v4 remains the practical edge -- v3's own dated close is a natural resting point before the ark itself is touched -- but the case rests on that dated closure and the summons/response root-echo, not on v4 as a whole marking a clean subject-and-verb change.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 5:2-10 as one unbroken procession scene erases the summons/response symmetry that gives vv2-3 their own closed shape before the Levites act at v4b; splitting instead at v4a/v4b, inside v4, is the finer-grained alternative the whole-verse cut declines in favor of the dated closural formula at v3.

boundary_rationale: Verse 4's opening clause, וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ כֹּ֖ל זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ('all the elders of Israel came'), is a bare wayyiqtol continuing 5:3's וַיִּקָּהֲל֧וּ with no fronted element and no particle, and its subject is the identical body Solomon summoned at v2 (אֶת זִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל) -- not a change of grammatical subject, as decision M8-2Chr-016 now also states. The genuinely new material sits in v4's second clause, וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ הַלְוִיִּ֖ם אֶת הָאָרֽוֹן ('the Levites took up the ark'), which starts the procession's own action for the first time. The scene then tracks one continuous movement: bearing the ark and Tent of Meeting up (v5), sacrificing innumerable flocks en route (v6 -- the span's one genuinely disjunctive clause, וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וְכָל עֲדַ֧ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הַנּוֹעָדִ֥ים עָלָ֖יו לִפְנֵ֣י הָאָר֑וֹן מְזַבְּחִים֙, waw plus fronted compound subject plus participle, widening the cast to king-and-whole-assembly), and installing the ark beneath the cherubim in the inner sanctuary (vv7-8). It closes on two scribal asides that both read as closural: the poles-visibility note ending 'there to this day' (וַֽיְהִי שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה, v9) and the ark-contents note recalling the Horeb tablets (אֵ֚ין בָּֽאָר֔וֹן רַ֚ק שְׁנֵ֣י הַלֻּח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥ן מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּחֹרֵ֑ב, v10); WLC marks a single-witness PE right after v10, a small extra nod toward the same edge. Verse 11 opens a new temporal clause shifting focus from the ark itself to the priests leaving the holy place and the massed choir, arguing against extending this unit further.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v4 itself -- treating v4a as still part of decision M8-2Chr-016's summons unit and only v4b as this unit's true opening -- is rejected in favor of the whole-verse cut adopted here because 016's own dated closural formula at 5:3 (בֶּחָ֑ג ה֖וּא הַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִעִֽי, 'at the feast, which was in the seventh month') and the summons/response root-echo (יַקְהֵ֨יל/וַיִּקָּהֲל֧וּ) together close 5:2-3 before v4 opens, not merely because the sub-verse split overstates the syntax; a further, weaker alternative -- folding vv4-6 backward into 016's summons unit outright, since v4a shares its subject with v2/v3 -- is rejected because the procession's own action (the ark-lifting) and destination only begin at v4b, giving vv4-10 a coherent movement-and-installation shape distinct from the summons proper.

boundary_rationale: The opening clause of v11 (וַיְהִ֕י בְּצֵ֥את הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים מִן הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ כִּ֠י כָּל הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַֽנִּמְצְאִים֙ הִתְקַדָּ֔שׁוּ...) pulls attention from the ark's placement to the priestly withdrawal and the long description of the Levitical singers, Asaph/Heman/Jeduthun, and the hundred-twenty trumpeting priests (11b-13a), a stage-setting aside kept here because its whole purpose is to prepare the doxology it introduces. That doxology, 'For he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever' (כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ, v13), is genuinely rare: a book-wide check of 2Chr_oshb.txt turns up the full two-clause form only here and at 7:3 (7:6 carries a shorter single-clause cousin, לְהֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּֽי לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֔וֹ, describing the instruments David made rather than repeating the congregation's cry, so it is not a third occurrence of the pair). The cloud that immediately fills the house closes the unit on divine acceptance (וְהַבַּ֛יִת מָלֵ֥א עָנָ֖ן בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה), ending 'for Yahweh's glory filled God's house' (כִּֽי מָלֵ֥א כְבוֹד יְהוָ֖ה אֶת בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים, v14) -- WLC's single-witness PE after this verse adds its usual thin support to the edge. 6:1 then pivots to Solomon's own speech with the same pivot-word that opened 5:2 (אָ֖ז אָמַ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה יְהוָ֣ה אָמַ֔ר לִשְׁכּ֖וֹן בָּעֲרָפֶֽל...), a genuine new beat rather than a continuation.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the priestly/choir aside (11b-13a) from the doxology-and-cloud (13b-14) would strand a stage direction from the very event it exists to stage, against the inset principle that frames travel with what they introduce.

boundary_rationale: אָ֖ז אָמַ֣ר שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה יְהוָ֣ה אָמַ֔ר לִשְׁכּ֖וֹן בָּעֲרָפֶֽל ('Then Solomon said, Yahweh has said he would dwell in the thick darkness') answers the cloud that has just filled the house, and pairs structurally with the assembly's own opening at 5:2 as the complex's two hinge-openings. The two verses form a closed couplet with no named human addressee -- 'I have built you a house and home, a place for you to dwell in forever' (וּמָכ֥וֹן לְשִׁבְתְּךָ֖ עוֹלָמִֽים, v2). Verse 3 changes both grammatical subject and addressee: 'the king turned his face, and blessed all the assembly of Israel,' a deliberate gesture toward a named audience that opens the next unit rather than continuing this one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 6:1-3 as one continuous introduction to the blessing speech is plausible since v3 frames the speech that follows, but the turn from reflecting on Yahweh's dwelling to physically facing a named audience is a real seam, and the couplet's self-contained parallelism argues for its own boundary.

boundary_rationale: 'The king turned his face, and blessed all the assembly of Israel; and all the assembly of Israel stood' (וַיַּסֵּ֤ב הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶת פָּנָ֔יו וַיְבָ֕רֶךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל..., v3) is the frame for the direct speech opening at v4, 'He said, Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel,... and has with his hands fulfilled it,' (וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל...וּבְיָדָ֥יו מִלֵּ֖א) -- the same assembly named in the frame is still standing through the speech. The recital moves from the choice of Jerusalem and David (vv5-6) to the transfer of the building charge from David to Solomon (vv7-9), closing on Solomon's two-verse fulfillment report: v10's 'Yahweh has performed his word that he spoke' (וַיָּ֣קֶם יְהוָ֔ה אֶת דְּבָר֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֵּ֑ר), the nearer thematic echo of v4's promise-fulfilled announcement even though it shares no root with v4's מִלֵּ֖א (קום, not מלא), and v11's own placement notice, 'there I have set the ark, in which is Yahweh's covenant' (וָאָשִׂ֥ים שָׁם֙ אֶת הָ֣אָר֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֖ם בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה) -- together a two-verse resolution of what v4 announced, not a single lexically-repeated inclusio. Verse 12 opens a new action clause, 'he stood before Yahweh's altar,' shifting Solomon's posture and addressee from the assembly to God and beginning the prayer's own frame. A near-verbatim echo of v4's promise-fulfilled formula recurs at 6:15 (וַתְּדַבֵּ֥ר בְּפִ֛יךָ וּבְיָדְךָ֥ מִלֵּ֖אתָ, 'you have spoken with your mouth, and fulfilled it with your hand,' restating v4's דִּבֶּ֣ר בְּפִ֔יו...וּבְיָדָ֥יו מִלֵּ֖א in the second person) -- a sweep of chapter 6 confirms the מלא root in this sense occurs at exactly these two places, 6:4 and 6:15 -- but 6:15 falls inside decision M8-2Chr-021's own prayer span, addressed to God rather than to the assembly; the change of addressee from the blessing's assembly (vv3-11) to the prayer's God (vv12ff) is what keeps 6:3-11 closed at v11/v12 despite the closer lexical echo at 6:15, not the weaker, root-different echo at v10 alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping v11 with the altar-standing of v12 as one transition would break the speech's own arc, since v4 announces the promise as fulfilled and vv10-11 report that fulfillment in Solomon's own voice as the recital's proper close, even though the echo across the pair is thematic rather than a repeated root.

boundary_rationale: 'He stood before Yahweh's altar... and spread out his hands' (וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֗ד לִפְנֵי֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה נֶ֖גֶד כָּל קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּפְרֹ֖שׂ, v12) stages the prayer physically, interrupted by a parenthetical note on the bronze platform Solomon had made (כִּֽי עָשָׂ֨ה שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה כִּיּ֣וֹר נְחֹ֗שֶׁת וַֽיִּתְּנֵהוּ֮ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעֲזָרָה֒...) and knelt on, closing 'and spread out his hands toward heaven' (וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ כַּפָּ֖יו הַשָּׁמָֽיְמָה, v13) -- the same kind of aside as the priestly/choir parenthesis at 5:11b-13, kept here for the identical reason: it exists only to prepare the speech-act that follows. The prayer proper opens at v14 (וַיֹּאמַ֗ר יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֵין כָּמ֣וֹךָ אֱלֹהִ֔ים בַּשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּבָאָ֑רֶץ..., 'there is no God like you... who keep covenant and loving kindness'), and builds through the dynastic petition, both parts opening on the anaphoric וְעַתָּ֞ה ('and now,' vv16-17 -- an address-to-petition pivot recurring three times in this prayer alone, at 16, 17, and again at 41, וְעַתָּ֗ה -- treated here as an internal rhetorical joint inside one continuous address rather than a unit-opening formula, since the whole of vv14-21 remains one uninterrupted speech from the same speaker to the same addressee) to the general request that Yahweh's 'eyes may be open toward this house day and night' (לִהְיוֹת֩ עֵינֶ֨יךָ פְתֻח֜וֹת אֶל הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה, v20) and 'when you hear, forgive' (וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֖ וְסָלָֽחְתָּ, v21) -- a formula that is itself a one-off in the book (this exact adjacent pairing occurs nowhere else in 2Chr) and whose forgiveness element does not recur as such in every later case: a book-wide sweep of 6:22-39 finds the forgiveness root only at vv25, 27, 30, and 39 (the defeat, drought, plague, and exile cases), while the oath (v23), foreigner (v33), and battle (v35) cases close instead on a verb of doing ('hear from heaven, act, and judge your servants,', 'and do according to all that the foreigner calls to you for;', 'hear from heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.'); what does recur in every one of the seven later cases is the 'hear from heaven' idiom, though not uniformly worded: the מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם ('from heaven') preposition is present in six of the seven cases (23, 25, 30, 33, 35, 39) and absent only at 6:27, which reads תִּשְׁמַ֣ע הַשָּׁמַ֗יִם without מִן. Verse 22 opens the first such case with its own conditional, 'if a man sins against his neighbor' (אִם יֶחֱטָ֥א אִישׁ֙ לְרֵעֵ֔הוּ וְנָֽשָׁא ב֥וֹ אָלָ֖ה לְהַֽאֲלֹת֑וֹ...), a distinct form marking the transition into the petition series.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the posture-notice (12-13) from the prayer's address (14-21) would isolate a bare stage direction with no independent content, against the same inset logic that keeps 5:11b-13 with the doxology it stages; splitting again at vv16-17's וְעַתָּ֞ה would over-fragment a single uninterrupted address into pieces smaller than the petition series' own protasis-marked cases that follow, none of which this prayer's own structure treats as a fresh unit boundary. A third rival reads 6:20-21 as heading the case series that follows rather than closing this row's own address, since v21's וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֖ וְסָלָֽחְתָּ ('when you hear, forgive') is precisely the unconditioned hear-and-forgive pairing the calamity cases individually instantiate (the hear-idiom recurs at 6:23,25,27,30,33,35,39, with the forgive-verb added at 25,27,30,39); this is rejected because v21 itself carries no protasis, while v22's אִם יֶחֱטָ֥א opens the conditional chain proper, so v21 belongs to this row's general petition rather than to the case series it anticipates.

boundary_rationale: Four petitions make up this panel, each triggered by its own conditional and each closing on its own mark -- SAMEKH after v23, PE after v25, SAMEKH after v27, SAMEKH after v31, four marks for four sub-cases (all single-witness, weak, never drivers): an individual's oath dispute (אִם יֶחֱטָ֥א אִישׁ֙ לְרֵעֵ֔הוּ וְנָֽשָׁא ב֥וֹ אָלָ֖ה לְהַֽאֲלֹת֑וֹ..., v22), national defeat with repentance (וְֽאִם יִנָּגֵ֞ף עַמְּךָ֧ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לִפְנֵ֥י אוֹיֵ֖ב כִּ֣י יֶֽחֶטְאוּ לָ֑ךְ..., v24 -- sharing its sin-clause כִּ֣י יֶֽחֶטְאוּ לָ֑ךְ byte-for-byte with v26's drought case, a lexical bond the oath case at vv22-23 does not share), drought (בְּהֵעָצֵ֧ר הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם וְלֹֽא יִהְיֶ֥ה מָטָ֖ר כִּ֣י יֶֽחֶטְאוּ לָ֑ךְ..., v26), and a compounding list of famine, pestilence, blight, and siege (רָעָ֞ב כִּֽי יִהְיֶ֣ה בָאָ֗רֶץ..., v28), all resolved by the repeated 'hear from heaven' idiom (vv23,25,27,30). Verse 31 closes the group with a purpose clause, 'that they may fear you, to walk in your ways' (לְמַ֣עַן יִֽירָא֗וּךָ לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ בִּדְרָכֶ֔יךָ...), the fourth of these four consecutive marked closes; the following panel (6:32-39) carries no internal marks at all, a real asymmetry against this one, but the marks corroborate an already-independent tier-1 pattern (each sub-case opens its own protasis-apodosis) rather than driving the grouping, and a four-way split into vv22-23/24-25/26-27/28-31 is rejected below rather than silently passed over. Verse 32 marks a deliberate pivot (וְגַ֣ם אֶל הַנָּכְרִ֗י אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֥א מֵעַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ הוּא֒...), which WEB renders 'Moreover, concerning the foreigner' -- the prayer's only case introduced by an explicit topic-shift particle rather than a bare conditional.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two rivals compete with the chosen four-petition panel. The more textually grounded is a cleavage at 6:23/6:24: the oath case (22-23) is individual and judicial, granting no forgiveness, while 6:24, 6:26, and 6:28-31 are national and share resolution tissue the oath case lacks (the byte-identical sin-clause at 6:24/6:26, כִּ֣י יֶֽחֶטְאוּ לָ֑ךְ, and the forgiveness verb at 6:25/6:27/6:30); this reads as a real internal seam rejected here only because the campaign's granularity for this prayer groups protasis-marked cases at the panel level (matching decisions M8-2Chr-021's and M8-2Chr-023's panel-sized grain), not because the oath case is textually indistinguishable from the other three. The coarser rival, treating vv22-39 as one uninterrupted catalog, is defensible given the shared refrain but buries the marked pivot at v32, the strongest internal seam the prayer supplies. A third, finer rival divides the panel four ways, at vv22-23/24-25/26-27/28-31, one petition per mark; this is rejected because the four single-witness marks corroborate an already-independent tier-1 pattern (each sub-case opens its own protasis-apodosis) rather than driving the grouping, and the panel-sized grain here matches the grain decisions M8-2Chr-021 and M8-2Chr-023 use for this same prayer.

boundary_rationale: This panel opens on the explicit pivot already marked at v32, 'and also concerning the foreigner who is not of your people Israel' (וְגַ֣ם אֶל הַנָּכְרִ֗י אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֥א מֵעַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ הוּא֒...), moves to a battle-abroad petition with its own conditional, 'if your people go out to battle' (כִּֽי יֵצֵ֨א עַמְּךָ֤ לַמִּלְחָמָה֙..., v34), and reaches the captivity petition, 'if they sin against you (for there is no man who doesn't sin)' (כִּ֣י יֶחֶטְאוּ לָ֗ךְ כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין אָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא יֶחֱטָ֔א, v36) -- a universalizing parenthetical about humanity that is not, however, unique to this case: v30's plague-cluster petition already closes on the same device, כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ לְבַדְּךָ֣ יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת לְבַ֖ב בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם ('for you, even you only, know the hearts of the children of men'), with v29 already widening scope to לְכָל הָ֣אָדָ֔ם (gloss: 'all mankind') a verse earlier still; nor is the captivity case markedly longer by consonant count (a book-wide character count places it within two percent of the famine-and-siege case, 304 against 299). What genuinely sets this case apart is narrower than a full exile-and-return sequence: the setting itself, captivity in a foreign land (בְּאֶ֤רֶץ שִׁבְיָם֙, vv37-38), is what this case alone supplies -- the directional prayer toward the city and the house that vv37-38 add is already shared with 6:34's own אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחַ֣רְתָּ בָּ֔הּ...אֲשֶׁר בָּנִ֥יתִי לִשְׁמֶֽךָ, and the turning-and-restoration element already appears at 6:24's וְשָׁ֨בוּ and 6:25's וַהֲשֵׁיבוֹתָם֙ -- only the foreign-captivity setting is unique to this case, signaling the climactic weight toward exile and return. Verse 39 closes on 'forgive your people who have sinned against you' (וְסָלַחְתָּ֥ לְעַמְּךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָֽטְאוּ לָֽךְ), the series' final resolution. With no mark disclosed at this exact 39/40 seam, verse 40 shifts register from third-person conditionals to a direct plea, 'now, my God, let, I beg you, your eyes be open' (עַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֗י יִֽהְיוּ נָ֤א עֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ פְּתֻח֔וֹת), whose precative נָא carries the register change, echoing v20's 'eyes... open' language and closing the whole series with a summarizing address rather than adding another case. A single-witness SAMEKH follows v40 itself (weak, non-driving), read as internal to decision M8-2Chr-024's own 40-42 unit -- separating v40's entreaty from v41's imperative escalation there, per that row's own account -- rather than as support for pulling v40 back into this panel, since it falls one verse after this row's own v39 close, not at the 39/40 seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this panel through v42 would merge the third-person petition idiom with the imperative closing invocation ('arise, Yahweh God'), a distinct liturgical register, not another conditional case.

boundary_rationale: Verse 40's plea, 'now, my God, let, I beg you, your eyes be open, and let your ears be attentive to the prayer that is made in this place' (עַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֗י יִֽהְיוּ נָ֤א עֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ פְּתֻח֔וֹת וְאָזְנֶ֖יךָ קַשֻּׁב֑וֹת לִתְפִלַּ֖ת הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה), recaps the 'eyes open' language of v20 and closes the conditional-petition series; its opening עַתָּ֣ה is bare, without the vav that prefixes every other verse-initial occurrence of this particle in the prayer (וְעַתָּ֞ה at 6:16, וְעַתָּ֕ה at 6:17, and וְעַתָּ֗ה at 6:41). WLC places a single-witness SAMEKH after v40. A book-wide sweep of the vav-prefixed form shows it does not reliably bind backward: an independent sweep confirms the form occurs at fifteen verse-initial addresses in 2Chr -- three inside this prayer (6:16, 6:17, 6:41) and twelve outside it (web:2Chr.2.7 = oshb:2Chr.2.6 (MT), web:2Chr.2.13 = oshb:2Chr.2.12 (MT), web:2Chr.2.15 = oshb:2Chr.2.14 (MT), 7:16, 10:11, 13:8, 18:22, 19:7, 20:10, 28:10, 28:11, 32:15) -- and at 6:16 and 6:17 it pivots from the historical recital to a fresh petition without opening a new unit, since 6:14-21 is one continuous address, Solomon speaking to God throughout with no change of interlocutor; v41's וְעַתָּ֗ה קוּמָ֞ה is the same kind of internal pivot, not proof of tight binding to v40 by itself, so the mark and the particle chain are both weaker grounds than this row previously claimed. Two further shifts mark v41 as a genuine intensification: the divine address changes from the first-person-suffixed אֱלֹהַ֗י (v40) to the compound יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ (vv41-42), and the mood shifts from jussive-plus-entreaty (יִֽהְיוּ נָ֤א) to a run of bare imperatives (קוּמָ֞ה, אַל תָּשֵׁ֖ב, זָכְרָ֕ה). Read as escalation rather than a fresh address, vv40-42 form one closing crescendo -- entreaty rising into summons -- and 7:1's own retrospective frame, וּכְכַלּ֤וֹת שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל ('when Solomon had finished praying'), treats the whole of 6:14-42 as a single, undifferentiated act of prayer without distinguishing an entreaty sub-unit from an imperative one, which is the textual anchor this row rests on for keeping 40-42 together as the prayer's own closing movement. The unit closes with 'remember your loving kindnesses to David your servant' (יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים אַל תָּשֵׁ֖ב פְּנֵ֣י מְשִׁיחֶ֑יךָ זָכְרָ֕ה לְחַֽסְדֵ֖י דָּוִ֥יד עַבְדֶּֽךָ, v42, PE, single-witness); 7:1 then opens the new theophany scene.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v40/v41 on the SAMEKH plus the appellation and mood shift is now the genuinely stronger rival than this row once credited -- OL's book-wide check shows the very adverbial chain this row leaned on does not reliably bind backward elsewhere in the same prayer -- but it is declined because 7:1's retrospective 'finished praying' frame treats all of 6:14-42 as one undifferentiated act, giving no textual warrant for a boundary between an entreaty phase and an imperative phase inside that single closing movement. That same undifferentiated-act framing does not, however, forbid the 6:11|6:12, 6:21|6:22, 6:31|6:32, and 6:39|6:40 seams that decisions M8-2Chr-020 through M8-2Chr-023 draw within this same prayer, because none of those rows invokes 7:1 as its own warrant; each rests instead on directly observable internal shifts -- addressee change, topic pivot, conditional-clause structure -- that 7:1's summary characterization of the whole prayer as one act of praying neither confirms nor contradicts. This row's own case for 40-42 rests on the in-prayer evidence assembled above (bare particle vs. conjunctive pattern, the appellation shift, and the mood escalation), with 7:1 offered only as a supplementary frame for this seam specifically, at 6:42|7:1, not as a general principle barring internal structure elsewhere in the prayer.

boundary_rationale: 'When Solomon had finished praying' (וּכְכַלּ֤וֹת שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֔ל וְהָאֵ֗שׁ יָֽרְדָה֙ מֵֽהַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַתֹּ֥אכַל הָעֹלָ֖ה וְהַזְּבָחִ֑ים וּכְב֥וֹד יְהוָ֖ה מָלֵ֥א אֶת הַבָּֽיִת) opens a new scene with fire falling and 'Yahweh's glory' filling the house (v1), echoed in v2's 'the priests could not enter... because Yahweh's glory filled Yahweh's house' (וְלֹ֤א יָֽכְלוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים לָב֖וֹא אֶל בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה) -- a doubled glory-notice bracketing the fire event. Verse 3 shifts to the people's response, וְכֹ֣ל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל ('all the children of Israel looked on'...), 'they bowed themselves... and gave thanks to Yahweh, saying,' closing with the same doxology already sung at 5:13, 'for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever' (וְהוֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב כִּ֥י לְעוֹלָ֖ם חַסְדּֽוֹ). A consonantal sweep of the full two-clause refrain across 2Chr_oshb.txt finds it exactly twice, at 5:13 and here at 7:3, and nowhere else; the shorter, truncated form lacking 'for he is good' surfaces separately at 7:6 and 20:21, neither a third instance of the full pair. This 5:13/7:3 bracket, not any change of subject at v4, is what closes the unit: v4's clause, וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל הָעָ֑ם זֹבְחִ֥ים זֶ֖בַח לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה ('the king and all the people offered sacrifices before Yahweh'), is a waw-plus-fronted-subject participial clause -- background/circumstantial, not the wayyiqtol that actually advances the sacrifice scene (that is v5's וַיִּזְבַּ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֮ אֶת) -- and its cast is not new either: v3's 'all the children of Israel' and v4's 'the king and all the people' name one congregation with the king added, not a fresh participant set. The refrain bracket closing exactly at v3 is the sufficient, independently-verified ground for the edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping 7:1-3 with the sacrifices of 7:4-11 as one 'theophany-and-feast' sweep is the natural rival given v4's continuity of cast and its circumstantial, non-advancing clause type, but it is rejected because the 5:13/7:3 doxology bracket is a tier-1, book-wide-verified refrain that closes the theophany scene on its own terms, independent of whatever kind of clause opens v4.

boundary_rationale: וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְכָל הָעָ֑ם זֹבְחִ֥ים זֶ֖בַח לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (v4 -- 'the king and all the people offered sacrifices before Yahweh,' a circumstantial waw-plus-participle clause, a single-witness SAMEKH following it, oshb:2Chr.7.4) opens the feast proper following the people's doxology in v3, specified into advancing action by v5's wayyiqtol, וַיִּזְבַּ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֮ ('king Solomon offered'). The unit reports Solomon's enormous sacrifice (v5), the priests and Levites at their stations 'with instruments of music... which David the king had made' (v6 -- carrying only the short single-clause echo לְהֹד֤וֹת לַיהוָה֙ כִּֽי לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּ֔וֹ describing the instruments, not a spoken cry, and itself followed by a further single-witness SAMEKH, oshb:2Chr.7.6), the dedication week plus festival week that v9 distinguishes -- שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֔ים for the altar's dedication and a further שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים for the feast itself, closed by the eighth-day assembly (בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֖י עֲצָ֑רֶת, v9), not a single fourteen-day feast (vv8-9), and the dismissal 'on the twenty-third day of the seventh month' (וּבְי֨וֹם עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י שִׁלַּ֥ח אֶת הָעָ֖ם לְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֑ם, v10). It closes on the completion formula 'Solomon finished Yahweh's house and the king's house' (וַיְכַ֧ל שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה אֶת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ...) '...and successfully completed all that came into Solomon's heart' (וְאֵ֨ת כָּל הַבָּ֜א עַל לֵ֣ב שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֧וֹת בְּבֵית יְהוָ֛ה וּבְבֵית֖וֹ הִצְלִֽיחַ, v11); the SAMEKHs after v4 and v6 sit strictly inside this span (potential internal rival seams, both single-witness, weak, neither driving a split here), while a single-witness PE stands after v11 at the span's own closing edge, not inside it in the same sense -- weak edge corroboration for this row's own closing boundary, though the completion language already carries the argument on its own. Verse 12 opens an entirely new scene with a night-theophany formula, 'Yahweh appeared to Solomon by night' (וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בַּלָּ֑יְלָה), changing time, mode, and initiative from human dedication to divine response.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit to include v12 as its capstone would treat the completion formula of v11 as merely transitional rather than as the closing bracket it functions as, since 'finished... and succeeded' answers building language that runs back through the whole complex.

boundary_rationale: וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בַּלָּ֑יְלָה (v12) shares its niphal root and stem with the earlier Gibeon theophany (בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא נִרְאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִשְׁלֹמֹ֑ה, 1:7), though the two differ in every other slot -- subject אֱלֹהִ֖ים there against יְהוָ֛ה here, a qatal there against this verse's wayyiqtol, and the addressee marked by ל- there against אֶל here -- a shared lexeme across the book's two Solomon-theophanies, not a repeated formula. This one opens with direct divine ratification, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֶת תְּפִלָּתֶ֔ךָ וּבָחַ֜רְתִּי בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֛ה ('I have heard your prayer, and have chosen this place'), then answers the very shape of ch.6's own petition series: a national calamity-and-repentance conditional of its own, 'if I shut up the sky... if I command the locust... if I send pestilence' resolved by 'my people... will humble themselves,... then I will hear from heaven, will forgive... and will heal' (vv13-14, הֵ֣ן אֶֽעֱצֹ֤ר הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙...וְיִכָּנְע֨וּ עַמִּ֜י...וַאֲנִי֙ אֶשְׁמַ֣ע...וְאֶסְלַח֙...וְאֶרְפָּ֖א), then a first-person promise fixed on the temple itself, 'now my eyes will be open... for now I have chosen and made this house holy,' (vv15-16, עַתָּ֗ה עֵינַי֙...וְעַתָּ֗ה בָּחַ֤רְתִּי וְהִקְדַּ֨שְׁתִּי֙), before the reciprocal conditional addressed to Solomon by name, 'as for you, if you will walk before me' (2ms throughout: וְאַתָּ֞ה אִם תֵּלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנַ֗י, תֵּלֵ֣ךְ, צִוִּיתִ֑יךָ, תִּשְׁמֽוֹר, v17), closing with the dynastic guarantee, 'I will establish the throne of your kingdom' (וַהֲקִ֣ימוֹתִ֔י אֵ֖ת כִּסֵּ֣א מַלְכוּתֶ֑ךָ...) '...there shall not fail you a man to be ruler in Israel' (לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל, v18) -- answering Solomon's own dynastic plea at 6:16 (וְעַתָּ֞ה...). Vv13-16 hold their own complete protasis-apodosis, referring throughout in the third person to 'my people' while the address itself never leaves Solomon -- fixed at v12 by אֶת תְּפִלָּתֶ֔ךָ (2ms), since no 2nd-person form occurs anywhere in 13-16, and are kept inside this positive panel because they specify the mechanism (hearing, forgiving, healing in response to national repentance) that the reciprocal, second-person promise of vv17-18 then personalizes onto the dynasty; they are not folded forward with v19's own conditional because that verse marks an explicit grammatical turn: 'but if you turn away' (2mp, plural: וְאִם תְּשׁוּב֣וּן אַתֶּ֔ם וַעֲזַבְתֶּם֙, addressee shifting from Solomon's 2ms in v17 to the nation's 2mp), with the apodosis at v20 turning third-plural, 'then I will pluck them up by the roots' (וּנְתַשְׁתִּ֗ים מֵעַ֤ל אַדְמָתִי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙, 'them' 3mp) -- an addressee-broadening shift from the singular royal conditional to a plural national one, not a positive/negative mirror addressed to the same hearer.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The closer rejected alternative splits 13-16 from 17-18: vv13-16 form their own complete protasis-apodosis referring to 'my people' in the third person, which might read as a distinct national oracle; this is rejected because the address itself never shifts away from Solomon across the seam -- no 2nd-person form appears anywhere in 12-16, and the 2ms address resumes explicitly at v17's וְאַתָּ֞ה אִם תֵּלֵ֣ךְ -- so 13-16 and 17-18 remain one continuous speech to the same addressee, the national mechanism (13-16) feeding directly into the personalized dynastic promise (17-18) it grounds. Taking the whole night oracle (12-22) as a single unbroken speech is also reasonable given its one setting and one speaker, but the addressee-broadening turn at v19 -- singular royal conditional giving way to plural national conditional with third-plural consequences -- is a real structural hinge the Chronicler builds into the oracle itself.

boundary_rationale: 'But if you turn away and forsake my statutes' (וְאִם תְּשׁוּב֣וּן אַתֶּ֔ם וַעֲזַבְתֶּם֙ חֻקּוֹתַ֣י..., v19) opens the oracle's warning panel, mirroring v17's positive conditional with its own marked antithesis, and moves through the temple's threatened uprooting and its becoming 'a proverb and a byword among all peoples' (vv20-21) to the closing causal summary, 'therefore he has brought all this evil on them' (עַל כֵּן֙ הֵבִ֣יא עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל הָרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת, v22), where WLC also places a single-witness PE, for whatever thin additional weight that carries at the outer edge of the whole complex. The complex ends here because 8:1 opens a wholly new time-frame formula, 'at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built Yahweh's house and his own house' (וַיְהִ֞י מִקֵּ֣ץ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר...) -- a clean chronological pivot of the kind the Chronicler regularly uses to open a fresh major section, confirming 7:22 as this part's outer edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 7:19-22 as a bridge leaning forward into ch.8's consolidation material would ignore 8:1's own explicit twenty-year time marker, which opens a distinct new unit on its own tier-1 terms.

boundary_rationale: A fresh time-frame formula opens the unit, וַיְהִ֞י מִקֵּ֣ץ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה ("at the end of twenty years"), WEB "At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built Yahweh's house and his own house" -- the same מִקֵּ֣ץ ("end of") device the strategy names as a verified time-frame transition, marking the shift from the dedication complex to civil consolidation; a sweep confirms the specific prefixed form מִקֵּ֣ץ occurs only here in 2Chr (8:1), though the consonantal root קץ itself recurs twice more, at 18:2's לְקֵ֨ץ שָׁנִ֤ים and 21:19's הַקֵּ֜ץ -- so it is the prefixed string that is unique, not the temporal-transition device in general. Solomon builds the cities Huram had given him (v2), then goes to Hamath Zobah and prevails against it, וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ חֲמָ֣ת צוֹבָ֔ה וַיֶּחֱזַ֖ק עָלֶֽיהָ (v3, a movement-and-conquest clause -- the same וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ-plus-destination scene-change device the strategy treats as tier-1 at 10:1's וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֖ם -- not a building notice; what he then builds "in Hamath," אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֖ה בַּחֲמָֽת, is the separate storage-city notice of v4, alongside Tadmor). This list of building projects (Tadmor, the Hamath storage cities, Beth Horon upper and lower, Baalath, further storage/chariot/horse cities) is rounded off by a totalizing close, וְאֵ֣ת כָּל חֵ֣שֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָשַׁק֙ לִבְנ֤וֹת בִּירֽוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וּבַלְּבָנ֔וֹן וּבְכֹ֖ל אֶ֥רֶץ מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ ("all that Solomon desired to build...in all the land of his dominion," v6) that subsumes v3's conquest notice under one wider report on the whole span of Solomon's twenty-year building activity, rather than v3 opening any unit of its own inside it; before v7 opens an unrelated population topic with כָּל הָ֠עָם הַנּוֹתָ֨ר ("all the people who remained").
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the row through v10 to include the labor/officer tally loses because v7's casus-pendens topic opens a distinct population-administration notice rather than continuing the building list's syntax.

boundary_rationale: The unit begins where a casus-pendens topic-fronting, כָּל הָ֠עָם הַנּוֹתָ֨ר ("all the people who remained"), introduces a fresh administrative topic -- the ethnic stratification of forced labor -- distinct from the building catalog just closed; within v7 itself, אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹ֥א מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵֽמָּה is a relative clause whose own predicate closes on the pronoun הֵֽמָּה (gloss: 'who were not of Israel'), not a resumptive element following the fronted topic -- the construction's actual resumption sits in v8's third-plural object suffix on וַיַּעֲלֵ֤ם (gloss: 'Solomon conscripted them'), matching WEB's own punctuation, which closes v7 on a dash and resumes in v8 with 'of them Solomon conscripted forced labor...' WEB v8-9 continues the same register ("of their children who were left...Solomon conscripted forced labor" against "of the children of Israel, Solomon made no servants"), and it closes with the officer tally in v10, אֲשֶׁר לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמָאתָ֑יִם הָרֹדִ֖ים ("who ruled over the people"), a numeric close typical of this device. Note that a PE sits mid-span, after v9 rather than at either edge (oshb:2Chr.8.9, single-witness); a single-witness mark carries no authority to relocate the seam, and since v10's tally simply continues v9's topic, none is claimed here on its account. V11's fronted object, וְאֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה, then opens an unrelated domestic notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v11 into this register as a final administrative item loses because v11's topic -- a marriage-diplomacy household arrangement justified by the ark's holiness -- is not a labor/office matter and opens its own fronted-object clause rather than continuing the register's list syntax.

boundary_rationale: A fronted direct object launches this verse, "וְאֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֶעֱלָ֤ה שְׁלֹמֹה֙" ("and Pharaoh's daughter, Solomon brought up"), a marked word order foregrounding a new referent against the labor register's closing officer tally at v10 ("אֲשֶׁר לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמָאתָ֑יִם הָרֹדִ֖ים בָּעָֽם", "who ruled over the people"). The verse is self-terminating: it runs from the relocation notice to Solomon's own quoted rationale, "כִּי קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֔מָּה אֲשֶׁר בָּֽאָ֥ה אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָֽה" ("for holy are they, to whom the ark of Yahweh has come"), WEB "the places where Yahweh's ark has come are holy" -- and stops there, before v12's own "אָ֣ז"-clause, "אָ֣ז הֶעֱלָ֧ה שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה עֹל֖וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה", opens the cultic-administration unit on a fresh topic and formula. The PE mark following the verse (oshb:2Chr.8.11, single-witness) weakly corroborates a break at exactly this point.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching v11 to the following cultic unit (8:12-16) under a shared "sacred-space propriety" theme loses because v11's rationale clause is complete and self-terminating, and v12 introduces its own new "אָ֣ז"-formula rather than continuing v11's topic or syntax.

boundary_rationale: This span turns on the "אָ֣ז"-clause that opens it, "אָ֣ז הֶעֱלָ֧ה שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה עֹל֖וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה" ("then Solomon offered burnt offerings to Yahweh") -- the first of exactly two "אָ֣ז"-initial clauses counted in this chapter, the other opening v17. It sets the offering calendar (Sabbaths, new moons, three annual feasts), David's priestly/Levitical divisions, the doorkeeper rota, and treasury compliance (WEB v15, "they didn't depart from the commandment of the king...concerning any matter or concerning the treasures"), then closes on a second, distinct completion formula, "וַתִּכֹּן֙ כָּל מְלֶ֣אכֶת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה" ... "שָׁלֵ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה" ("and all Solomon's work was accomplished... Yahweh's house was completed"); the Masoretic paragraphing drops a SAMEKH right after it (oshb:2Chr.8.16, single-witness) -- weak by itself, but landing exactly where the completion formula finishes. This rounds off the construction-plus-cultic complex before the second "אָז֩"-clause at v17, "אָז֩ הָלַ֨ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה לְעֶצְיֽוֹן גֶּ֧בֶר", pivots to a trade notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 8:1-16 as one undivided consolidation row loses because it collapses two structurally distinct devices -- the building catalog's totalizing v6 close and this unit's own "שָׁלֵ֖ם"-completion close at v16 -- into a single span, obscuring the chapter's two-stage shape.

boundary_rationale: The chapter's second "אָז֩"-clause pivots the narrative here, "אָז֩ הָלַ֨ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה לְעֶצְיֽוֹן גֶּ֧בֶר" ("then Solomon went to Ezion Geber"), moving from cultic administration to a maritime venture. The unit is self-contained -- Huram's ships and servants, the Ophir voyage, the cargo count "אַרְבַּע מֵא֥וֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים כִּכַּ֣ר זָהָ֑ב" ("four hundred fifty talents of gold") -- and closes with delivery to the king, "וַיָּבִ֖יאוּ אֶל הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה" ("and they brought them to King Solomon"), a PE follows in the tradition here too (oshb:2Chr.8.18, single-witness) -- unremarkable alone, but consistent with the close argued for. This wealth-delivery close also sets up the pivot into chapter 9, where a foreign visitor arrives with gold and spices in response to Solomon's fame, opening with "וּמַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֗א שָֽׁמְעָה֮ אֶת שֵׁ֣מַע שְׁלֹמֹה֒".
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the row across the chapter seam into 9:1 to keep the wealth-notice thread continuous loses because 9:1's fresh subject opens an entirely new participant and scene, not a continuation of the Ezion Geber report's own syntax.

boundary_rationale: The chapter opens on a fresh subject, "וּמַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֗א שָֽׁמְעָה֮ אֶת שֵׁ֣מַע שְׁלֹמֹה֒ וַתָּב֣וֹא לְנַסּוֹת֩ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה בְחִיד֜וֹת בִּירֽוּשָׁלִַ֗ם בְּחַ֣יִל כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֡ד וּ֠גְמַלִּים נֹשְׂאִ֨ים בְּשָׂמִ֧ים וְזָהָ֛ב לָרֹ֖ב וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם לְבָבָֽהּ" ("When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to test Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great caravan, including camels that bore spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones. When she had come to Solomon, she talked with him about all that was in her heart."), introducing a new character and scene against the trade notice just closed at 8:18. The riddle-testing motif this pair announces is resolved within these two verses, closing with "וַיַּגֶּד לָ֥הּ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת כָּל דְּבָרֶ֑יהָ וְלֹֽא נֶעְלַ֤ם דָּבָר֙ מִשְּׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹ֦א הִגִּ֖יד לָֽהּ" ("Solomon answered all her questions. There wasn’t anything hidden from Solomon which he didn’t tell her."). V3's "וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙" opening is not an independent scene-pivot in its own right, though not because Hebrew narrative requires the queen's name to be restated whenever a prior verse hands the subject slot to Solomon -- it does not: at 9:12, after 'the king Solomon gave' (וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה נָתַ֣ן), the subject reverts to the queen with no name at all, וַֽתַּהֲפֹ֛ךְ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ לְאַרְצָ֖הּ, her name appended only afterward as apposition (הִ֥יא וַעֲבָדֶֽיהָ); re-nomination at v3 is simply the unmarked narrative choice, not an obligation, and no fresh location, audience, or formula accompanies the resumption. The seam this row draws rests instead on content -- the riddle-and-answer exchange that opens and closes inside vv1-2 is a complete unit in itself, distinct from the material-splendor observation that v3 begins, even though the grammar carrying v3, "וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ מַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֔א אֵ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָֽה" ("When the queen of Sheba had seen the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he had built,"), is ordinary continuation rather than a formal boundary marker.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The stronger rival, on inspection, is treating 9:1-9 as one continuous arrival-to-gift unit, since v3's clause is grammatically required resumption rather than an independent tier-1 device; the row is kept separate only on the thinner ground that the riddle-testing exchange and the material-observation-and-speech that follows are two distinct content beats, which is why confidence is lowered here.

boundary_rationale: Perception language launches the unit, "וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ מַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֔א אֵ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה" ("and the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon"), listing what she observed (house, table, servants, ascent to the temple) through v4's "there was no more spirit in her," and her direct speech opens at v5, "וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֱמֶת֙" ("and she said to the king, 'True is the report'"), running through v8. Per the inset rule, this embedded speech is not isolated as its own row because no tier-1 frame closes it on the far side -- v9 continues the narrative directly with her gift, "וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ כַּבֹּ֣שֶׂם הַה֔וּא אֲשֶׁר נָתְנָ֥ה מַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֖א לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה" ("there was never before such spice as the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon"), rather than a resumption formula such as 'when she had finished speaking'; that absence keeps the speech inside its host perception-and-gift unit. The unit's own closing edge, at 9:9/9:10, is argued from v10's fronted compound subject and topic shift, וְגַם עַבְדֵ֤י חירם חוּרָם֙ וְעַבְדֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה ('and also the servants of Huram [ketiv חירם, qere חוּרָם] and the servants of Solomon'), swinging entirely off the queen onto Huram's and Solomon's own trading crews and their Ophir cargo before 9:12 returns the narrative to her; that fronted, compound, וְגַם-marked subject is the fresh scene-opening this row's host unit lacks anywhere before it, and it is what closes this unit at v9 rather than v10.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating vv5-8 as a stand-alone royal-speech row loses under the inset rule because the host unit is bounded on only one side (the 'she said' opening) and never regains an explicit resumption marker -- the gift-giving in v9 simply continues the same narrative thread.

boundary_rationale: An additive particle opens the aside, "וְגַם עַבְדֵ֤י חירם חוּרָם֙ וְעַבְדֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁר הֵבִ֥יאוּ זָהָ֖ב מֵאוֹפִ֑יר הֵבִ֛יאוּ עֲצֵ֥י אַלְגּוּמִּ֖ים וְאֶ֥בֶן יְקָרָֽה" ("The servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum trees and precious stones."), the servants of Huram and Solomon bringing algum wood and precious stones from the same Ophir shipment noted at 8:18 -- a topic unrelated to the queen herself -- continuing into v11's report of what the wood became, "וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת עֲצֵ֨י הָֽאַלְגּוּמִּ֜ים מְסִלּ֤וֹת לְבֵית יְהוָה֙ וּלְבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכִנֹּר֥וֹת וּנְבָלִ֖ים לַשָּׁרִ֑ים וְלֹא נִרְא֥וּ כָהֵ֛ם לְפָנִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה" ("The king used algum tree wood to make terraces for Yahweh’s house and for the king’s house, and harps and stringed instruments for the singers. There were none like these seen before in the land of Judah."), before v12 resumes the Sheba frame directly, "וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה נָתַ֣ן לְמַֽלְכַּת שְׁבָ֗א אֶת כָּל חֶפְצָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔לָה מִלְּבַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר הֵבִ֣יאָה אֶל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ" ("King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked, more than that which she had brought to the king"), and closes the whole episode with her departure, "וַֽתַּהֲפֹ֛ךְ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ לְאַרְצָ֖הּ הִ֥יא וַעֲבָדֶֽיהָ" ("she turned and went to her own land, she and her servants"), an inclusio with the arrival at 9:1; the close aligns with the PE mark at v.12 (oshb:2Chr.9.12, single-witness). V11's own closing clause, already quoted above, is a negated-uniqueness figure that belongs on the record at this seam too: it shares a construction with the clause closing v9, "וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ כַּבֹּ֣שֶׂם הַה֔וּא" (the previous row's own close), and with two more later in the chapter (v19b, v20b) -- a chapter-wide figure, though not exclusive to it, since comparable negated-uniqueness clauses stand at 1:12 and 35:18. That figure straddles rather than marks the 9:9/9:10 seam, since its two nearest members fall on opposite sides of a division neither one drives; the topical warrant for that seam -- the gift-giving closing at v9 against the unrelated Ophir-cargo aside opening v10 -- stands on its own regardless. This is a genuinely marginal call: the algum aside could instead be read as a coda to vv3-9's gift exchange rather than its own unit, and no mark or fresh formula settles it beyond the topic shift itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv10-12 into the preceding row (9:3-9) as one continuous gift-and-craft sequence loses because v10's algum-wood aside is not about the queen's gift at all, but a separate Ophir-cargo note that only rejoins her narrative at v12.

boundary_rationale: A fresh register begins here, "וַיְהִי֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥א לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּשָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים וָשֵׁ֖שׁ כִּכְּרֵ֥י זָהָֽב" ("Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,") -- an itemized list of annual gold income (v13), the traders'-and-kings' supplement introduced by the particle "לְבַ֞ד" (v14), and then two further items, the golden shields (v15) and the ivory throne (v17), each opening with its own fresh wayyiqtol plus explicit royal subject, "וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה" and "וַיַּ֧עַשׂ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ" respectively. That construction is not itself a unit-opening signal here: the identical shape already introduced the algum-craft aside at 9:11 ("וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ") and recurs at 12:10 in Rehoboam's own reign ("וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ רְחַבְעָם֙"), showing it functions as a repeatable catalog item-opener within this book's inventory register rather than a device that starts a new row each time it appears; vv18-21 continue with bare wə-noun and particle continuations that carry the throne-and-vessel material forward without a comparable opener. A PE does fall mid-span, immediately before v17's fresh opener (oshb:2Chr.9.16, single-witness); mark and clause-shape converge there, but on an item-boundary internal to one catalog, not a row-boundary, since the surrounding material never breaks its inventory register. The row closes on the Tarshish fleet's concrete cargo, "אַחַת֩ לְשָׁל֨וֹשׁ שָׁנִ֜ים תָּב֣וֹאנָה אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ נֹֽשְׂאוֹת֙ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֔סֶף שֶׁנְהַבִּ֥ים וְקוֹפִ֖ים וְתוּכִּיִּֽים" ("Once every three years, the ships of Tarshish came bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks."); here the tradition's own paragraph mark, a PE (oshb:2Chr.9.21, single-witness), lands right at the row's edge instead, for whatever weak, single-witness weight that is worth. Kept coarse as one row for its specific-inventory character, distinct from the generalizing rhetoric that follows at v22.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the shields (15-16) or the throne (17-19) into their own rows tests the item-opener construction at its strongest, since both verses do open with a fresh subject-bearing wayyiqtol, but the same construction recurring at 9:11 and 12:10 as a plain catalog item-marker, never elsewhere treated in this campaign as a row-opener, is why the split is not adopted.
