boundary_rationale: Generalizing rhetoric takes over from the itemized inventory here: "וַיִּגְדַּל֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ לְעֹ֖שֶׁר וְחָכְמָֽה" ("and King Solomon became great above all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom"), a claim that broadens to "all the kings of the earth" seeking his presence and bringing tribute, and closes on the recurring-tribute formula "דְּבַר שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשָׁנָֽה" ("a matter of year in year"); a PE closes the tradition's own paragraph at the identical verse (oshb:2Chr.9.24, single-witness), single-witness weight only, but not a hindrance to the reading proposed. This summary is distinguished from the specific numeric inventory just closed (13-21) by its shift from concrete quantities to universalizing claims, and from the following unit (25-28) by its own closing annual-recurrence formula rather than a fresh "וַיְהִ֨י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֜ה"-opened numeric list.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 22-28 into a single summary row loses the seam v25's fresh "וַיְהִ֨י" clause marks: it reopens with concrete stall and horsemen counts that verbally echo 1:14-17's own inventory, a distinct rhetorical register from 22-24's generalized tribute claim.

boundary_rationale: Three of this span's four verses verbally echo 1:14-17 closely enough to argue a textual inclusio; the fourth, v26, is a distinct dominion notice absorbed into the same recapitulation on topical rather than lexical grounds. It opens with "וַיְהִ֨י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אַרְבַּעַת֩ אֲלָפִ֨ים אֻֽרְי֤וֹת סוּסִים֙ וּמַרְכָּב֔וֹת וּשְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּנִּיחֵם֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְעִם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם" ("Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen that he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem."), closing with "וַיַּנִּיחֵם֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְעִם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם" -- identical but for a single pointing mark to 1:14's own closing clause, "וַיַּנִּיחֵם֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְעִם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּירֽוּשָׁלִָֽם". V26 then intervenes with a territorial notice unparalleled in 1:14-17's wealth catalog, "וַיְהִ֥י מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל הַמְּלָכִ֑ים מִן הַנָּהָר֙ וְעַד אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַ֖ד גְּב֥וּל מִצְרָֽיִם" ("He ruled over all the kings from the River even to the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt."); it shares no exact token with 1:16-17's horse-trade notices -- 9:26's מִצְרָֽיִם is a bare, unprefixed form against 1:16's and 1:17's prefixed מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם and מִמִּצְרַ֤יִם -- and its only lemma-level contacts are the toponym Egypt and a common king-plus-quantifier collocation (9:26's בְּכָל הַמְּלָכִ֑ים against 1:17's לְכָל מַלְכֵ֧י... וּמַלְכֵ֥י...), neither a topical parallel, since 9:26 marks a dominion border while 1:16-17 name a trade source. V27's silver-and-cedar hyperbole, "וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אֶת הַכֶּ֛סֶף בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם כָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת הָאֲרָזִ֗ים נָתַ֛ן כַּשִּׁקְמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה לָרֹֽב" ("The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedars to be as abundant as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland."), is consonantally and vocalically identical to 1:15's parallel, "וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת הַכֶּ֧סֶף וְאֶת הַזָּהָ֛ב בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם כָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת הָאֲרָזִ֗ים נָתַ֛ן כַּשִּׁקְמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה לָרֹֽב" ("The king made silver and gold to be as common as stones in Jerusalem, and he made cedars to be as common as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland."), but for 1:15's inserted "וְאֶת הַזָּהָ֛ב" ("and the gold"); the two verses' accentuation differs as well, on the word for 'the king' (הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ against הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ) and on the word for 'the silver' (הַכֶּ֛סֶף against הַכֶּ֧סֶף), a mechanical redistribution of cantillation around that one inserted phrase rather than a further wording difference. V28's horses-from-Egypt notice, "וּמוֹצִיאִ֨ים סוּסִ֧ים מִמִּצְרַ֛יִם לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה וּמִכָּל הָאֲרָצֽוֹת" ("They brought horses for Solomon out of Egypt and out of all lands."), is looser in wording than 1:16's parallel, "וּמוֹצָ֧א הַסּוּסִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וּמִקְוֵ֕א סֹחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מִקְוֵ֥א יִקְח֖וּ בִּמְחִֽיר", but shares the same topic, closing the recapitulation before v29's source-citation formula opens the reign's close. This span is the arguable in-book inclusio partner of 1:14-17 the strategy names on three of its four verses; the parallel is intra-Chronicles and textual, never drawn from the Kings Vorlage.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating all four verses as equally weighted inclusio echoes overstates v26's fit; the sharper reading keeps the row's edges as drawn but grounds the near-verbatim claim in vv25, 27 and 28 alone, with v26 carried along as the recapitulation's territorial capstone rather than a fourth echo. A genuine rival span, not just an internal weighting, would run 9:24-28 as one undivided recapitulation, since v24's own gift-tribute notice, דְּבַר שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשָׁנָֽה ('a rate year by year'), sits inside the same wealth register that 25-28 continues; this is declined because v24 closes out the preceding kings-seeking-Solomon unit begun at v23 (מְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת פְּנֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה, 'sought the presence of Solomon') rather than opening the 1:14-17 recapitulation itself, which begins its own fresh, inclusio-marked material only at v25's horse-and-chariot notice.

boundary_rationale: The reign's close is anchored by two named devices: the source-citation formula, "וּשְׁאָר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאֲחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים" ("and the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, aren't they written"), naming Nathan, Ahijah, and Iddo, followed by the forty-year reign length, and then the death-and-succession formula, "וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב שְׁלֹמֹה֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֔הוּ בְּעִ֖יר דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑יו" ... "וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ רְחַבְעָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו" ("and Solomon slept with his fathers...and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place"); the Masoretic tradition's last word on the matter is a PE at this very verse (oshb:2Chr.9.31, single-witness), a fittingly final if evidentially modest flourish. This closes the entire Solomon complex (1:1-9:31) before 10:1's fresh scene-opener, "וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֖ם שְׁכֶ֑מָה" ("Rehoboam went to Shechem"), begins the division narrative outside this part's range.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v29's source citation into the preceding wealth recapitulation (25-28) loses because the source-formula's own list-closing syntax is a distinct register-closing device this book uses specifically to terminate reigns, not to extend an inventory.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the travel notice "וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֖ם שְׁכֶ֑מָה" (“Rehoboam went to Shechem”), a scene-and-participant marker of the same class as the return notice at 19:1, and WEB's own frame (“Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king”, v.1) confirms a fresh occasion rather than a continuation of ch. 9's Solomon material. The crowd's grievance is voiced in direct speech at v.4 (“Your father made our yoke grievous…”), and the unit closes at v.5 with the king's stalling reply and "וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ הָעָֽם" (WEB “So the people departed”), a clean scene-exit separating the public demand from the private counsel-seeking that follows in v.6. SAMEKH marks v.5 (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only), sitting exactly at this seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv.1-9 into one 'assembly' unit is possible since the old-men consultation in v.6 answers the same grievance, but the new verb of royal consultation at v.6 marks a sharper participant-and-setting change than any seam inside vv.1-5.

boundary_rationale: The seam opens at v.6 with "וַיִּוָּעַ֞ץ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת הַזְּקֵנִים֙" (“King Rehoboam took counsel with the old men”), a new consultation verb absent from the crowd-scene just closed; the unit is built as a paired contrast (old men counseled first, vv.6-7, WEB 'please them, and speak good words'; young men next, vv.8-9, same consultation root), and closes on the young men's quoted ultimatum ending "אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֖י בָּֽעֲקְרַבִּֽים" (WEB “My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions”) -- a line the narrative repeats almost verbatim at v.14 once the answer is actually delivered, showing the deliberation's content is fixed here, before the day-three meeting resumes. SAMEKH marks v.11 (single-witness), matching this closural sense.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival segmentation would run vv.6-15 together as one counsel-and-answer unit, but the resumptive date clause "וַיָּבֹ֨א יָרָבְעָ֧ם וְכָל הָעָ֛ם אֶל רְחַבְעָ֖ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֑י" at v.12 (echoing v.5's three-day wait) functions as resumptive repetition (Wiederaufnahme) bracketing a same-timeline digression, not a flashback to an earlier moment -- the deliberation vv.6-11 fill narrates events occurring within the very three-day interval v.5 opens, so the split is favored on that ground instead.

boundary_rationale: Opens at v.12 with "וַיָּבֹ֨א יָרָבְעָ֧ם וְכָל הָעָ֛ם אֶל רְחַבְעָ֖ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֑י" (WEB “So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day”), which resumes the plot from the stall in v.5 rather than continuing the deliberation digression just closed; the unit narrates the harsh answer (vv.13-14, echoing the young men's scorpions line) and closes with the narrator's verdict: "וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי הָיְתָ֤ה נְסִבָּה֙" joined to "אֶת דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֤ר דִּבֶּר֙ בְּיַד֙" [→ Ahijah] (WEB “So the king didn't listen to the people; for it was brought about by God, that Yahweh might establish his word, which he spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite”, v.15) -- an explanatory aside rather than advancing action, distinct in register from the crowd's own perception-reaction that opens v.16.
strongest_rejected_alternative: V.16 and v.17 both front a bare subject noun phrase before their finite verb ("וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּ֠י..." and the parallel construction opening v.17), matching 11:13's disjunctive casus-pendens shape more precisely than v.15 does; v.15 itself is a verb-first negated clause, "וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֥ע..." (waw-lo-qatal, verb before subject), a distinct type from v.16-17's subject-fronted pattern, so calling all three 'the same criterion' as 047's driver overstates the identity. The row still closes at v.15 rather than v.14 because v.15's own verdict clause, וְלֹֽא שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל הָעָ֑ם ('the king didn't listen to the people'), is itself the narrator's direct characterization of the harsh answer and elders-forsaking just narrated in vv13-14 (וַיַּעֲנֵ֥ם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ קָשָׁ֑ה, 'the king answered them harshly'), not an independent notice; v.15's own causal clause, כִּֽי הָיְתָ֤ה נְסִבָּה֙...לְמַעַן֩ הָקִ֨ים יְהוָ֜ה אֶת דְּבָר֗וֹ..., depends grammatically on that same just-given answer for its referent, tying v.15 backward to vv.13-14 on its own terms; the echo of שָׁמַ֥ע at v.16 lies across the row's own boundary and is neutral on where that boundary falls, not a warrant for placing it here.

boundary_rationale: Opens with a fronted-subject casus pendens, "וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּ֠י לֹא שָׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּלֶךְ֮" (WEB "When all Israel saw that the king didn't listen to them" -- the WEB rendering supplies 'saw' where the Hebrew has no perception verb at the verse head; the sole ר-א-ה root in the whole verse is the later imperative "רְאֵ֥ה" addressed to David's house), resumed by the wayyiqtol "וַיָּשִׁ֣יבוּ הָעָ֣ם" before their direct-speech repudiation ("What portion do we have in David?...", v.16) and its violent sequel (Hadoram stoned and the king's flight, v.18); it closes on the standing-condition refrain "וַיִּפְשְׁע֤וּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּבֵ֣ית דָּוִ֔יד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה" ("So Israel rebelled against David’s house to this day."), an etiological 'to this day' formula marking a permanent state rather than a further event. Three SAMEKH marks stand at 10:16, 10:18 and 10:19 (all single-witness); the tightest run of consecutively MARKED verses in the part is actually 10:18-10:19-11:1 (SAMEKH-SAMEKH-PE, no gap), so the seam corroboration these tier-3 witnesses lend belongs to the 10:19 mark sitting at this row's own closing edge, not to a 'densest run' claim restricted to this span alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: V.17's own opening, "וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיֹּֽשְׁבִ֖ים" (WEB "But as for the children of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah"), is a genuinely disjunctive subject-fronted clause, formally the same casus-pendens shape this cluster credits as a tier-1 divider at 11:13 ("וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם..."); but disjunction alone does not divide absent an accompanying participant or topic change, and v.17 introduces neither -- it names the same split kingdom's other half, the topic v.16 has just been narrating -- so it stays inside this row as a parenthetical notice.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the new-location notice "וַיָּבֹ֣א רְחַבְעָם֮ יְרוּשָׁלִַם֒ וַיַּקְהֵל֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית יְהוּדָ֜ה וּבִנְיָמִ֗ן מֵאָ֨ה וּשְׁמוֹנִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף בָּח֖וּר עֹשֵׂ֣ה מִלְחָמָ֑ה לְהִלָּחֵם֙ עִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה לִרְחַבְעָֽם" ("When Rehoboam had come to Jerusalem, he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand chosen men who were warriors, to fight against Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam."), a mobilization scene marking a change of scene, participants, and register from the schism refrain just closed at 10:19 -- new location (Jerusalem), a fresh governing verb (וַיַּקְהֵל֩, 'he assembled'), and a narrated event succeeding an etiological standing-condition refrain, not an absence of shared subject-matter: 10:19's וַיִּפְשְׁע֤וּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּבֵ֣ית דָּוִ֔יד ('Israel rebelled against the house of David') and 11:1's לְהִלָּחֵם֙ עִם יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה לִרְחַבְעָֽם ('to fight against Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam') share the name Israel, and v.1 is a direct attempt to reverse the very rupture v.10:19 declares permanent; the SAMEKH keyed to 10:19 (single-witness) sits exactly at this opening seam, while the PE keyed to 11:1 (single-witness) falls after it, internal to this row's own span rather than at its edge. The whole unit -- mobilization, Shemaiah's veto oracle (vv.2-4a), and the stand-down -- is kept together per the inset rule, since the oracle receives no resumption frame apart from the compliance clause fused into v.4 itself: "כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה לֹא תַעֲלוּ֩ וְלֹא תִלָּ֨חֲמ֜וּ עִם אֲחֵיכֶ֗ם שׁ֚וּבוּ אִ֣ישׁ לְבֵית֔וֹ כִּ֧י מֵֽאִתִּ֛י נִהְיָ֖ה הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַֽיִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ מִלֶּ֥כֶת אֶל יָרָבְעָֽם" ("‘Yahweh says, “You shall not go up, nor fight against your brothers! Every man return to his house; for this thing is of me.”’” So they listened to Yahweh’s words, and returned from going against Jeroboam."); the PE keyed to v.4 (single-witness) does fall at this row's own closing edge (11:4/11:5), matching the book strategy's own reading of this passage as the closing beat of the whole division account (10:1-11:4).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two rivals were weighed: isolating Shemaiah's oracle (vv.2-4a) alone fails the inset rule since no tier-1 frame resumes the host narrative apart from the compliance clause fused into v.4; splitting instead at v.1/v.2, where v.2's own "וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל שְׁמַֽעְיָ֥הוּ אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר" opens this book's own listed oracle-frame device, is the sharper rival, but v.1's mobilization reports no outcome of its own -- it is raised only to be stood down by the oracle's veto in v.4 -- so severing them would leave a raised army with no narrated resolution until a row later.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the settlement-and-building notice "וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב רְחַבְעָ֖ם בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיִּ֧בֶן עָרִ֛ים לְמָצ֖וֹר בִּיהוּדָֽה" (WEB “Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and built cities for defense in Judah”), a peacetime topic wholly distinct from the war-mobilization-then-standdown scene just closed; the fifteen-name toponym list (vv.6-10) and garrison notice (vv.11-12) form a register-like catalog the strategy directs writers to keep coarse. It closes with the summary formula "וַיְהִי ל֖וֹ יְהוּדָ֥ה וּבִנְיָמִֽן" (WEB “Judah and Benjamin belonged to him”), a possession-summary wrapping the fortification catalog before the subject changes to religious personnel in v.13.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The toponym list (vv.6-10) could be split from the garrison-and-summary notice (vv.11-12), but both share one catalog register and one closing function (consolidating Judah and Benjamin under Rehoboam), so splitting would fragment a single coarse-grained list against the granularity guidance for catalogs.

boundary_rationale: The disjunctive, subject-first clause "וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִֽתְיַצְּב֥וּ" (WEB “The priests and the Levites who were in all Israel stood with him”), breaking the wayyiqtol chain of the fortification catalog, marks a genuine topic and participant change -- clergy and northern God-seekers replacing city-names and garrisons. V.16 opens with the same waw-X-qatal shape as v.13, "וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל..." (WEB "After them, out of all the tribes of Israel..."), its athnach even falling on the same word, "יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל", as v.13's own -- but its anaphoric "וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם" ('after them') explicitly continues v.13-15's migration topic rather than opening a new one, subordinating the lay God-seekers' arrival to the same clergy-exodus thread as a second wave rather than a fresh unit. The unit explains why the Levites left Jeroboam's realm (v.14), his counterfeit priesthood (v.15), and the northern loyalists' pilgrimage (v.16), then closes on the doubled temporal bracket "כִּ֣י הָֽלְכ֗וּ בְּדֶ֧רֶךְ דָּוִ֛יד וּשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְשָׁנִ֥ים שָׁלֽוֹשׁ" (WEB “…for three years, for they walked three years in the way of David and Solomon”), sealing this consolidation report before the narrative turns to Rehoboam's domestic life in v.18.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The sharper rival is splitting at 11:15/11:16, since v.16 reproduces v.13's own waw-X-qatal disjunctive shape down to the athnach falling on the same word; it is not adopted because the anaphoric 'after them' ties the lay migration explicitly to the clergy migration just narrated, one continuing topic rather than two.

boundary_rationale: Opens on a register shift rather than a new construction: v.17's plain wayyiqtol summary formula closing the consolidation report gives way at v.18 to the domestic material of a family register, though the wayyiqtol shape itself, "וַיִּֽקַּֽח ל֤וֹ רְחַבְעָם֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה" (WEB "Rehoboam took a wife for himself"), is not formally distinct -- it is the same plain consecutive verb opening vv.15, 17, 19, 21, 22 and 23 in this stretch, and a book-wide sweep finds no other instance of this exact verb-plus-noun pairing anywhere else in 2Chr, so 'formula' overstates a single occurrence rather than a recurring pattern; the genuinely disjunctive clause-openings in this neighborhood are the waw-X-qatal shapes at 11:13 and 11:16 -- 11:13 fronting its subject, וְהַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם, 11:16 fronting the adverbial וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם -- of which only 11:13 is taken as a boundary here, 11:16's disjunction subordinating to it rather than opening a fresh unit of its own; and not this one. The unit lists two wives and their children (vv.18-21), names Abijah's designation as heir (v.22), and closes with the dispersal-and-provision notice "וַיָּבֶן֩ וַיִּפְרֹ֨ץ מִכָּל בָּנָ֜יו לְֽכָל אַרְצ֧וֹת יְהוּדָ֣ה וּבִנְיָמִ֗ן לְכֹל֙ עָרֵ֣י הַמְּצֻר֔וֹת וַיִּתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֛ם הַמָּז֖וֹן לָרֹ֑ב וַיִּשְׁאַ֖ל הֲמ֥וֹן נָשִֽׁים" ("He dealt wisely, and dispersed some of his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to every fortified city. He gave them food in abundance; and he sought many wives for them."), wrapping the domestic register before 12:1's time-frame clause turns to the reign's theological summary.
strongest_rejected_alternative: This register could be folded forward into the Shishak account as mere background, but 12:1 opens its own decisive time-frame formula unrelated in form and topic to the wife-and-sons list, so the family register is better bounded on its own -- matching the strategy's flag on exactly this attachment question.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the circumstantial time-frame clause "וַיְהִ֗י כְּהָכִ֞ין מַלְכ֤וּת רְחַבְעָם֙ וּכְחֶזְקָת֔וֹ עָזַ֖ב אֶת תּוֹרַ֣ת" (WEB “When the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and he was strong, he abandoned Yahweh's law”), the same time-frame-transition device the strategy identifies elsewhere (8:1's וַיְהִ֞י מִקֵּ֣ץ and 31:1's וּכְכַלּ֣וֹת כָּל זֹ֗את) as a boundary-driver -- a functional category spanning both wayehi and non-wayehi openers, of which only 8:1 shares this row's own וַיְהִי-plus-temporal-clause shape (31:1 opens waw-plus-kaf-plus-infinitive-construct, with no וַיְהִי anywhere in its clause), here pivoting from the family register to national apostasy; v.2 itself opens with the sole wayehi-plus-dated-year specimen among 2Chr's 38 verse-initial wayehi clauses, "וַיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַֽחֲמִישִׁית֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֔ם" (WEB "In the fifth year of King Rehoboam"), a single-witness PE also falls at v.1 itself (oshb:2Chr.12.1, pe, single-witness), internal to this row's own span at the contested 12:1|12:2 juncture, outweighed here by the same tier-1 causal subordination described next: yet its own closing clause, "כִּ֥י מָעֲל֖וּ בַּיהוָֽה" (WEB "because they had trespassed against Yahweh"), ties Shishak's dated advance back to v.1's apostasy by explicit causation, subordinating the invasion notice's own tier-1 opener to the reign-wide frame v.1 has already set rather than opening a competing unit; the unit narrates Shishak's advance and army roster (vv.2-4a) and closes with "וַיָּבֹ֖א עַד יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם" (WEB “and came to Jerusalem”), SAMEKH marked (single-witness) at v.4, the advance's terminus before the prophet enters.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The more serious rival is splitting at 12:1/12:2, since v.2 carries the book's only dated wayehi opening; it is not adopted because v.2's own closing causal clause binds the invasion to v.1's apostasy as one cause-and-consequence unit rather than two independent notices.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the disjunctive participant-introduction "וּֽשְׁמַֽעְיָ֤ה הַנָּבִיא֙ בָּ֣א אֶל רְחַבְעָ֔ם" (WEB “Now Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam”), the prophet-notice frame the strategy lists among 2Chr's boundary-driving speech devices; the exchange runs from the judgment word (v.5) through the princes' confession 'Yahweh is righteous' (v.6) to Yahweh's reversal announced to Shemaiah (v.7), closing on the purpose clause "כִּ֥י יִהְיוּ ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִ֑ים וְיֵדְעוּ֙ עֲב֣וֹדָתִ֔י וַעֲבוֹדַ֖ת מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאֲרָצֽוֹת" (WEB “…that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries”), SAMEKH marked (single-witness) at v.8. It resumes at v.9 with "וַיַּ֨עַל שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם֮ עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַם֒", an almost word-for-word repeat of the closing portion of v.2's own clause, עָלָ֛ה שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (וַיְהִ֞י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַֽחֲמִישִׁית֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֔ם has no counterpart in v.9's shorter clause) -- the two also differ in verb form, v.2's qatal עָלָ֛ה after its own fronted temporal clause against v.9's verse-initial wayyiqtol וַיַּ֨עַל, which strengthens rather than weakens the far-side frame this row depends on -- a resumptive-repetition (Wiederaufnahme) that reopens the wider invasion narrative rather than bracketing this row specifically, since the repeated clause pair's true span is 12:3-8, not 12:5-8, with v.3's chariot roster, "בְּאֶ֤לֶף וּמָאתַ֨יִם֙ רֶ֔כֶב וּבְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֗ר לָעָ֞ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֤אוּ עִמּוֹ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לוּבִ֥ים סֻכִּיִּ֖ים וְכוּשִֽׁים" ("with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen. The people were without number who came with him out of Egypt: the Lubim, the Sukkiim, and the Ethiopians."), and v.4's capture notice intervening between the two members; the row's own near frame is supplied directly by v.5's disjunctive prophet-notice opening, already quoted above, which needs no help from v.2's echo to satisfy the inset rule.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the oracle fused inside one long 12:1-12 host unit (the inset rule's default absent a clear frame) is the strongest rival, but v.5's own disjunctive prophet-notice opening already supplies the near-side tier-1 frame the inset rule requires, and v.9's return to Shishak's advance closes it on the far side, so the split is preferred without needing the v.2/v.9 echo to do that work.

boundary_rationale: Resumes the invasion plot with "וַיַּ֨עַל שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַיִם֮ עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַם֒" (WEB “So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem”), the Wiederaufnahme echo of v.2's "עָלָ֛ה שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם" that reopens the plunder narrative after the oracle exchange; the unit reports the treasury seizure (v.9), Rehoboam's bronze-shield replacement and its recurring guard ritual (vv.10-11), and closes with the theological summary "וּבְהִכָּֽנְע֗וֹ שָׁ֤ב מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ אַף יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א לְהַשְׁחִ֖ית לְכָלָ֑ה" (WEB “When he humbled himself, Yahweh's wrath turned from him, so as not to destroy him altogether”), SAMEKH marked (single-witness) at v.12, before the regnal closing formula begins in v.13.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The root כנע ('humble') does thread through this complex -- "וַיִּכָּנְע֥וּ שָׂרֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְהַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ צַדִּ֥יק יְהוָֽה" (12:6, WEB "Then the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, “Yahweh is righteous.”") and its own twice-repeated echo in v.7 ("וּבִרְא֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ כִּ֣י נִכְנָ֔עוּ הָיָה֩ דְבַר יְהוָ֨ה אֶל שְׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה לֵאמֹ֛ר נִכְנְע֖וּ לֹ֣א אַשְׁחִיתֵ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֨י לָהֶ֤ם כִּמְעַט֙ לִפְלֵיטָ֔ה וְלֹא תִתַּ֧ךְ חֲמָתִ֛י בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּיַד שִׁישָֽׁק") -- before v.12's own "וּבְהִכָּֽנְע֗וֹ" -- but that thread crosses the 12:8/12:9 row seam into the oracle exchange itself, so it argues for a single larger 12:5-12 unit at least as readily as it isolates v.12 from vv.9-11; it is not, on inspection, a warrant for this particular split. The genuine counter-signal sits in v.12's own grammar: its fronted bet-plus-infinitive-construct opening stands outside the wayyiqtol chain (וַיַּ֨עַל ... וַיִּקַּ֞ח...וַיַּ֨עַשׂ) that carries vv.9-10 -- v.11 itself opens with a different, frequentative form, וַיְהִ֛י מִדֵּי ב֥וֹא ('and it happened, as often as [the king] came'), not a fourth link in that chain, which argues, if anything, toward treating v.12 as its own beat rather than binding it to the shield notice. The row is kept as bounded because the theological summary still functions as this reign-episode's single verdict-close, matching the SAMEKH at its edge, but that closural function is the real basis, not a humbling-root echo that in fact reaches past this row's own left edge.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the reign-resumption formula "וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֞ק הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֛ם בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיִּמְלֹ֑ךְ כִּ֣י בֶן אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וְאַחַ֣ת שָׁנָה֩ רְחַבְעָ֨ם בְּמָלְכ֜וֹ" (WEB “So King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned; for Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign”), the age-formula device the strategy lists among 2Chr's regnal specimens, here repurposed as a retrospective reign-summary rather than an initial accession (Rehoboam's succession was already noted at 9:31); the theological-summary register of the preceding invasion account (v.12) gives way to formulaic biography -- reign length, mother's name, moral evaluation (v.14, SAMEKH marked, single-witness), source citation to Shemaiah and Iddo (v.15) -- and closes with the death-burial-succession formula "וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב רְחַבְעָם֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲבִיָּ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ" (WEB “Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in David's city; and Abijah his son reigned in his place”), PE marked (single-witness) at v.16, the seam-out point into the next reign's synchronism-accession opening.
strongest_rejected_alternative: This cluster might be split into a reign-summary row (vv.13-14) and a source-citation-plus-death row (vv.15-16), since each has its own formula type, but all four verses form one continuous closing-formula sequence with no intervening narrative action, so one row respects the register-light, formula-driven character the strategy assigns to regnal closes.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the Chronicler's synchronism-dated accession type, בִּשְׁנַ֛ת שְׁמוֹנֶ֥ה עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ יָרָבְעָ֑ם וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ אֲבִיָּ֖ה (WEB: "In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah"), a dated formula distinct from the age-formula and succession types the book uses elsewhere. Verse 2 completes the standard reign-length/mother's-name notice and adds a war notice; v3 shifts into troop-muster register, וַיֶּאְסֹ֨ר אֲבִיָּ֜ה אֶת הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה בְּחַ֨יִל֙ גִּבּוֹרֵ֣י מִלְחָמָ֔ה אַרְבַּע מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף אִ֣ישׁ בָּח֑וּר ("Abijah joined battle...four hundred thousand chosen men"), still list-style content rather than scene narration. The row closes before v4's rise-and-speak formula, וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שְׁמָע֖וּנִי יָרָבְעָ֥ם וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל ("and said, 'Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel'"), which opens direct address in a different register entirely. A double SAMEKH follows v3 in the WLC (single-witness), weak corroboration for a break exactly where the muster ends and the oration begins, though the register shift itself is the real driver.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating only 13:1-2 as the row and folding v3's muster forward into the speech complex loses the point that v3 is still list-register content, not oration, and needlessly narrows the accession unit to bare regnal data.

boundary_rationale: Abijah's oration is framed on its near side by the rise-and-speak formula of v4, וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שְׁמָע֖וּנִי יָרָבְעָ֥ם וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל ("and said, 'Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel'"), a vocative opening that v1-3's muster report does not share; a SAMEKH+SAMEKH double mark (single-witness) closes v.3 immediately before it, additional left-edge corroboration for this row's own near boundary. The speech argues Davidic legitimacy against the revolt and priestly fidelity against the golden-calf cult, turning at v10 on the contrastive וַאֲנַ֛חְנוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ (WEB: "But as for us, Yahweh is our God"). It closes before v13 resumes third-person battle report, וְיָֽרָבְעָ֗ם הֵסֵב֙ אֶת הַמַּאְרָ֔ב לָב֖וֹא מֵֽאַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם ("Jeroboam caused an ambush to come about behind them") -- a disjunctive waw-plus-fronted-subject clause, fronting יָרָבְעָם before the finite verb הֵסֵב, marking a genuine scene-shift back to Jeroboam's own maneuver rather than an ordinary return to narration after quoted speech. Isolating a speech this way is only warranted under the inset rule where a tier-1 frame brackets both sides; the rise-and-speak opening at v.4 and this disjunctive resumption at v.13 both supply that frame, so the row stands, though the call is close enough to hold it below high.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the oration inside a single 13:1-20 war-narrative row, the inset rule's default preference, is defensible and loses only the ability to name the speech's own covenant-argument shape as a row. Internal SAMEKH marks also fall at v.5 and v.9 (both single-witness), the latter exactly at the v.9/v.10 turn this row's own rationale names as the oration's rhetorical pivot (וַאֲנַ֛חְנוּ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ); neither is read as licensing a split, since the oration's own rhetorical continuity -- one continuous address, Abijah speaking to Jeroboam and Israel throughout with no change of interlocutor, Davidic legitimacy argued straight through into priestly fidelity -- outweighs tier-3, single-witness marks that a formal covenant-argument speech need not otherwise obey.

boundary_rationale: Narrative resumes with Jeroboam's own maneuver, וְיָֽרָבְעָ֗ם הֵסֵב֙ אֶת הַמַּאְרָ֔ב לָב֖וֹא מֵֽאַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם ("Jeroboam caused an ambush to come about behind them"), pulling the scene from Abijah's speech to third-person report: the trumpet-cry (v14), the shout and divine strike (v15), the rout, and finally Jeroboam's ruin, וְלֹֽא עָצַ֧ר כֹּֽחַ יָרָבְעָ֛ם ע֖וֹד בִּימֵ֣י אֲבִיָּ֑הוּ וַיִּגְּפֵ֥הוּ יְהוָ֖ה וַיָּמֹֽת ("Jeroboam didn't recover strength again in the days of Abijah. Yahweh struck him, and he died"). That death notice disposes of the rival king entirely before the text turns, in v21, to an unrelated topic, וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֣ק אֲבִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּ֨שָּׂא ל֔וֹ ("Abijah grew mighty and took for himself..."), his own household. A PE mark (single-witness) follows v20, weakly corroborating the break at that exact point.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the pursuit (v19-20) from the battle proper (v13-18) manufactures a seam where the text gives no change of formula or subject, only continued action against the same defeated army.

boundary_rationale: וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֣ק אֲבִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּ֨שָּׂא ל֔וֹ נָשִׁ֖ים אַרְבַּ֣ע עֶשְׂרֵ֑ה ("Abijah grew mighty and took for himself fourteen wives") opens a household tally wholly apart from the war report just closed, counting wives, sons, and daughters; a PE (single-witness) closes v.20 immediately before it, left-edge corroboration for this row's own opening, while a SAMEKH (single-witness) closes v.21 itself, an internal counter-signal that would split the household tally from the source-citation formula that follows -- not adopted here, since both halves are the same kind of terse dynastic-tally material this book's reign-closing block conventionally bundles, and the mark is tier-3, single-witness, non-driving. The chapter then turns to this book's recurring reign-closing source citation, וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אֲבִיָּ֔ה וּדְרָכָ֖יו וּדְבָרָ֑יו כְּתוּבִ֕ים בְּמִדְרַ֖שׁ הַנָּבִ֥יא עִדּֽוֹ ("The rest of the acts of Abijah...are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo"); the incipit heading it, "וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י", is not fixed across the class -- 9:29 opens "וּשְׁאָר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י" and 12:15 opens "וְדִבְרֵ֣י", each its own variant -- but 13:22's exact head recurs verbatim at 20:34's "וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֔ט", its nearest lexical twin later in the book, while Asa's own closing formula at 16:11 varies further still, "וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י". That formula is the row's hard right edge: what follows is a death-and-succession report of a different, narrative kind, וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אֲבִיָּ֜ה עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקְבְּר֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד ("So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in David's city"), which also crosses into the WEB/MT offset (web:2Chr.14.1 = oshb:2Chr.13.23 (PE, single-witness, MT)).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 13:21-22 forward into the death-succession verse ignores that the source formula is itself the book's recognized reign-closer and that the offset zone begins only at the verse following it. The internal SAMEKH at 13:21 (single-witness) could instead split the household tally from the source-citation formula, but both are kept in one row because they are the same terse dynastic-tally genre this book's reign-closing block conventionally bundles, and a single tier-3 mark does not override that generic unity.

boundary_rationale: This single verse is the whole hinge of the WEB/MT offset, web:2Chr.14.1 = oshb:2Chr.13.23 (MT), וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אֲבִיָּ֜ה עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקְבְּר֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָסָ֥א בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו בְּיָמָ֛יו שָׁקְטָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ עֶ֥שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים (WEB: "So Abijah slept with his fathers, and they buried him in David's city; and Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days, the land was quiet ten years"). It is bounded on the left by Abijah's source-citation close (13:22) and on the right by Asa's own regnal-evaluation opening, web:2Chr.14.2 = oshb:2Chr.14.1 (MT), וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אָסָא֙ הַטּ֣וֹב וְהַיָּשָׁ֔ר בְּעֵינֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו ("Asa did that which was good and right in Yahweh his God's eyes"). Death-succession-peace and evaluation are distinct forms, so neither neighbor absorbs this verse cleanly; a PE mark (single-witness) follows it in the WLC, corroborating a break here. The verse's own "שָׁקְטָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ" ('the land was quiet') is not a one-off closing flourish, though: the same שקט root recurs in "וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה לְפָנָֽיו" (14:4 MT, WEB 14:5, 'the kingdom was quiet before him') and again in "כִּֽי שָׁקְטָ֣ה הָאָ֗רֶץ" (14:5 MT, WEB 14:6, 'for the land was quiet'), a verb chain recurring twice more, two rows later (M8-2Chr-058, whose span 2Chr.14.2-2Chr.14.8 contains both remaining occurrences), not across three consecutive rows -- MT 14:1-3 (= WEB 14:2-4) carry no שקט token at all, and the adjacent row M8-2Chr-056 (13:21-22) carries none either; that two-rows-later recurrence, not the WEB/MT numbering, is the honest ground for holding this one-verse row at medium rather than high despite its clean formulaic footing on both sides.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this verse to the following reform report as its opening line would blur the death-succession-peace formula into the evaluation formula, though the shared 'quiet' motif makes that reading the strongest rival.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the evaluation formula, web:2Chr.14.2 = oshb:2Chr.14.1 (MT), וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אָסָא֙ הַטּ֣וֹב וְהַיָּשָׁ֔ר בְּעֵינֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו, then itemizes cultic reform and a directive to Judah, web:2Chr.14.4 = oshb:2Chr.14.3 (MT), וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לִֽיהוּדָ֔ה לִדְר֕וֹשׁ אֶת יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וְלַעֲשׂ֖וֹת הַתּוֹרָ֥ה וְהַמִּצְוָֽה ("commanded Judah to seek Yahweh, the God of their fathers, and to obey his law and command"), before turning to peacetime building and, at the close, an army muster, web:2Chr.14.8 = oshb:2Chr.14.7 (MT), וַיְהִ֣י לְאָסָ֗א חַיִל֮ נֹשֵׂ֣א צִנָּ֣ה וָרֹמַח֒ מִֽיהוּדָה֙ שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אֶ֔לֶף וּמִבִּנְיָמִ֗ן נֹשְׂאֵ֤י מָגֵן֙ וְדֹ֣רְכֵי קֶ֔שֶׁת מָאתַ֥יִם וּשְׁמוֹנִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף כָּל אֵ֖לֶּה גִּבּ֥וֹרֵי חָֽיִל ("Asa had an army of three hundred thousand...two hundred eighty thousand"). That inventory-style muster closes the peacetime report; the next verse breaks in with a named foreign invader, web:2Chr.14.9 = oshb:2Chr.14.8 (MT), וַיֵּצֵ֨א אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם זֶ֣רַח הַכּוּשִׁ֗י ("Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them"), a participant-change device unlike the register material just closed. A PE mark (single-witness) already stands one verse earlier, after the building programme's own success formula at web:2Chr.14.7 = oshb:2Chr.14.6 (MT); a SAMEKH mark (single-witness) then follows the muster verse itself, so both tier-3 witnesses sit inside this closing pair rather than only the one the row leaned on.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying the muster (v8) forward as the Zerah unit's own cause-clause is possible, but Jehoshaphat's later muster at 17:14-19 closes an identical list-shape ("אֵ֖לֶּה הַמְשָׁרְתִ֣ים אֶת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ מִלְּבַ֞ד אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥ן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ בְּעָרֵ֥י הַמִּבְצָ֖ר בְּכָל יְהוּדָֽה", WEB "These were those who waited on the king, in addition to those whom the king put in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.") and is trailed by wholly unrelated material at 18:1 ("וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹ֑ב וַיִּתְחַתֵּ֖ן לְאַחְאָֽב"), not a battle -- showing a tallied muster caps a king's-strength report in this book's own convention rather than setting a scene for whatever follows, which is the discriminating reason the 'descriptive inventory' label alone was missing.

boundary_rationale: Zerah's entrance, web:2Chr.14.9 = oshb:2Chr.14.8 (MT), וַיֵּצֵ֨א אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם זֶ֣רַח הַכּוּשִׁ֗י ("Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them"), opens the war the prior row's muster anticipated. Inside it Asa's prayer is quoted, web:2Chr.14.11 = oshb:2Chr.14.10 (MT), וַיִּקְרָ֨א אָסָ֜א אֶל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָיו֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ ("Asa cried to Yahweh his God, and said"); under the inset rule it stays inside this battle report rather than forming its own row, since nothing frames it off on the far side and the very next clause is Yahweh's answering strike. The unit runs through pursuit and plunder to its close, web:2Chr.14.15 = oshb:2Chr.14.14 (MT), וְגַם אָהֳלֵ֥י מִקְנֶ֖ה הִכּ֑וּ וַיִּשְׁבּ֨וּ צֹ֤אן לָרֹב֙ וּגְמַלִּ֔ים וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם ("They also struck the tents of those who had livestock...then returned to Jerusalem"), which is also the last verse of the WEB/MT offset. A SAMEKH mark (single-witness) follows this verse, and the next unit opens with an unrelated prophetic frame, web:2Chr.15.1, וַעֲזַרְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן עוֹדֵ֔ד הָיְתָ֥ה עָלָ֖יו ר֥וּחַ אֱלֹהִֽים ("The Spirit of God came on Azariah the son of Oded"), where WEB and MT numbering realign.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating the prayer (v11) as its own row finds tier-3 color in the SAMEKH (single-witness) standing right behind it, between the prayer and the strike -- but per the marker policy that mark is weak corroboration only, never a driver, and the immediate divine strike shows prayer and victory are one continuous clause-chain, not a bracketed insert, so the mark does not unseat that continuity.

boundary_rationale: A fresh prophet-notice frame opens the row, וַעֲזַרְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן עוֹדֵ֔ד הָיְתָ֥ה עָלָ֖יו ר֥וּחַ אֱלֹהִֽים ("The Spirit of God came on Azariah the son of Oded"), and Azariah addresses Asa with the same vocative device Abijah used earlier in this part (13:4), here at v2, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ שְׁמָע֕וּנִי אָסָ֖א וְכָל יְהוּדָ֣ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ן ("and said to him, 'Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin'"). The oracle runs through Israel's lawless past to an exhortation and closes before Asa's reaction, וְכִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אָסָ֜א הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְהַנְּבוּאָה֮ עֹדֵ֣ד הַנָּבִיא֒ הִתְחַזַּ֗ק ("When Asa heard these words...he took courage"), a response formula that shifts from direct address to third-person report. A SAMEKH mark (single-witness) follows v7, corroborating the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the row through v8 to include Asa's response would merge two distinct forms, oracle and reform report, under one label, when the 'when X heard' formula is itself a recognized transition.

boundary_rationale: "וְכִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אָסָ֜א הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְהַנְּבוּאָה֮ עֹדֵ֣ד הַנָּבִיא֒ הִתְחַזַּ֗ק וַיַּעֲבֵ֤ר הַשִּׁקּוּצִים֙ מִכָּל אֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן וּמִן הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָכַ֖ד מֵהַ֣ר אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיְחַדֵּשׁ֙ אֶת מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֕ר לִפְנֵ֖י אוּלָ֥ם יְהוָֽה" ("When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominations out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from the hill country of Ephraim; and he renewed Yahweh’s altar that was before Yahweh’s porch.") opens his reform response to the oracle just closed, moving from idol removal to an assembly summons; the qal "וַיִּקְבֹּ֗ץ" of v.9, with Asa himself as agent, gives way to the niphal "וַיִּקָּבְצ֥וּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י לִשְׁנַ֥ת חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה לְמַלְכ֥וּת אָסָֽא" of v.10 ("So they gathered themselves together at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign."), the people now the grammatical subject of their own dated compliance -- a PE mark (single-witness) stands between the two verses, but v.10's niphal carries no independent subject expression of its own; it reads as the executed result of v.9's qal summons, with the date attaching to the compliance rather than opening a fresh scene, so the shift is summons-then-compliance inside one assembly frame, not an unmarked participant-change seam. (Disclosure: the strategy's device matrix labels this class 'קהל-family openings,' but a consonantal sweep of the whole of ch.15 returns zero קהל-root hits; the forms actually instantiated at 15:9-10 are both קבץ-root, so the device-matrix citation named for this locus is the wrong root family, and the text-internal grammatical reading above, not the matrix entry, is what carries this row's boundary reading.) Sacrifice and covenant oath follow, and the unit closes on the rest notice, "וַיִּשְׂמְח֨וּ כָל יְהוּדָ֜ה עַל הַשְּׁבוּעָ֗ה כִּ֤י בְכָל לְבָבָם֙ נִשְׁבָּ֔עוּ וּבְכָל רְצוֹנָ֣ם בִּקְשֻׁ֔הוּ וַיִּמָּצֵ֖א לָהֶ֑ם וַיָּ֧נַח יְהוָ֛ה לָהֶ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב" ("All Judah rejoiced at the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found by them. Then Yahweh gave them rest all around."), which is no bare topic-marker: the same rest-and-'all around' diction closes Asa's earlier building report three rows back, "וַיָּ֥נַֽח לָ֖נוּ מִסָּבִ֑יב" (14:6 MT, WEB 14:7, "he has given us rest on every side"), bracketing the whole reform-battle-covenant complex this cluster's rows traverse; only after that echoed close does the text pivot, "וְגַֽם מַעֲכָ֞ה אֵ֣ם אָסָ֣א הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ" ("Also Maacah, the mother of Asa the king"), to a personal notice no longer tied to the assembly. That right-edge pivot is a plain topic change rather than a marked formula, but it follows an inclusio-strengthened rest notice rather than a bare one, which is why confidence moves up here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying the row through v19 to include the Maacah and treasury notices would treat the whole chapter's second half as one block, obscuring that the assembly-and-oath material has its own inclusio-marked rest-notice close.

boundary_rationale: וְגַֽם מַעֲכָ֞ה אֵ֣ם אָסָ֣א הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ ("Also Maacah, the mother of Asa the king") opens a dynastic notice unconnected to the assembly just closed, at once qualified by וְהַ֨בָּמ֔וֹת לֹא סָ֖רוּ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ("the high places were not taken away out of Israel"), a caveat on the reform's completeness. It closes on the chronological peace notice, וּמִלְחָמָ֖ה לֹ֣א הָיָ֑תָה עַ֛ד שְׁנַת שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְחָמֵ֖שׁ לְמַלְכ֥וּת אָסָֽא ("There was no more war to the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign"), answered almost word for word by the next chapter's crisis, בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָשֵׁשׁ֙ לְמַלְכ֣וּת אָסָ֔א עָלָ֞ה בַּעְשָׁ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עַל יְהוּדָ֔ה ("In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha...went up"). That paired year-count is the row's firm right edge; its own left edge, the 'also' notice, is a weaker connective, so confidence is held at medium.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 15:16-18 as a coda separate from the v19 peace notice is possible, but v19 carries no formula strong enough to isolate it from the Maacah-and-fidelity material it summarizes.

boundary_rationale: The year-count crisis notice, בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָשֵׁשׁ֙ לְמַלְכ֣וּת אָסָ֔א עָלָ֞ה בַּעְשָׁ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עַל יְהוּדָ֔ה ("In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah"), answers 15:19's peace notice directly and opens the row. Asa's message to Ben-hadad is sent via the ordinary messenger formula closing v.2, "וַיֹּצֵ֨א אָסָ֜א כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֗ב מֵאֹֽצְר֛וֹת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֶל בֶּן הֲדַד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הַיּוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּדַרְמֶ֖שֶׂק לֵאמֹֽר" ("Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of Yahweh’s house and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben Hadad king of Syria, who lived at Damascus, saying,"), with the message itself quoted in full at v.3 alone, "בְּרִית֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ וּבֵ֥ין אָבִ֖י וּבֵ֣ין אָבִ֑יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה שָׁלַ֤חְתִּֽי לְךָ֙ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב לֵ֞ךְ הָפֵ֣ר בְּרִֽיתְךָ֗ אֶת בַּעְשָׁא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיַעֲלֶ֖ה מֵעָלָֽי" ("“Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Behold, I have sent you silver and gold. Go, break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.”"); it is a messenger speech rather than a letter -- no מכתב or אגרות lexeme appears in either verse, unlike the book's actual letter insets (21:12's "מִכְתָּ֔ב", 30:1's "אִגְּרוֹת֙") -- and as one verse of quoted content framed by v.2's sending notice, it stays inside this diplomatic-and-military report under the inset rule rather than forming its own row. Ben-hadad's raid answers the message at once, striking Israelite cities (v.4), and Baasha responds by abandoning the Ramah works, וַיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ בַּעְשָׁ֔א וַיֶּחְדַּ֕ל מִבְּנ֖וֹת אֶת הָרָמָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁבֵּ֖ת אֶת מְלַאכְתּֽוֹ (“when Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah, and let his work cease,” v.5); a SAMEKH (single-witness) follows this verse too. The unit closes on Asa's own building notice, וַיִּ֣בֶן בָּהֶ֔ם אֶת גֶּ֖בַע וְאֶת הַמִּצְפָּֽה ("he built Geba and Mizpah with them"), completing rather than merely following v.5's abandonment: Asa dismantles the very Ramah fortress named at v.1's opening and repurposes its stones and timber to build Geba and Mizpah, an inclusio on Ramah rather than two adjacent, unrelated building notices; the next verse introduces a new figure with a time-marker, וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא בָּ֚א חֲנָ֣נִי הָרֹאֶ֔ה אֶל אָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ("At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said"), a prophet-entrance frame unrelated to the building report. A SAMEKH mark (single-witness) follows the building notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting Asa's message off as its own row overstates a one-verse quoted speech that never functions apart from the two-verse sending-and-message frame that carries it.

boundary_rationale: Hanani's arrival, וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא בָּ֚א חֲנָ֣נִי הָרֹאֶ֔ה אֶל אָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ("At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said"), opens the row and echoes Azariah's earlier arrival in this same part (15:1-2), though the message here rebukes rather than exhorts, turning on כִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה עֵינָ֞יו מְשֹׁטְט֤וֹת בְּכָל הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ לְ֠הִתְחַזֵּק עִם לְבָבָ֥ם שָׁלֵ֛ם אֵלָ֖יו נִסְכַּ֣לְתָּ עַל זֹ֑את ("Yahweh's eyes run back and forth throughout the whole earth...You have done foolishly in this"). Unlike the Azariah scene, the reaction here is folded into the same row rather than answered by reform: וַיִּכְעַ֨ס אָסָ֜א אֶל הָרֹאֶ֗ה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֨הוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמַּהְפֶּ֔כֶת כִּֽי בְזַ֥עַף עִמּ֖וֹ עַל זֹ֑את וַיְרַצֵּ֥ץ אָסָ֛א מִן הָעָ֖ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא ("Then Asa was angry with the seer, and put him in the prison...Asa oppressed some of the people at the same time"), a single verse of hostile reaction too slight to carry its own row. The row ends there because v.11 opens the reign-closing source-citation class in its own presentative variant, וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א הָרִאשׁוֹנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֤ם כְּתוּבִים֙ ("Behold, the acts of Asa, first and last...are written") — that fronted וְהִנֵּה֙ opener is unique to 16:11 among the book's reign-closers, though its own closing verb (“they are written”) is not distinctive on its own: a consonantal sweep for henam ketuvim returns 11 hits book-wide (16:11, 20:34, 24:27, 25:26, 27:7, 28:26, 32:32, 33:19, 35:25, 35:27, 36:8), so it is the class's ordinary closing verb rather than a mark of 16:11's own individuality. The class's opener otherwise runs וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י ten times (13:22 among them), וּשְׁאָר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י once at 9:29, or a bare וְדִבְרֵ֣י at 12:15 -- and 24:27 is a further exception, opening on neither pattern, וּבָנָ֞יו ורב יִ֧רֶ֞ב הַמַּשָּׂ֣א עָלָ֗יו (“and his sons, and the greatness of the burden that was on him”), a second morphologically-deviant reign-closer beside 12:15's bare form. 16:11 shares the class's citation register (divre plus first-and-last plus 'written in the book') without repeating any of these other openers. Reinforcing this row's own close, the phrase וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא that opens Hanani's arrival in v.7 recurs to close v.10, בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא, a temporal bracket binding rebuke and reprisal into one span rather than resting on brevity alone.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the oracle (7-9) from Asa's one-verse reaction (10) would mirror the Azariah/response split in ch15, but the reaction here is too brief and too tightly bound to the rebuke's closing clause to stand alone.

boundary_rationale: וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א הָרִאשׁוֹנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֤ם כְּתוּבִים֙ עַל סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֔ים לִיהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל ("Behold, the acts of Asa, first and last...are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel") opens the row on the reign-closing source-citation class, though in its own presentative variant — a hinneh-opening rather than the וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י-type opener that heads ten other reign-closers in the book, Abijah's own included at 13:22 — sharing the class's register (divre plus first-and-last plus 'written in the book') without repeating 13:22's incipit. What follows is disease, וַיֶּחֱלֶ֣א אָסָ֡א בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלוֹשִׁ֨ים וָתֵ֤שַׁע לְמַלְכוּתוֹ֙ בְּרַגְלָ֔יו עַד לְמַ֖עְלָה חָלְי֑וֹ ("Asa was diseased in his feet...in the thirty-ninth year of his reign"), then the death notice proper, וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אָסָ֖א עִם אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיָּ֕מָת בִּשְׁנַ֛ת אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וְאַחַ֖ת לְמָלְכֽוֹ ("Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the forty-first year of his reign"), an instance of the book's own REGNAL DEATH-AND-SUCCESSION class (verified specimen at 21:1), then burial, וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֣הוּ בְקִבְרֹתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּֽרָה לוֹ֮ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִיד֒ וַיַּשְׁכִּיבֻ֗הוּ בַּמִּשְׁכָּב֙...וַיִּשְׂרְפוּ ל֥וֹ שְׂרֵפָ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֥ה עַד לִמְאֹֽד ("They buried him in his own tomb...and they made a very great fire for him"). The real asymmetry with Abijah's own close is not sequence — MT 13:23 (= WEB 14:1) likewise opens on death-and-burial, וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אֲבִיָּ֜ה עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקְבְּר֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד, right after 13:22's citation formula, the identical order this row follows — but completeness: 13:23 fuses death, burial, and succession in one verse, וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָסָ֥א בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו, while Asa's own successor is not named until 17:1, so nothing inside 16:12-14 supplies a rival succession notice to cut against. Together these four verses form Asa's whole reign-closing complex, and the row ends exactly at this part's assigned last verse; a PE mark (single-witness) follows it, and the next reign begins beyond this part with the succession formula וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו ("Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place").
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the disease-and-death notices (12-14) from the source formula (11) would separate a citation formula from the reign-summary material it introduces; unlike at 13:22/13:23, no succession clause sits inside 16:12-14 to supply a natural joint for such a cut.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the succession formula וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו (“Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place,” WEB 17:1), the accession-type specimen the book strategy already flags for this verse. Vv.2-6 unpack that opening as one theological assessment: military consolidation (v.2), the fidelity antithesis וְלֹ֥א דָרַ֖שׁ לַבְּעָלִֽים (“didn’t seek the Baals,” v.3) against לֵֽאלֹהֵ֤י אָבִיו֙ דָּרָ֔שׁ (“sought the God of his father,” v.4), the causal “therefore” of v.5 (Yahweh established the kingdom, tribute, riches and honor), and the closing reform notice הֵסִ֛יר אֶת הַבָּמ֥וֹת וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרִ֖ים מִיהוּדָֽה (“he took away the high places and the Asherah poles out of Judah,” v.6). V.7 then opens with its own dating clause, וּבִשְׁנַ֨ת שָׁל֜וֹשׁ לְמָלְכ֗וֹ שָׁלַ֤ח, tying the next episode to a specific regnal year with no antecedent in vv.1-6, marking a fresh initiative; restricted to this clause-initial form, the construction opens an episode at all five loci where it stands clause-initially — 13:1, 16:1, 17:7, 34:8, and 36:22 — whereas the same dated phrase continues a clause already underway wherever it falls mid-clause, at 3:2, 16:12, and 16:13, including twice within Asa's own account this very part closes. The PE mark following 17:6 (single-witness, tier-3) weakly corroborates this seam but is not the driver; the dated clause at v.7 is.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through v.9 to fold the law-teaching mission into the same assessment block loses the force of the v.7 regnal-year dating clause: narrowed to its clause-initial form, the construction opens a fresh episode at all five loci carrying it clause-initially (13:1, 16:1, 17:7, 34:8, 36:22), never continuing one already underway the way the identical dated phrase does at 3:2, 16:12, and 16:13, where it falls mid-clause.

boundary_rationale: A fresh regnal-year formula launches this unit, וּבִשְׁנַ֨ת שָׁל֜וֹשׁ לְמָלְכ֗וֹ שָׁלַ֤ח (“also in the third year of his reign he sent...”), introducing a named roster of officials, joined by the Levites and priests named at וְעִמָּהֶ֣ם הַלְוִיִּ֗ם...וְעִמָּהֶ֛ם אֱלִישָׁמָ֥ע וִֽיהוֹרָ֖ם הַכֹּהֲנִֽים ("with them the Levites...and with them Elishama and Jehoram the priests," v.8), whose task is stated in a resumptive repetition of the piel root lamad across three occurrences: v.7's purpose infinitive ("to teach in the cities of Judah") running into v.9's doubled finite verbs, וַֽיְלַמְּדוּ֙ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְעִ֨מָּהֶ֔ם סֵ֖פֶר תּוֹרַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּסֹ֨בּוּ֙ בְּכָל עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַֽיְלַמְּד֖וּ בָּעָֽם, opening and closing v.9 ("taught in Judah...and taught among the people"); the medial occurrence's own בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה complement echoes v.7's closing בְּעָרֵי יְהוּדָה, binding purpose and fulfillment on the shared place-name. This three-fold teach/taught/taught pattern closes the circuit report cleanly, with the intervening note that they carried וְעִ֨מָּהֶ֔ם סֵ֖פֶר תּוֹרַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (“the book of Yahweh’s law,” v.9). That teach/taught pairing closes the circuit report cleanly. V.10 pivots to a different grammatical subject and topic — a shift to what neighboring kingdoms now do toward Judah — with no verbal link back to the teaching mission’s vocabulary, so the unit does not run on into v.10.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading vv.7-11 as one ‘Jehoshaphat’s influence abroad’ unit conflates a completed teaching circuit, bracketed by its own teach/taught verbs, with a separate consequence-notice that opens its own vayehi clause; the PE after 17:11 (single-witness, tier-3) offers weak mark-level corroboration for that wider reading, but v.10's new-subject clause (a shift to what neighboring kingdoms now do toward Judah) breaks the teaching circuit before v.11 is reached, so the tier-1 grammatical signal still prevails over the tier-3 mark.

boundary_rationale: This two-verse notice opens on its own subject, וַיְהִ֣י פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֗ה עַ֚ל כָּל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת (“the fear of Yahweh fell on all the kingdoms...,” v.10), rather than continuing the teaching mission’s vocabulary, and reports a distinct consequence: regional non-aggression, then מְבִיאִ֧ים לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט מִנְחָ֖ה (“brought Jehoshaphat...tribute,” v.11) from Philistines and Arabians. V.12 opens a clause built on the identical new-subject device, וַיְהִ֧י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט הֹלֵ֥ךְ וְגָדֵ֖ל עַד לְמָ֑עְלָה ("Jehoshaphat grew great..."), so the seam here rests on a device this book does not treat as reliably boundary-driving -- the very next instance is absorbed without comment into an eight-verse catalog next door (M8-2Chr-069) rather than prompting a comparable split. Book-wide, the exact 'fear of Yahweh' string recurs at 14:13 (MT; dual-cited web:2Chr.14.14 = oshb:2Chr.14.13 (MT)) and 19:7, but the closer structural analogue is the clause-type וַיְהִי֙ פַּ֣חַד at 20:29, וַיְהִי֙ פַּ֣חַד אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל כָּל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת בְּשָׁמְעָ֕ם כִּ֚י נִלְחַ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה עִ֖ם אוֹיְבֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, matching 17:10 across six of its first seven words; that instance functions as an aftermath clause closing out the battle just narrated (20:27-30) rather than opening independent material, which cuts against, not for, reading vv.10-11 as their own unit. The marks bracket 17:7-11 as one unbroken witness-stretch, with a PE after 17:6 (single-witness) and a PE after 17:11 (single-witness) but no mark falling anywhere at 17:7-10 between them; that stretch is exactly co-extensive with the union of this row and M8-2Chr-067 (17:7-9), while the next marked stretch runs 17:12-19, exactly co-extensive with M8-2Chr-069's own span. This tier-3 material leans weakly toward the rival reading that would fold vv.10-11 forward with vv.7-9 rather than treating them as their own unit, but remains non-driving corroboration only.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating vv.10-11 as the direct fruit of vv.7-9's teaching campaign, or as an unmarked continuation folding forward into v.12's building notice, both remain live: the nearest analogue in the book (20:29) attaches this device to what precedes rather than launching a stand-alone unit. What differentiates vv.10-11 from both neighbors is content, not device: the two verses report Judah's external relations — regional non-aggression (v.10) then Philistine silver-tribute and quantified Arabian livestock (v.11) — a subject matter shared with neither the teaching circuit before it (17:7-9, M8-2Chr-067) nor the building-and-muster catalog after it (17:12-19, M8-2Chr-069).

boundary_rationale: Opens on the new subject-first clause וַיְהִ֧י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט הֹלֵ֥ךְ וְגָדֵ֖ל עַד לְמָ֑עְלָה ("Jehoshaphat grew great exceedingly; and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah," v.12), then moves into a register-style roster of Judah's and Benjamin's captains (vv.14-18). The roster is itself bracketed: it opens וְאֵ֥לֶּה פְקֻדָּתָ֖ם ("This was the numbering of them according to their fathers’ houses," v.14) and closes אֵ֖לֶּה הַמְשָׁרְתִ֣ים אֶת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ ("These were those who waited on the king," v.19), a 'these...these' frame marking the list as one self-contained catalog rather than a run of independent entries. This is a genuine tier-1 list-register seam -- וְאֵ֥לֶּה פְקֻדָּתָ֖ם is one of only four clause-initial vav-prefixed 'these' register-openers book-wide (3:3, 8:10, 17:14, 24:26); the roster's own bare-form closer at v.19 is a further clause-initial member of the wider 'these' class beyond that vav-prefixed set, reinforcing rather than weakening the bracket argument -- so the row concedes rather than dismisses that vv.12-13 sit two verses ahead of the catalog's own textually-marked start; the roster's own closing phrase, בְּעָרֵ֥י הַמִּבְצָ֖ר ("fortified cities," v.19), draws on 17:2's own עָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה הַבְּצֻר֑וֹת ("the fortified cities of Judah") rather than v.12's differently-rooted building notice, so the catalog's back-reference does not itself bind vv.12-13 into the list. What keeps them in one row is the occasion-and-catalog relationship: the strategy elsewhere licenses coarser treatment for register material of exactly this kind, not a shared vocabulary tie. The five SAMEKH marks after each named captain (17:14-18, single-witness) are per-entry list punctuation and, being that dense and regular, corroborate the catalog's internal formatting rather than any macro-seam; the PE mark keyed to 17:19 (single-witness) sits precisely at the roster's own closing formula. 18:1 then opens Jehoshaphat's marriage alliance with Ahab, a wholly new topic with its own vayehi clause.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 17:14, where the genuine list-register frame opens (one of only four clause-initial vav-prefixed 'these' register-openers in the book: 3:3, 8:10, 17:14, 24:26), is the real rival to weigh -- stronger than fragmenting the roster at each captain's SAMEKH (e.g., isolating 17:14-16 Judah from 17:17-18 Benjamin), which the marks themselves do not license as macro-divisions. It is not adopted here because vv.12-13's growth-and-building notice supplies the register's own occasion, and the book strategy's instruction to keep catalog material coarse favors holding occasion and catalog in one row over splitting on the register frame alone.

boundary_rationale: V.1 reuses 17:5's own royal-prosperity notice: 17:5 closes וַֽיְהִי ל֥וֹ עֹֽשֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹֽב ("he had riches and honor in abundance"), 18:1 opens וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹ֑ב וַיִּתְחַתֵּ֖ן לְאַחְאָֽב ("Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance...allied himself with Ahab"), the identical existential-plus-quantifier collocation with only the beneficiary changed from bound pronoun to proper name. This is a stock Chronistic royal-prosperity frame rather than a bespoke echo -- the same existential-plus-beneficiary shape recurs with a different quantifier at 32:27, וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד ("gloss: Hezekiah had riches and honor in great abundance") -- so the reuse functions as a resumptive relaunch of the narrative rather than a bracketing inclusio closing a unit that began at 17:5. The scene then runs continuously: descent to Samaria, Ahab's feast, and the enticement to Ramoth Gilead, וַיֵּרֶד֩ לְקֵ֨ץ שָׁנִ֤ים אֶל אַחְאָב֙ ("gloss: at the end of some years he went down to Ahab," v.2), then Jehoshaphat's assent, כָּמ֤וֹנִי כָמ֨וֹךָ֙ וּכְעַמְּךָ֣ עַמִּ֔י וְעִמְּךָ֖ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה ("gloss: I am as you are...we will be with you in the war," v.3). The bare noun for 'end' stands in exactly three verses book-wide -- 8:1, 18:2, and 21:19 -- each in a different prefixed or bare form, and only 8:1 and 18:2 carry it in a temporal-transition construction, which is all the positional argument needs. Unlike 8:1's own clause-initial opener, which opens a full temporal frame, 18:2's phrase is an adjunct subordinate to the already-fronted motion verb וַיֵּרֶד֩, continuing the subject Jehoshaphat established in v.1 rather than launching an independent time-frame; that positional difference, not silence about the lexeme, is why no formula break falls at v.2. V.4, by contrast, opens with Jehoshaphat's own counter-initiative ('inquire first for Yahweh's word'), redirecting the whole episode toward the prophetic inquiry that follows; that is the real pivot, not v.3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the 17:5/18:1 phrase repetition as an inclusio bracketing all of 17:1-18:1 into one ‘Jehoshaphat’s greatness’ unit ignores the dated and topic-shifted sub-episodes at 17:7, 17:10, and 17:12 that intervene, erasing real seams the text itself marks.

boundary_rationale: Jehoshaphat’s request, דְּרָשׁ נָ֥א כַיּ֖וֹם אֶת דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (“inquire first for Yahweh’s word,” v.4), opens the whole Micaiah episode by redirecting the king of Israel’s war plan toward prophetic consultation. What follows is one continuous movement: the king of Israel puts the question to the four hundred prophets, הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם אֶחְדָּ֑ל (“shall we go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or shall I forbear,” v.5), gets their unanimous yes, is pressed by Jehoshaphat for a genuine prophet, names and disparages Micaiah, and sends a messenger to fetch him who tries to coach his answer; the unit closes on Micaiah’s oath, חַי יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֛י אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֹאמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר (“as Yahweh lives...I will say what my God says,” v.13). V.14 narrates Micaiah’s arrival and puts the identical question to him, הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם אֶחְדָּ֑ל, word-for-word identical to v.5 (verified: this exact phrase recurs nowhere else in 2Chr) — a deliberate two-stage ‘ask the crowd, then ask the true prophet’ design that marks v.13/14 as the real seam within the inquiry scene, not any point inside vv.4-13.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The book strategy's own instruction to keep the inquiry scene 18:4-27 coherent (§5) might seem to bar any internal split, but the identical must-not-be-over-split language governs Solomon's dedication complex (§5, 5:2-7:22) while that complex is itself decomposed into its own named sub-parts (procession, prayer, theophany); read the same way here, the repeated question bracketing vv.5 and 14 marks a sub-division of one coherent scene into its two type-scene stages (ask the compliant crowd, then the true prophet), not a violation of the coherence instruction. Splitting instead at v.9 (the enthronement-and-audience notice) to separate the summons from the messenger's coaching would cut through the single unbroken 'send for Micaiah' action and has no formulaic marker of its own -- the weaker rival this row should not lean on.

boundary_rationale: The scene restarts with Micaiah’s arrival and the same question repeated verbatim from v.5, הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם אֶחְדָּ֑ל (v.14), then runs through the ironic false ‘go up’ (14b), the adjuration to speak truth (15), the true sheep-without-shepherd oracle (16), the king’s complaint to Jehoshaphat (17), Micaiah’s throne-vision speech, לָכֵ֖ן שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה (“hear Yahweh’s word,” vv.18-22), Zedekiah’s blow, וַיִּגַּשׁ֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בֶֽן כְּנַעֲנָ֔ה (“Zedekiah...came near,” v.23), and closes on Micaiah’s own oath and public address, שִׁמְע֖וּ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם (“listen, you people, all of you,” v.27). SAMEKH marks fall after 18:17 and 18:22 (both single-witness) and could tempt a finer three-way split (complaint / vision / confrontation), but that would sever the vision-speech from Zedekiah's blow in v.23, a direct physical reaction to what Micaiah has just said; the scene's dramatic logic depends on keeping speech and retaliation together, so the marks are disclosed only as non-driving tier-3 corroboration, not as the row's actual warrant. The PE mark after 18:27 (single-witness) falls exactly where the narrative genuinely turns outward to the march on Ramoth Gilead in v.28.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 18:18-22 as a separate oracle-inset row is defensible in the abstract -- וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָכֵ֖ן שִׁמְע֣וּ supplies a real opening frame, and its 'hear the word' collocation occurs nowhere else in 2Chr -- but the book strategy's own INSET RULE requires both an opening frame AND a resumption formula after to isolate an inset, and no resumption follows v.22 before Zedekiah's blow in v.23; failing that second half of the test, the vision-speech stays inside its host regardless of the SAMEKH marks at vv.17/22, and severing it here would in any case strand v.23's blow without its narrative trigger, fragmenting the single confrontation the source presents as one beat.

boundary_rationale: A new movement formula opens the unit, וַיַּ֧עַל מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָֽד (“the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat...went up to Ramoth Gilead,” v.28), leaving the court scene for the battlefield. The unit is held together by a deliberate matched pair of clauses: וַיְהִ֡י כִּרְאוֹת֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָרֶ֜כֶב אֶת יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט (“when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat,” v.31, the mistaken-identity danger, resolved when God diverts them) against וַיְהִ֗י כִּרְאוֹת֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב כִּ֥י לֹא הָיָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (“when the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel,” v.32, the correction that clears the way for Ahab’s actual death). Splitting between these mirrored clauses would break a doublet the text itself constructs; the unit only closes with the death notice וַיָּ֕מָת לְעֵ֖ת בּ֥וֹא הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (“he died at sunset,” v.34), which ends not just this row but the whole Ramoth Gilead episode — the next material, outside this part, opens a fresh return notice at 19:1.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v.31/32 to separate Jehoshaphat’s near-miss from Ahab’s actual death looks tidy by content but cuts directly through the mirrored ‘when the captains saw...when the captains saw’ doublet that binds the two halves into one action.

boundary_rationale: The opening breaks hard from the battlefield scene that closed the previous part: 18:34 ends with the king of Israel's death at sunset (וַיָּ֕מָת לְעֵ֖ת בּ֥וֹא הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ), a different subject in a different place, while 19:1 pivots to Jehoshaphat's own homecoming on the שוב root, “Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned to his house in peace to Jerusalem” (וַ֠יָּשָׁב יְהוֹשָׁפָ֨ט מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֧ה אֶל בֵּית֛וֹ בְּשָׁל֖וֹם לִֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם). Jehu ben Hanani's arrival supplies a genuine oracle-opening frame, וַיֵּצֵ֣א אֶל פָּנָ֗יו יֵה֣וּא בֶן חֲנָ֘נִי֮ הַחֹזֶה֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֔ט (“gloss: he went out to meet him, Jehu ben Hanani the seer, and said to King Jehoshaphat”), for the rebuke-and-mitigation oracle: “should you help the wicked, and love those who hate Yahweh?” (הֲלָרָשָׁ֣ע לַעְזֹ֔ר וּלְשֹׂנְאֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה תֶּאֱהָ֑ב) answered by “you have set your heart to seek God” (וַהֲכִינ֥וֹתָ לְבָבְךָ֖ לִדְרֹ֥שׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִֽים). Verse 4 answers the return notice not through its own opening verb but through its own internal returning-root pair: the king “went out again among the people…and brought them back to Yahweh” (וַיָּ֜שָׁב וַיֵּצֵ֣א בָעָ֗ם מִבְּאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֨בַע֙ עַד הַ֣ר אֶפְרַ֔יִם וַיְשִׁיבֵ֕ם אֶל יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽם), a finite-plus-hiphil pairing on the same returning root that opens 19:1's own וַ֠יָּשָׁב -- a textually-verifiable root-level inclusio bracketing the whole return-rebuke-response arc. (V.4 itself opens on the unrelated dwelling root, וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם, gloss: “Jehoshaphat lived at Jerusalem” -- a homograph of the returning-root form once vowel-pointing is set aside, not a shared root.) This inclusio is corroborated but not driven by the SAMEKH after v.4 (single-witness). That bracket is a real but unlisted device, thinner than a book_strategy_draft.md §1 tier-1 opener -- no time-frame transition, relocation, or new named subject falls at v.5 -- so the register shift to institutional appointment, “he set judges in the land” (וַיַּעֲמֵ֨ד שֹֽׁפְטִ֜ים בָּאָ֗רֶץ), rests on this thinner warrant, which is why this row's confidence does not claim more than the evidence supports.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating vv.2-3 as a standalone prophetic-judgment inset is not defeated merely by asserting no closing frame separates it: v.2's own arrival notice is a genuine oracle-opening frame, and v.4a's re-naming and re-locating of Jehoshaphat arguably answers it. The stronger ground for keeping vv.1-4 whole is structural: isolating vv.2-3 would strand the one-verse return notice at 19:1 as its own orphan row, and the SAMEKH mark (single-witness) falls after v.4 rather than between v.3 and v.4, so the only available tier-3 corroboration sits on the row's side of that seam, not the rival's.

boundary_rationale: Verse 5 opens a fresh administrative register, “he set judges in the land throughout all the fortified cities” (וַיַּעֲמֵ֨ד שֹֽׁפְטִ֜ים בָּאָ֗רֶץ), followed by a charge speech grounding the judges' authority in Yahweh rather than in man, “for you don't judge for man, but for Yahweh” (כִּ֣י לֹ֧א לְאָדָ֛ם תִּשְׁפְּט֖וּ כִּ֣י לַיהוָ֑ה). Verse 8 extends the same reform to Jerusalem with the additive “moreover”, “Moreover in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed…” (וְגַ֣ם בִּ֠ירוּשָׁלִַם הֶעֱמִ֨יד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֜ט), explicitly continuing rather than restarting the report, so the local judges and the central tribunal read as one installation, not two. The unit closes on the charge's own benediction, “Deal courageously…and may Yahweh be with the good” (חִזְק֣וּ וַעֲשׂ֔וּ וִיהִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִם הַטּֽוֹב), the last verse of ch.19, where a PE follows (single-witness); 20:1's own time-formula, “After this…” (וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן בָּ֣אוּ בְנֵי מוֹאָב֩ וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן), then opens an unrelated military crisis with new subjects, Moab and Ammon, confirming the break.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the local judges (5-7) from the Jerusalem tribunal (8-11) into separate rows ignores that v.8's “moreover” explicitly continues, rather than restarts, the appointment report.

boundary_rationale: “It happened after this” (וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן בָּ֣אוּ בְנֵי מוֹאָב֩ וּבְנֵ֨י עַמּ֜וֹן) opens a new crisis unrelated to the judicial reform just closed, and WEB signals the same reset with "After this". The coalition report escalates across two notices: a bare arrival (“the children of Moab, the children of Ammon…came against Jehoshaphat to battle”) and then a detailed messenger report locating the threat, “a great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea…from Syria” (בָּ֣א עָלֶ֜יךָ הָמ֥וֹן רָ֛ב מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיָּ֖ם מֵאֲרָ֑ם). Verse 3 answers with Jehoshaphat's own decisive act, reintroducing his name as grammatical subject: “Jehoshaphat was alarmed, and set himself to seek Yahweh. He proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah” (וַיִּרָ֕א וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט אֶת פָּנָ֖יו לִדְר֣וֹשׁ לַיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקְרָא צ֖וֹם עַל כָּל יְהוּדָֽה), a royal decree that closes the threat-and-response movement before the next verse shifts to the nation's own collective compliance, “Judah gathered themselves together”, a change of grammatical subject from king to people.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping only the two threat-notices (1-2) as their own row and folding v.3 into the assembly scene is defensible, since v.3's fast-proclamation directly triggers v.4's gathering; this rival is not clearly weaker, hence the reduced confidence on this row's closing edge.

boundary_rationale: Where the prior unit ended on the king's own decree to fast (וַיִּרָ֕א וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט אֶת פָּנָ֖יו לִדְר֣וֹשׁ לַיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקְרָא צ֖וֹם עַל כָּל יְהוּדָֽה), this one opens with the nation's collective action, “Judah gathered themselves together to seek help from Yahweh” (וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ יְהוּדָ֔ה לְבַקֵּ֖שׁ מֵֽיְהוָ֑ה גַּ֚ם מִכָּל עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה בָּ֖אוּ לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת יְהוָֽה), flowing directly into Jehoshaphat's standing address in the assembly, “Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in Yahweh's house” (וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט בִּקְהַ֧ל יְהוּדָ֛ה וִירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לִפְנֵ֖י הֶחָצֵ֥ר הַחֲדָשָֽׁה). The prayer builds to its own admission of helplessness, “we don't know what to do, but our eyes are on you” (וַאֲנַ֗חְנוּ לֹ֤א נֵדַע֙ מַֽה נַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה כִּ֥י עָלֶ֖יךָ עֵינֵֽינוּ), and the unit closes on the tableau of the whole community's posture, “all Judah stood before Yahweh, with their little ones, their wives, and their children” (וְכָ֨ל יְהוּדָ֔ה עֹמְדִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה גַּם טַפָּ֖ם נְשֵׁיהֶ֥ם וּבְנֵיהֶֽם); a single-witness PE sits at this close. Verse 14 then introduces an entirely new actor by full genealogy, and the Spirit's descent “in the middle of the assembly” answers rather than continues the human posture just described, marking the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking the prayer itself (5-12) away from its closing tableau (13) would isolate the oracle's answer from the very posture it responds to, since the assembly Jahaziel addresses in v.15 is the standing congregation just described in v.13.

boundary_rationale: This unit is framed by name: Jahaziel is introduced with a five-generation genealogy, “Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the sons of Asaph” (וְיַחֲזִיאֵ֡ל בֶּן זְכַרְיָ֡הוּ בֶּן בְּ֠נָיָה בֶּן יְעִיאֵ֧ל בֶּן מַתַּנְיָ֛ה הַלֵּוִ֖י מִן בְּנֵ֣י אָסָ֑ף הָיְתָ֤ה עָלָיו֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ הַקָּהָֽל), far fuller than the single patronymic given the seer who confronted Jehoshaphat at 19:2, “Jehu the son of Hanani the seer” (יֵה֣וּא בֶן חֲנָ֘נִי֮ הַחֹזֶה֒), marking this oracle as a set-piece.
