This is narrower than a unique exclusion: Uzziah too received a differentiated, causally-explained burial, “בִּשְׂדֵ֤ה הַקְּבוּרָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַמְּלָכִ֔ים כִּ֥י אָמְר֖וּ מְצוֹרָ֣ע ה֑וּא” (26:23, “in the field of burial which belonged to the kings, for they said, he is a leper”), against the plain notices for Amaziah (25:28) and Jotham (27:9); Ahaz alone is denied the royal tombs (לְקִבְרֵ֖י) specifically. 29:1's accession formula for Hezekiah lies beyond this part's range.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Detaching the burial-exclusion clause from the death formula it is grammatically part of would isolate a single causal clause (“because...”) from the sentence it explains.

boundary_rationale: The regnal-opening pair 29:1-2 begins exactly where the prior reign's death-and-succession formula ends: 'וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב אָחָ֜ז עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו ... וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הֽוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו' (28:27; WEB 'Ahaz slept with his fathers... Hezekiah his son reigned in his place') and a WLC single-witness PE break registers exactly at that handoff. The age-formula proper, 'בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה' and 'וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָתֵ֨שַׁע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם' (29:1; WEB 'Hezekiah began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem'), pairs with the fixed evaluation clause 'וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה' (29:2; WEB 'He did that which was right in Yahweh's eyes') to close a self-contained two-verse unit before the narrative pivots to a dated first-act notice at 29:3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 29:1-2 into the following temple-reopening narrative as one 'Hezekiah's first acts' span loses because the age+evaluation formula is a self-contained regnal-notice form, distinct from the dated first-year action that only begins at 29:3.

boundary_rationale: A dated first-year notice, “ה֣וּא בַשָּׁנָה֩ הָרִאשׁוֹנָ֨ה לְמָלְכ֜וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן פָּתַ֛ח אֶת דַּלְת֥וֹת בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה וַֽיְחַזְּקֵֽם” (29:3; WEB “In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of Yahweh’s house and repaired them.”), launches this span right after the evaluation formula closes at 29:2. Its own syntax is fronted and off-line -- an independent pronoun plus two date phrases ahead of the qatal פָּתַ֛ח -- unlike the wayyiqtol chain proper, which only begins at v4's וַיָּבֵ֥א; but nothing separates the dated act from what it triggers, since the doors Hezekiah opens are precisely what he then staffs by summoning the priests and Levites in the very next clause, so the 3/4 join shares one continuous first-act notice rather than splitting a date-heading from its own consequence. The summons of priests and Levites, “וַיָּבֵ֥א אֶת הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְאֶת הַלְוִיִּ֑ם וַיַּֽאַסְפֵ֖ם לִרְח֥וֹב הַמִּזְרָֽח” (29:4), runs straight into direct address with no intervening frame, “וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָהֶ֖ם שְׁמָע֣וּנִי הַלְוִיִּ֑ם עַתָּ֣ה הִֽתְקַדְּשׁ֗וּ וְקַדְּשׁוּ֙ אֶת בֵּ֤ית יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְהוֹצִ֥יאוּ אֶת הַנִּדָּ֖ה מִן הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ” (29:5; WEB “and said to them, “Listen to me, you Levites! Now sanctify yourselves, and sanctify the house of Yahweh, the God of your fathers, and carry the filthiness out of the holy place.”), so the inset rule keeps the reform-charge speech (5-11) inside its introducing narrative rather than isolating it. The speech's final imperative, “בָּנַ֕י עַתָּ֖ה אַל תִּשָּׁל֑וּ כִּֽי בָכֶ֞ם בָּחַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לַעֲמֹ֤ד לְפָנָיו֙ לְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ וְלִהְי֥וֹת ל֖וֹ מְשָׁרְתִ֥ים וּמַקְטִרִֽים” (29:11; WEB “My sons, don’t be negligent now; for Yahweh has chosen you to stand before him, to minister to him, and that you should be his ministers and burn incense.””), carries a WLC single-witness SAMEKH, after which 29:12 turns to a new grammatical subject, the Levites' own action.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating v3 as its own dated-heading row is the closer rival this challenge raised, but v3's opening clause is a real, completed action -- Hezekiah opening and repairing the temple doors, WEB "In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of Yahweh’s house and repaired them." -- not an emptiness the merger argument can lean on; the case for merger rests instead on sequence: v3 is a complete dated first act whose immediate consequence is the v4 summons, so treating it as a self-standing unit would strand a finished act from the very reform it sets in motion.

boundary_rationale: Subject change marks the seam here: “וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ הַ֠לְוִיִּם” (29:12; WEB “Then the Levites arose:”) follows directly on the SAMEKH-marked close of the speech at 29:11. The clan-by-clan roll (12-14) gives way to the Levites' own self-sanctifying and entry, “וַיַּֽאַסְפ֤וּ אֶת אֲחֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּֽתְקַדְּשׁ֔וּ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ כְמִצְוַת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּדִבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לְטַהֵ֖ר בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה” (29:15; WEB “They gathered their brothers, sanctified themselves, and went in, according to the commandment of the king by Yahweh’s words, to cleanse Yahweh’s house.”), but the purge of the sanctuary's inner part is priestly, not Levitical: “וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ הַ֠כֹּהֲנִים לִפְנִ֣ימָה בֵית יְהוָה֮ לְטַהֵר֒” (29:16; WEB “The priests went into the inner part of Yahweh’s house to cleanse it,”), with the Levites relaying the debris out to Kidron in the same verse. The dated completion note follows, “וַ֠יָּחֵלּוּ בְּאֶחָ֞ד לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן֮ לְקַדֵּשׁ֒ וּבְי֧וֹם שְׁמוֹנָ֣ה לַחֹ֗דֶשׁ בָּ֚אוּ לְאוּלָ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וַיְקַדְּשׁ֥וּ אֶת בֵּית יְהוָ֖ה לְיָמִ֣ים שְׁמוֹנָ֑ה וּבְי֨וֹם שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן כִּלּֽוּ” (29:17; WEB “Now they began on the first day of the first month to sanctify, and on the eighth day of the month they came to Yahweh’s porch. They sanctified Yahweh’s house in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.”), and the report to the king stays with this execution rather than opening a fresh unit: “וַיָּב֤וֹאוּ פְנִ֨ימָה֙ אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ” (29:18; WEB “Then they went in to Hezekiah the king”), where the same rare verb-root that named the priests' own entry to the inner house at 29:16 (an adverbial locative, פְּנִימָה, not a verb-root, attested in exactly three places in the book -- here, 29:16, and 3:4, where it names no entry at all, describing only the overlaid gold of the porch, WEB "The porch that was in front, its length, across the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and the height one hundred twenty; and he overlaid it within with pure gold.") now names their entry to report -- an adverbial-locative echo, not a shared verb-root, and a change of referent from the temple's inner house to the king's presence at that. The book's actual entry-verb, בוא 3mp wayyiqtol, occurs sixteen times in the book, including at 29:15 itself, which any exclusivity claim for the execution/report cohesion here has to set aside. It ends on the note about King Ahaz's discarded vessels, “הִזְנִיחַ֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֧ז בְּמַלְכוּת֛וֹ” (29:19; WEB “which King Ahaz threw away in his reign”), where a second WLC single-witness SAMEKH corroborates the shift to 29:20's new day and new royal subject.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off 29:18-19 as its own report-unit is the closer rival, since it opens with a location-and-addressee shift into Hezekiah's presence, but the same adverbial-locative פְּנִימָה naming the priests' inner-house entry at 29:16 recurs at 29:18's entry to report, tying report to execution rather than opening a fresh scene, notwithstanding the different referent each occurrence has.

boundary_rationale: Hezekiah's early rising reopens the action at 29:20, “וַיַּשְׁכֵּם֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֶּאֱסֹ֕ף אֵ֖ת שָׂרֵ֣י הָעִ֑יר וַיַּ֖עַל בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה” (WEB “Then Hezekiah the king arose early, gathered the princes of the city, and went up to Yahweh’s house.”), immediately after the SAMEKH-marked report closes at 29:19. The rite proceeds through the sevenfold sin-offering “פָרִים שִׁבְעָה֩ וְאֵילִ֨ים שִׁבְעָ֜ה וּכְבָשִׂ֣ים שִׁבְעָ֗ה וּצְפִירֵ֨י עִזִּ֤ים שִׁבְעָה֙ לְחַטָּ֔את עַל הַמַּמְלָכָ֥ה וְעַל הַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ וְעַל יְהוּדָ֑ה” (29:21; WEB “seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats, for a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah.”) and the priestly slaughter, ending on the summary atonement clause “לְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הָעוֹלָ֖ה וְהַחַטָּֽאת” (29:24; WEB “they made a sin offering with their blood on the altar, to make atonement for all Israel; for the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Israel.”). The primary officiant and authority-citation shift at 29:25, from the Aaronide priests slaughtering under the king's command, “וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לִבְנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים” (29:21; WEB “He commanded the priests the sons of Aaron”), to Levitical musicians installed under a newly cited authority, “וַיַּֽעֲמֵ֨ד אֶת הַלְוִיִּ֜ם בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֗ה בִּמְצִלְתַּ֨יִם֙ בִּנְבָלִ֣ים וּבְכִנֹּר֔וֹת בְּמִצְוַ֥ת דָּוִ֛יד וְגָ֥ד חֹזֵֽה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְנָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֑יא כִּ֧י בְיַד יְהוָ֛ה הַמִּצְוָ֖ה בְּיַד נְבִיאָֽיו” (29:25; WEB “He set the Levites in Yahweh’s house with cymbals, with stringed instruments, and with harps, according to the commandment of David, of Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet; for the commandment was from Yahweh by his prophets.”); the priests do not disappear -- they resume with trumpets at 29:26, “וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים בַּחֲצֹצְרֽוֹת” -- but the authority-citation formula, absent from the atonement rite of 20-24, is what marks this as a fresh unit -- the Hebrew quote and this WEB span now matched, running from the atonement clause through the verse's own royal-command כִּ֤-clause on both sides.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 29:20-36 as one continuous 'sacrifice liturgy' span loses because 29:25's shift to Levitical musicians under the cited authority of David, Gad, and Nathan introduces a new officiant-class and a new authority-citation formula absent from the atonement rite of 20-24.

boundary_rationale: A new authority-citation formula opens this span: “וַיַּֽעֲמֵ֨ד אֶת הַלְוִיִּ֜ם בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֗ה בִּמְצִלְתַּ֨יִם֙ בִּנְבָלִ֣ים וּבְכִנֹּר֔וֹת בְּמִצְוַ֥ת דָּוִ֛יד וְגָ֥ד חֹזֵֽה הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְנָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֑יא כִּ֧י בְיַד יְהוָ֛ה הַמִּצְוָ֖ה בְּיַד נְבִיאָֽיו” (29:25; WEB “He set the Levites in Yahweh’s house with cymbals, with stringed instruments, and with harps, according to the commandment of David, of Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet; for the commandment was from Yahweh by his prophets.”), distinct from the priestly rite just closed; a first single-witness SAMEKH follows 29:25 and a second follows 29:26, both disclosed here as tier-3 corroboration that never drives the call. The unit's real cohesion is a dependency, not a bracket: the burnt offering and song beginning together at 29:27, “וּבְעֵ֞ת הֵחֵ֣ל הָֽעוֹלָ֗ה הֵחֵ֤ל שִׁיר יְהוָה֙” (WEB “When the burnt offering began, Yahweh’s song also began,”), presupposes the personnel and instruments in place at 29:25-26, so the performance cannot be cut from its own setup: 29:25 is hiphil with Hezekiah as subject and the Levites alone as object, while 29:26 switches to qal with the Levites and priests together as subject and no royal agent -- a stem contrast the row preserves rather than attributing both classes' positioning to Hezekiah's hiphil act alone. It runs until “הַכֹּ֕ל עַ֖ד לִכְל֥וֹת הָעֹלָֽה” (29:28; WEB “until the burnt offering was finished.”) and closes on a terminal worship-gesture cluster rather than a true inclusio -- a book-wide sweep of שתחו-root forms finds exactly eleven occurrences in 2Chr, three of them consecutive here (29:28-30) with nothing of the kind at the span's 25-26 opening -- so the bowing at the offering's end, “כָּרְע֗וּ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְכָֽל הַנִּמְצְאִ֥ים אִתּ֖וֹ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֽוּ” (29:29), and the second bowing, “וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֽוּ” (29:30, bearing a WLC single-witness PE), form a closing doublet, not a frame proving unity on their own; the 29:27 dependency does that work instead. Hezekiah's own declarative speech opens a new phase at 29:31. A book-wide sweep of the שתחו-root confirms exactly eleven occurrences in 2Chr (7:3, 7:19, 7:22, 20:18, 24:17, 25:14, 29:28, 29:29, 29:30, 32:12, 33:3), three of them the consecutive closing doublet reported here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the instrument-setting (25-26) from the performance (27-30) loses because 29:27's burnt-offering-and-song opening presupposes the personnel and instruments just stationed in 25-26, a real dependency the two internal SAMEKH marks (25, 26) only weakly corroborate and cannot themselves overcome.

boundary_rationale: Hezekiah's own answered-and-said formula launches a new phase at 29:31, 'וַיַּ֨עַן יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר עַתָּ֨ה מִלֵּאתֶ֤ם יֶדְכֶם֙ לַיהוָ֔ה' (WEB 'Then Hezekiah answered, Now you have consecrated yourselves to Yahweh'), distinct from the fixed liturgy just closed. Freewill thank-offerings follow, and the Chronicler's own editorial aside on the priest shortage caps the sequence: 'רַ֤ק הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ הָי֣וּ לִמְעָ֔ט' (29:34) and 'כִּ֤י הַלְוִיִּם֙ יִשְׁרֵ֣י לֵבָ֔ב לְהִתְקַדֵּ֖שׁ מֵֽהַכֹּהֲנִֽים' (WEB '...the Levites were more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests'). The episode ends on the summary-notice formula 'כִּ֥י בְּפִתְאֹ֖ם הָיָ֥ה הַדָּבָֽר' (29:36; WEB 'for the thing was done suddenly'), flagged by a WLC single-witness PE at the chapter's close, before chapter 30 opens on an entirely new royal initiative addressed to all Israel and Judah.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Absorbing 29:31-36 back into the preceding liturgy row (treating 25-36 as one span) loses because 29:31's answered-and-said formula marks a new speech-initiated movement that only follows after the fixed cultic liturgy has already closed.

boundary_rationale: Chapter 30 begins on a scope shift beyond the prior row's Jerusalem-only reform: “וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל וִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וְגַֽם אִגְּרוֹת֙ כָּתַב֙ עַל אֶפְרַ֣יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לָב֥וֹא לְבֵית יְהוָ֖ה בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת פֶּ֔סַח לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל” (30:1; WEB “Hezekiah sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to Yahweh’s house at Jerusalem, to keep the Passover to Yahweh, the God of Israel.”), right after the PE-marked close of chapter 29. The king's counsel-taking, “וַיִּוָּעַ֨ץ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֛יו וְכָל הַקָּהָ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַפֶּ֖סַח בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִֽי” (30:2), leads to the decree's establishment, “וַיַּֽעֲמִ֣ידוּ דָבָ֗ר לְהַעֲבִ֨יר ק֤וֹל בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִבְּאֵֽר שֶׁ֣בַע וְעַד דָּ֔ן לָב֞וֹא לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת פֶּ֛סַח לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֣י לֹ֥א לָרֹ֛ב עָשׂ֖וּ כַּכָּתֽוּב” (30:5; WEB “from Beersheba even to Dan,”). A courier-dispatch frame plus the speech-opening infinitive construct לֵאמֹ֑ר takes over at 30:6, ending the deliberation-report register. The near edge, however, is thinner than the far one: 30:1's opening verb is an ordinary narrative wayyiqtol, structurally identical to the wayyiqtol forms opening 30:5, 30:6 and 30:10 elsewhere in this same chapter, carrying no distinguishing grammatical form of its own; the near edge in fact rests on the topical scope-widening plus the tier-3 PE after 29:36, which corroborates but never drives. Only the far edge, 30:6's courier-dispatch frame plus the speech-opening infinitive construct, is tier-1 grounded in its own distinct form. book_strategy_draft.md §6 flags 30:1-12 broadly as a low-confidence letter-section-edges region; that flag is better honored than overridden here, since only one of this row's two edges carries its own grammatical warrant.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the letter itself (30:1-9 as one 'royal Passover initiative') loses because 30:6's courier-dispatch frame plus the speech-opening infinitive construct לֵאמֹ֑ר marks a formal shift from reported deliberation to direct-quoted letter content.

boundary_rationale: A messenger formula frames the letter on its near side: “וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ הָרָצִ֨ים בָּֽאִגְּר֜וֹת מִיַּ֧ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֗יו בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וּכְמִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שׁ֚וּבוּ אֶל יְהוָ֗ה” (30:6; WEB “saying, “You children of Israel, turn again to Yahweh,”). The exhortation runs through “וְאַל תִּֽהְי֗וּ כַּאֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ וְכַ֣אֲחֵיכֶ֔ם” (30:7; WEB “Don’t be like your fathers and like your brothers,”) and “עַתָּ֕ה אַל תַּקְשׁ֥וּ עָרְפְּכֶ֖ם כַּאֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם” (30:8; WEB “Now don’t be stiff-necked, as your fathers were,”), ending on its own appeal, “כִּֽי חַנּ֤וּן וְרַחוּם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹא יָסִ֤יר פָּנִים֙ מִכֶּ֔ם אִם תָּשׁ֖וּבוּ אֵלָֽיו” (30:9; WEB “because Yahweh your God is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you if you return to him.””), which carries a WLC single-witness PE. The frame closes on the far side too: 30:10's “וַיִּֽהְי֨וּ הָרָצִ֜ים עֹבְרִ֨ים” resumes the same runners-motif that opened the letter, satisfying the inset rule's requirement of isolation on both sides.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the letter merged with its surrounding courier narrative (30:1-12 as one unit) loses because the resumptive repetition of the runners-motif at 30:10, mirroring 30:6, is itself a tier-1 frame closing the inset on both sides, so isolating the quoted letter better preserves the deliberation-report and response-notice around it.

boundary_rationale: The runners-motif resumes narration once the letter's frame closes: “וַיִּֽהְי֨וּ הָרָצִ֜ים עֹבְרִ֨ים” (30:10; WEB “So the couriers passed from city to city”). Mixed response follows, and the contrast particle introduces the humbled exception, “אַךְ אֲנָשִׁ֛ים מֵאָשֵׁ֥ר וּמְנַשֶּׁ֖ה וּמִזְּבֻל֑וּן נִֽכְנְע֔וּ וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם” (30:11; WEB “Nevertheless some men of Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.”). The row ends on its own summary clause, “גַּ֣ם בִּיהוּדָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ יַ֣ד הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם לֵ֣ב אֶחָ֑ד לַעֲשׂ֞וֹת מִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִ֖ים בִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה” (30:12; WEB “Also the hand of God came on Judah to give them one heart, to do the commandment of the king and of the princes by Yahweh’s word.”), before 30:13 opens an entirely new gathering formula at Jerusalem. Though 30:12's cause clause -- to do the king's commandment -- is what 30:13's assembly then carries out, its opening גַּ֣ם ('also') continues the region-by-region tally begun at 30:10-11 (Ephraim/Manasseh/Zebulun, then Asher/Manasseh/Zebulun, then Judah) rather than launching the gathering itself, so the mixed-reception report stays a closed short unit before 30:13's fresh formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 30:12 forward into the assembly-and-Passover unit (30:10-13) is the stronger rival, since 30:12's cause clause is what 30:13's assembly executes, but it is answered by reading 30:12's גַּ֣ם as continuing the response tally already running through 30:10-11, keeping the mixed-reception report its own closed unit.

boundary_rationale: A fresh gathering formula launches this span at 30:13, “וַיֵּֽאָסְפ֤וּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עַם רָ֔ב ... קָהָ֖ל לָרֹ֥ב מְאֹֽד” (WEB “Many people assembled at Jerusalem ... a very great assembly.”), distinct from the 'one heart' summary that just closed. The assembly purges idolatrous altars, “וַיָּקֻ֕מוּ וַיָּסִ֨ירוּ֙ אֶת הַֽמִּזְבְּח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם” (30:14), slaughters the Passover on schedule, “וַיִּשְׁחֲט֣וּ הַפֶּ֔סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִ֑י” (30:15; WEB “Then they killed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month.”), following כְּתוֹרַ֖ת מֹשֶׁ֣ה אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (30:16; WEB “according to the law of Moses the man of God.”), and reaches its far edge in the verse accounting for the Levites' expanded role, “כִּי רַבַּ֥ת בַּקָּהָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם עַל שְׁחִיטַ֣ת הַפְּסָחִ֗ים לְכֹל֙ לֹ֣א טָה֔וֹר לְהַקְדִּ֖ישׁ לַיהוָֽה” (30:17; WEB “For there were many in the assembly who had not sanctified themselves; therefore the Levites were in charge of killing the Passovers for everyone who was not clean, to sanctify them to Yahweh.”). 30:18 opens with its own כי-clause, “כִּ֣י מַרְבִּ֣ית הָעָ֡ם רַ֠בַּת מֵֽאֶפְרַ֨יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֜ה יִשָּׂשכָ֤ר וּזְבֻלוּן֙ לֹ֣א הִטֶּהָ֔רוּ” (WEB “For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves,”), so the seam is not procedural mechanics giving way to causal explanation -- both verses open causally -- but a shift in what the cause clause accounts for. 30:15's slaughter verb has no stated subject; the same verse separately names the priests and Levites as those who "were ashamed and sanctified themselves," and 30:16 puts the Levites at the blood-relay, not at the knife. The text nowhere establishes that 30:15's unnamed slaughterers are the Levites, so 30:17's own Levitical slaughter is new information -- not an explanation of an act already told -- formally parallel to 30:18's eating-violation clause: 30:17 introduces the Levitical accommodation for the unsanctified, and 30:18's own causal clause introduces the unresolved Passover-eating violation among northern pilgrims that only Hezekiah's prayer, opening later in the same verse, resolves.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this span through to 30:18b's prayer frame is the more serious rival, since both 30:17 and 30:18a open with coordinate כי-clauses on the same purity problem, but 30:17's introduces the Levites' new accommodating role while 30:18's introduces the unresolved eating-violation that only the prayer resolves, so the sharper register shift is the prayer's own mid-verse introduction, not the clause boundary at 17/18.

boundary_rationale: This row groups the whole verses that carry the amnesty prayer, as book_strategy_draft.md §5 (Block map) anticipates ('amnesty prayer 30:18-20'); §1 (Genre and device matrix) locates only the sub-verse span '30:18b-19' for this same prayer, and it is that narrower citation the row's own near-edge warrant matches, since the unit's governing device sits mid-verse, not at 30:18's opening: “כִּ֣י מַרְבִּ֣ית הָעָ֡ם רַ֠בַּת מֵֽאֶפְרַ֨יִם וּמְנַשֶּׁ֜ה יִשָּׂשכָ֤ר וּזְבֻלוּן֙ לֹ֣א הִטֶּהָ֔רוּ” (30:18a; WEB “For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not cleansed themselves,”) is a כי-clause matching 30:17's own opening, “כִּי רַבַּ֥ת בַּקָּהָ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא הִתְקַדָּ֑שׁוּ”, in particle, quantifier, and a negated purity verb, so it continues the previous row's purity-problem language rather than opening a fresh unit on its own. The row's actual near-edge warrant is the prayer's own introduction, arriving later in the same verse, “כִּי֩ הִתְפַּלֵּ֨ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב יְכַפֵּ֥ר בְּעַֽד” (WEB “For Hezekiah had prayed for them, saying, “May the good Yahweh pardon everyone”), the middle causal clause of 30:18, WEB "yet they ate the Passover other than the way it is written," being the fresh cultic-offence clause that the petition's own verb actually pardons, so 30:18a is not wholly retrospective, which book_strategy_draft.md §1 itself locates at '30:18b-19.' The petition continues in 30:19, “וְלֹ֖א כְּטָהֳרַ֥ת הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ” (WEB “even if they aren’t clean according to the purification of the sanctuary.””), and the divine-response notice answers it directly, “וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶל יְחִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּרְפָּ֖א אֶת הָעָֽם” (30:20; WEB “Yahweh listened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.”), where a WLC single-witness SAMEKH corroborates. Subject and scope shift entirely at 30:21 to the people's own seven-day celebration.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the prayer merged with the surrounding Passover-practice report (13-20 as one span) loses because the mid-verse prayer-introduction formula at 30:18b and 30:20's divine-response notice frame the intercession as its own resolvable unit, distinct from the ritual mechanics reported in 13-17, even though 30:18a's own opening still belongs to that prior problem-language rather than to the prayer itself.

boundary_rationale: New grammatical subject and new time-frame mark the seam at 30:21, “וַיַּעֲשׂ֣וּ בְנֵֽי יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל הַנִּמְצְאִ֨ים בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם אֶת חַ֧ג הַמַּצּ֛וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה” (WEB “kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness.”), replacing the Hezekiah-and-Yahweh focus of the prayer unit; a WLC single-witness SAMEKH falls after this verse too, alongside the one disclosed at its far edge; a third mark, also SAMEKH, sits at 30:20, the join immediately preceding this row's own near edge -- the only one of the three nearby marks that corroborates an edge of this row rather than its interior. The tally here is three marks in total, none driving the call. Hezekiah's encouragement of the Levites follows, “וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ עַל לֵב֙ כָּל הַלְוִיִּ֔ם” (30:22; WEB “Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites”), reaching its far edge in the confession notice “וּמִ֨תְוַדִּ֔ים לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽם”, where a second WLC single-witness SAMEKH falls; both marks corroborate the surrounding two-verse span only weakly and do not drive the call. A fresh deliberation opens the next verse, “וַיִּוָּֽעֲצוּ֙ כָּל הַקָּהָ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים” (30:23; WEB “The whole assembly took counsel to keep another seven days,”), over a new deliberative object, seven more days beyond the feast just completed; the counsel-verb itself is not distinctive -- niphal wayyiqtol י-ע-ץ recurs seven times in the book, including 10:8 mid-episode with no accompanying break, and 30:2's form is third-singular against 30:23's third-plural -- so the new time-object, not a repeated verb-form, is what marks the fresh assembly decision.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 30:21-27 as one continuous 'feast of unleavened bread' span loses because 30:23's new deliberative object, seven additional days beyond the feast just completed, marks a fresh assembly decision separate from the days just reported, though the short span involved makes this a genuine close call.

boundary_rationale: A fresh assembly decision opens this span at 30:23, over a new deliberative object beyond the feast just completed, “וַיִּוָּֽעֲצוּ֙ כָּל הַקָּהָ֔ל לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים” (WEB “The whole assembly took counsel to keep another seven days,”); the counsel-taking verb itself recurs as thematic resonance with the Passover's original authorization at 30:2, “וַיִּוָּעַ֨ץ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ וְשָׂרָ֛יו וְכָל הַקָּהָ֖ל בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַפֶּ֖סַח בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִֽי” (WEB “For the king had taken counsel with his princes and all the assembly in Jerusalem to keep the Passover in the second month.”), but the two verbs differ in number (30:2's third-singular against 30:23's third-plural) and the same niphal form recurs elsewhere in the book without any accompanying break (10:8), so it is the new object, not a repeated form, that opens the span. Provisioning by king and princes follows, “כִּ֣י חִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְ֠הוּדָה” (30:24; WEB “For Hezekiah king of Judah”), and the joy notice recalling Solomon, “כִּ֠י מִימֵ֞י שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בֶן דָּוִיד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א כָזֹ֖את בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם” (30:26; WEB “for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Israel there was nothing like this in Jerusalem.”), gives way to the priestly benediction ascending to heaven, “וַיָּקֻ֜מוּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַלְוִיִּם֙ וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ אֶת הָעָ֔ם וַיִּשָּׁמַ֖ע בְּקוֹלָ֑ם וַתָּב֧וֹא תְפִלָּתָ֛ם לִמְע֥וֹן קָדְשׁ֖וֹ לַשָּׁמָֽיִם” (30:27; WEB “Then the Levitical priests arose and blessed the people. Their voice was heard, and their prayer came up to his holy habitation, even to heaven.”), where a WLC single-witness PE falls exactly at this close; marks recur throughout this stretch -- SAMEKH at 30:22, 30:24, 30:26 and 31:1 as well, with 30:24 and 30:26 lying inside this row's own span -- so the closing PE reads as one of several tier-3 marks corroborating this run rather than an isolated signal. The book's next unit opens on the completion-transition formula “וּכְכַלּ֣וֹת כָּל זֹ֗את” (31:1; WEB “Now when all this was finished,”), a fresh scene outside this part's range.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the extension-decision (23) from the provisioning-and-closing material (24-27) loses because the decree and its immediate provisioning, joy, and benediction form one continuous festival-extension report closed only once, by the ascension-to-heaven formula at 30:27.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the temporal-completion formula וּכְכַלּ֣וֹת כָּל זֹ֗את, WEB “Now when all this was finished,”, pivoting from the just-completed Passover feast (outside this part) to its physical aftermath: the assembled worshippers fan out through Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh to break the pillars, cut down the Asherim, and tear down the high places and altars “until they had destroyed them all.” The verse is a bounded sweep-and-return report, closing on the collective dispersal formula וַיָּשׁ֜וּבוּ כָּל בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אִ֥ישׁ לַאֲחֻזָּת֖וֹ לְעָרֵיהֶֽם, WEB “Then all the children of Israel returned, every man to his possession, into their own cities.” Verse 2 reopens on an entirely different actor and register with a fresh wayyiqtol subject, Hezekiah organizing priestly and Levitical rotas inside the temple, not the nationwide crowd tearing down shrines. The SAMEKH following v1 (single-witness) gives only weak corroboration that a unit break falls here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Annexing v1 to the preceding Passover complex as its coda is possible since “all this” refers back to it, but the prior part's seam-out already lands at 31:1 and the verse's own self-contained return-and-dispersal shape gives it complete internal unity apart from what follows.

boundary_rationale: Two explicit royal ordinances bracket a verbless middle clause, and the unit's real cohesion is the null-subject continuity across it: “וַיַּעֲמֵ֣ד יְחִזְקִיָּ֡הוּ אֶת מַחְלְק֣וֹת הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְ֠הַלְוִיִּם עַֽל מַחְלְקוֹתָ֞ם אִ֣ישׁ כְּפִ֣י עֲבֹדָת֗וֹ לַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְלַלְוִיִּ֔ם לְעֹלָ֖ה וְלִשְׁלָמִ֑ים לְשָׁרֵת֙ וּלְהֹד֣וֹת וּלְהַלֵּ֔ל בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֖י מַחֲנ֥וֹת יְהוָֽה”, “Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests…” (v2), names Hezekiah explicitly, but v3, “וּמְנָת֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ מִן רְכוּשׁ֜וֹ לָעֹל֗וֹת לְעֹלוֹת֙ הַבֹּ֣קֶר וְהָעֶ֔רֶב וְהָ֣עֹל֔וֹת לַשַּׁבָּת֖וֹת וְלֶחֳדָשִׁ֣ים וְלַמֹּעֲדִ֑ים כַּכָּת֖וּב בְּתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה”, has no finite verb and no expressed royal subject -- only the genitive 'the king's portion' inside a nominal clause -- so v4's null-subject וַיֹּ֤אמֶר … לָתֵ֕ת מְנָ֥ת הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם, “he commanded… to give the portion of the priests and the Levites”, recovers its referent back across the nominal v3 to v2's explicit יְחִזְקִיָּ֡הוּ. The chain closes on a rare clause-final formula shared by only one other verse in the book: בְּתוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָֽה, 'in Yahweh's law,' ends both v3 and v4, and recurs just once more, at 35:26. A book-wide sweep confirms תורת יהוה occurs six times in 2Chr (12:1, 17:9, 31:3, 31:4, 34:14, 35:26) against תורת משה only twice (23:18, 30:16); restricted to the bound ב-form the chain here actually uses, the tally is three (31:3, 31:4, 35:26) against one (23:18, since 30:16 uses כ- rather than ב-). The unit stops before the causal hinge of v5, וְכִפְרֹ֣ץ הַדָּבָ֗ר, “as soon as the commandment went out”, which shifts the narrative from command to the people's response.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv2-4 into the compliance narrative that follows (vv5-10) as one long provisioning unit is tempting since v4's command is the direct antecedent of v5's response, but it would blur the command/response hinge and merge pure legislation with reported popular action.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the causal hinge, rendered by WEB as “As soon as the commandment went out,” (וְכִפְרֹ֣ץ הַדָּבָ֗ר, more literally 'when the matter broke forth'), turning royal legislation (vv2-4) into narrated compliance: firstfruits and tithe of grain, wine, oil and honey (v5); Israel and Judah bringing the tithe of herd, flock, and dedicated things and heaping it, “וַֽיִּתְּנ֖וּ עֲרֵמ֥וֹת עֲרֵמֽוֹת” (v6; WEB “and laid them in heaps.” -- the doubled Hebrew noun underlying WEB's single 'heaps'), corroborated by a single-witness SAMEKH; a fixed third-to-seventh-month timeline for completing the heaps, “בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֔י הֵחֵ֥לּוּ הָעֲרֵמ֖וֹת לְיִסּ֑וֹד וּבַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י כִּלּֽוּ” (v7), corroborated by a second single-witness SAMEKH; Hezekiah and the princes coming to inspect and bless what has accumulated, “וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ וְהַשָּׂרִ֔ים וַיִּרְא֖וּ אֶת הָעֲרֵמ֑וֹת וַֽיְבָרֲכוּ֙” (v8), corroborated by a single-witness PE; Hezekiah's inquiry (v9); and Azariah the chief priest's answer, closing on the summary וְהַנּוֹתָ֖ר אֶת הֶהָמ֥וֹן הַזֶּֽה, WEB “that which is left is this great store.”” (v10). None of the four tier-3 marks drives the seam -- a fourth mark, SAMEKH, sits at the span's own closing verse, v10, corroborating the far edge rather than the interior: the time-frame at v7 and the arrival of Hezekiah and the princes at v8 are real internal transitions, but both belong to the single inspection movement the tithe-bringing of vv5-7 is building toward -- the heaps have to be completed and dated before there is anything for the king to come inspect, question, and receive Azariah's answer about -- so the report holds together as one compliance-and-inspection unit rather than splitting at either point. Verse 11's fresh command, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ לְהָכִ֧ין לְשָׁכ֛וֹת בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה, 'Hezekiah commanded... to prepare rooms...', pivots from narrated abundance to the administrative apparatus built to store and distribute it, introducing a roster of previously unnamed officials.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the span at v7's time-frame notice or v8's arrival of Hezekiah and the princes is the closer internal rival, but both mark stages within one inspection movement -- dated heap-completion feeding directly into the king's arrival to inspect and question -- rather than two separable reports, so the tier-3 SAMEKH/PE marks at each stage corroborate without dividing it.

boundary_rationale: Hezekiah's command to prepare rooms, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ לְהָכִ֧ין לְשָׁכ֛וֹת בְּבֵ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה, immediately shifts into list-register mode: named overseers Conaniah and Shimei (v12); ten further named officers (v13); the gatekeeper Kore over the freewill offerings (v14); six named men, stationed under Kore's hand in the cities of the priests, distributing by division “to the great as well as to the small” (v15); three successive genealogical-registration clauses, covering males from age three (v16), then the priests by their fathers' houses and the Levites specifically from twenty years old and upward (v17, “וְהַ֨לְוִיִּ֔ם מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָ֑עְלָה” -- the age qualifier attaches to the Levites alone, not to both groups), then the whole household congregation (v18). V19 puts the sons of Aaron in the lamed phrase as recipients and introduces a distinct group of named men as the ones distributing portions to them (matching WEB: 'for the sons of Aaron the priests... there were men who were mentioned by name to give portions'), closing וּלְכָל הִתְיַחֵ֖שׂ בַּלְוִיִּֽם, “and to all who were listed by genealogy among the Levites” (v19). The book strategy flags this whole span as register-like and directs coarse handling rather than a verse-by-verse split of its names and categories. Verse 20 breaks the list format outright with an evaluative clause, וַיַּ֧עַשׂ כָּזֹ֛את יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכָל יְהוּדָ֑ה, “Hezekiah did so…”, assessing the king's conduct rather than cataloging personnel.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at the seam between named-overseer material (12-15) and the purely genealogical clauses (16-19) has some content support, but the strategy's explicit coarse-treatment instruction for this register outweighs multiplying near-identical list-formula rows.

boundary_rationale: Pivots entirely out of list-format into a summarizing verdict: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ כָּזֹ֛את יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכָל יְהוּדָ֑ה, “Hezekiah did so throughout all Judah”, followed by the evaluative triad “the good, the right, and וְהָ֣אֱמֶ֔ת” (the faithful/true) before Yahweh his God (v20). Verse 21 extends the same verdict across “every work he began… with all his heart”, closing on בְּכָל לְבָב֥וֹ עָשָׂ֖ה וְהִצְלִֽיחַ, “he did it… and prospered” — a stock Chronicles success-formula close, corroborated weakly by the PE mark (single-witness) that follows v21. This two-verse unit is the evaluative coda to the whole provisions complex (31:1-19), not fresh narrative content.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Appending vv20-21 to the register of vv11-19 as its concluding lines shares the same reform program, but it would merge a summarizing verdict with a list-format catalog across a clean pivot in verb and rhetorical mode.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the time-frame transition אַחֲרֵ֨י הַדְּבָרִ֤ים וְהָאֱמֶת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה בָּ֖א סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר, “after these things and this faithfulness… Sennacherib… came”, a formula the book strategy expects at exactly this seam; it even echoes the root of וְהָ֣אֱמֶ֔ת from 31:20 while launching a wholly new arc: Sennacherib's invasion. The unit spans Hezekiah's defensive water-stopping (vv2-4), fortification and armament (v5), appointment of war-captains (v6), and his direct address to the mobilized people, חִזְק֣וּ וְאִמְצ֔וּ…, “be strong and courageous”, ending וַיִּסָּמְכ֣וּ הָעָ֔ם עַל דִּבְרֵ֖י יְחִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה, “the people rested themselves on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah” (v8). Per the inset rule this royal speech stays inside its host mobilization scene: nothing frames it as isolated on both sides, since v6 sets it up and v8b folds straight back into narration without a resumption formula that would justify carving it out. Verse 9's אַ֣חַר זֶ֗ה שָׁ֠לַח, “after this, Sennacherib sent…”, returns Sennacherib himself to the grammatical subject and opens a different mode of aggression, verbal rather than defensive.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating Hezekiah's speech (vv7-8) as its own row is the natural rival given the direct quotation, but the inset rule requires a tier-1 closing frame that resumes narration distinctly from the speech, and v8b's report of the people's response continues the same beat rather than reopening one.

boundary_rationale: Reopens with אַ֣חַר זֶ֗ה שָׁ֠לַח, restoring Sennacherib as subject and launching the messenger-taunt scene, corroborated by a single-witness PE just before it at 32:8: his royal speech is quoted at length (vv10-15), addressed second-person to the besieged. Verse 16, וְעוֹד֙ דִּבְּר֣וּ עֲבָדָ֔יו, a paraphrase, not a WEB quotation (WEB reads "His servants spoke yet more against Yahweh God and against his servant Hezekiah."), signals continuation but its own plural verb governs only that clause; v17 shifts to a third-singular qatal with Sennacherib alone as subject and the object fronted, וּסְפָרִ֣ים כָּתַ֔ב, a paraphrase, not a WEB quotation (WEB reads "He also wrote letters insulting Yahweh, the God of Israel, and speaking against him, saying, “As the gods of the nations of the lands, which have not delivered their people out of my hand, so shall the God of Hezekiah not deliver his people out of my hand.”"), and v18 shifts again to a plural, spoken, public proclamation aimed at the wall's defenders, וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ בְקוֹל גָּד֜וֹל יְהוּדִ֗ית. None of these three shifts is itself an episode-opener of the kind the Chronicler otherwise uses to break a scene in this chapter -- though the exclusion criterion "fronts an off-line temporal marker" is falsified inside chapter 32 itself: 32:32's fronted nominal closes Hezekiah's reign with no temporal element, and 33:1's nominal age formula likewise has none, yet the sibling row M8-2Chr-139 lists both as belonging to "every other seam in this run" alongside 32:1, 32:9, and 32:24 -- under that wider criterion v17's own fronted-object qatal is precisely such an opener too, and what keeps this block together is referential continuity rather than the temporal-marker test: 32:9's own אַ֣חַר זֶ֗ה שָׁ֠לַח and 32:24's בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה plus qatal both front an off-line temporal marker that vv16-19 never supply -- and the same blasphemy runs through the whole block: v19's summary comparison, מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם, “the work of men's hands”, closes the insult the letters (17) and the proclamation (18) both carried forward. The whole complex therefore stays together under the inset rule as one continuous taunt rather than three separable reports; the single-witness SAMEKH at 32:19 closes it, again as weak, non-driving corroboration. It closes before v20 pivots to an entirely different subject and genre: Hezekiah and Isaiah's prayer.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating v17's letters as their own inset row is the closer rival the strategy names, and under the wider off-line-fronting criterion this cluster's own M8-2Chr-139 applies to 32:32 and 33:1, v17's fronted-object qatal is exactly such an opener; the row nonetheless keeps it here because no resumption formula marks a return to any prior scene after v17, and the same blasphemy referent that v16 signals and v18 proclaims aloud runs continuously through the letters themselves, closed only by v19's summary comparison.

boundary_rationale: A single terse notice, “וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֞ל יְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וִֽישַֽׁעְיָ֧הוּ בֶן אָמ֛וֹץ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל זֹ֑את וַֽיִּזְעֲק֖וּ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם”, reports in third person (not a quoted prayer) that “Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, prayed because of this, and cried to heaven.” The near edge is solid tier-1: a fresh subject pair, the king and the prophet named together, breaks from the preceding blasphemous speech-complex, corroborated (not driven) by the single-witness SAMEKH already disclosed after 32:19. The far edge is thinner and is stated as such rather than propped up by the mark: v21's וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ מַלְאָ֔ךְ, “Yahweh sent an angel”, does install Yahweh as sole acting subject for the first time in the chapter, but unlike every other seam in this run -- 32:1's אַחֲרֵ֨י הַדְּבָרִ֤ים וְהָאֱמֶת֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה, 32:9's אַ֣חַר זֶ֗ה שָׁ֠לַח, 32:24's בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה plus qatal, 32:32's fronted וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י, 33:1's nominal age formula בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה שָׁנָ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ -- v21 fronts nothing off-line; it is a bare wayyiqtol subject change from the human pair of v20. The single-witness PE following v20 is disclosed as tier-3 corroboration only and does not itself decide the seam; the case for keeping v20 as its own beat rests on the subject-and-genre shift alone, human petition giving way to divine action, acknowledged here as the softest boundary in this stretch of the chapter.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this one-verse notice into the deliverance narrative that follows (vv21-23) as a single petition-and-answer unit is a live, closely balanced rival rather than a decisively rejected one; it is set aside only because the petition's own named subject pair and the following verse's shift to Yahweh as sole actor are real actor changes worth keeping as adjoining beats, not because any mark settles the question.

boundary_rationale: Opens with Yahweh as sole grammatical subject, וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ מַלְאָ֔ךְ, sending the angel that annihilates the Assyrian camp's commanders, forcing Sennacherib's shameful retreat and assassination by his own sons in the house of his god (v21) -- an ironic reversal of v17's letter insulting “Yahweh, the God of Israel.” Verse 22 states the theological verdict, “Yahweh saved,” before v23 reports the consequence: gifts pouring in to Yahweh and to Hezekiah, and the king exalted “in the sight of all nations,” closing מֵאַֽחֲרֵי כֵֽן, where a single-witness SAMEKH also falls (tier-3, non-driving, disclosed here alongside the PE already cited at the row's near edge). This is not itself a temporal closure formula: it is the ordinary phrase אחרי כן carrying a prefixed preposition and standing clause-final, adverbial to וַיִּנַּשֵּׂ֛א ('he was exalted... from that point on'), reaching forward past the episode rather than sealing it -- a book-wide sweep finds the phrase family five times (20:1, 20:35, 24:4, 32:23, 33:14), and 32:23 is the only one both prefixed with מן and clause-final; the other four are clause-initial episode-openers. The literary reading of v23 as summarizing a lasting royal consequence still holds, but as inference from content, not from a closural grammatical device. The unit's actual close instead rests on v24's own off-line opener, בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה, a fronted time-frame notice of the kind this chapter uses elsewhere for genuine scene breaks (32:1, 32:9). The row's opening edge, at 32:20/21, is comparatively thinner: as decision 139 discloses, it turns on a bare subject change (from the human petitioners of v20 to Yahweh alone) rather than a fronted off-line marker, so this row's confidence is graded to reflect a firm far edge paired with a softer near edge rather than uniform strength across both.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit back to include v20's prayer notice as one continuous petition-through-consequence arc is a live, closely balanced rival that the row does not deny; v21's pivot to Yahweh as sole actor is what keeps the human petition and the divine response as adjoining but distinct beats, without the PE at 32:20 deciding the question.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the Chronicler's vague compressed-notice marker, בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ עַד לָמ֑וּת, “in those days Hezekiah was sick to the point of death…”, a fresh crisis in subject matter, though its opening demonstrative phrase requires an antecedent, which the text supplies only in the days just narrated at vv21-23; the illness is a different crisis, but the text expressly dates it inside the preceding frame -- an anaphoric time-frame anchoring a fresh subject, not a wholly unconnected one. The three verses trace a complete moral arc: failure to reciprocate God's benefit because “his heart was lifted up,” bringing wrath on him, Judah and Jerusalem (v25); then self-humbling that averts Yahweh's wrath, closing on the adjunct “in the days of Hezekiah” (v26). A book-wide sweep confirms the בִּימֵי+name construction occurs five times in 2Chr (9:20, 13:20, 26:5 twice, 32:26), and v26's is the only clause-final instance among them; one clause-final occurrence cannot constitute a device class, which is exactly the test this cluster's own M8-2Chr-140 applies when it refuses closural force to the unique clause-final adjunct at 32:23. Any retrospective, sealing force in v26's adjunct is content inference from the completed moral arc, not a formula, consistent with how M8-2Chr-140 now treats its own adjunct. Verse 27's fresh clause, וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד, “Hezekiah had exceedingly great riches and honor…”, opens a new topic in its own right, the wealth catalog, even though it is not wholly unconnected to what precedes: 32:31's later definite הַמּוֹפֵת֙, “the portent”, -- the only other occurrence of this noun in the book besides v24's own indefinite וּמוֹפֵ֖ת -- reaches back across the wealth material to name the very sign this row reports, so the illness notice's own vocabulary resurfaces after the catalog rather than being sealed off from it. The seam kept here at 26/27 rests instead on v27's own topic-opening formula and on the pride-and-humbling arc that closes complete in itself at v25-26, sealed by בִּימֵ֖י יְחִזְקִיָּֽהוּ.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping vv24-31 as one undifferentiated closing-notices block is a real rival strengthened by v31's definite הַמּוֹפֵת֙ reaching back to v24's sign, but the moral-closure formula sealing v25-26 still marks the pride-and-humbling episode complete in itself before v27 opens the wealth catalog that v31's own envoys-notice reaches back to answer.

boundary_rationale: Opens the wealth catalog proper, וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד… (treasuries of silver, gold, precious stones, spices and shields, v27; storehouses and stalls, v28; cities and herds WEB “for God had given him abundant possessions.” (v29), then folds in the Gihon engineering feat under the resumptive tag וְה֣וּא יְחִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ, glossed “and this same Hezekiah…” (v30) rather than quoted, a free rendering of the Hebrew rather than WEB’s own wording. Verse 31, introduced by the continuative וְכֵ֞ן, glossed here “and so… with the envoys of… Babylon” (a gloss, not a WEB quotation), does not behave like one more catalog item: its main clause inverts the pattern of vv27-30, which predicate acquisitions and works TO Hezekiah (וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיחִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ, עָֽשָׂה ל֠וֹ), by making God the subject and Hezekiah the object, עֲזָב֖וֹ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֑ים לְנַ֨סּוֹת֔וֹ, “God left him, to test him”; its closing לָדַ֖עַת כָּל בִּלְבָבֽוֹ, “to know all that was in his heart,” continues the same לב root that marked Hezekiah's pride at v25 (כִּ֥י גָבַ֖הּ לִבּ֑וֹ) and his humbling at v26 (בְּגֹ֣בַהּ לִבּ֔וֹ), a moral arc rather than a possession; and its definite הַמּוֹפֵת֙, 'the portent,' is anaphoric to v24's own indefinite וּמוֹפֵ֖ת (the only two occurrences of this noun in the book), pointing back to the illness notice rather than sideways to the treasuries. The row keeps v31 here because its own connective, וְכֵ֞ן, still ties it forward from v30 rather than opening independently, and because 32:32's fresh source-citation formula, expected at exactly this seam per the book strategy, is what actually closes the wealth-and-works material off from the reign's remaining formulas -- but the verse's true content belongs to the pride/humbling/testing arc opened at 32:24, not to the catalog it is grouped with.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching v31 to 141's illness-and-humbling unit (32:24-26) is the stronger rival now on record -- the shared לב root, the God-as-subject/Hezekiah-as-object reversal, and the מופת anaphora to v24 all pull it that direction -- and is only kept here because its own connective ties it forward from v30 and 32:32's source-citation formula is what actually closes this row off, not because the catalog reading is textually stronger.

boundary_rationale: Opens on the recurring reign-closing device, וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ וַחֲסָדָ֑יו הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים בַּחֲז֞וֹן יְשַֽׁעְיָ֤הוּ בֶן אָמוֹץ֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא עַל סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵי יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל, “now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his good deeds…”, citing the vision of Isaiah and “the book of the kings of Judah and Israel”, exactly the source-citation formula the book strategy lists as expected at this verse. It is immediately followed by the standard death-and-succession sequence, וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב יְחִזְקִיָּ֜הוּ עִם אֲבֹתָ֗יו, “Hezekiah slept with his fathers”, burial “in the ascent to the tombs of the sons of David”, national mourning, and closing וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו, “Manasseh his son reigned in his place.” This תַּחְתָּֽיו succession construction recurs twelve times across the book, but it stands verse-initial and reign-opening only once, at 17:1's וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּ֑יו; everywhere else, 32:33 included, it is clause-final, closing the predecessor's own report. Here it closes Hezekiah's, handing the throne to Manasseh, whose own reign narrative (33:1, beyond this part's range) opens instead on the differently-shaped nominal age formula, בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה שָׁנָ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ. A PE mark (single-witness) sits directly after v33, weak corroboration that the reign ends exactly here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: No serious rival groups these two verses with the preceding wealth catalog (vv27-31), since the source-citation formula is a recognized, distinct unit-closing device throughout Chronicles' regnal reports, not a continuation of narrative content.

boundary_rationale: בֶּן שְׁתֵּ֥ים עֶשְׂרֵ֛ה שָׁנָ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וְחָמֵשׁ֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם, ‘Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.’ (v1), opens directly onto the evaluation וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּתֽוֹעֲבוֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, ‘He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, after the abominations of the nations whom Yahweh cast out before the children of Israel’ (v2). From v3's plain narrative continuation, וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּ֨בֶן֙, an unbroken wayyiqtol chain runs the length of the indictment (rebuilt high places, Baal altars, host-of-heaven worship, child sacrifice in Hinnom, the idol set in God's house against Yahweh's own conditional word to David and Solomon) with no off-line opener inside it -- though v3's own opening verb is a plain wayyiqtol continuation, so the chain in fact opens at v4's waw-plus-qatal altar notice, וּבָנָ֥ה מִזְבְּח֖וֹת בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֥ם יִֽהְיֶה שְּׁמִ֖י לְעוֹלָֽם, not at v3, contrasting v5's true wayyiqtol of the same root, וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לְכָל צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בִּשְׁתֵּ֖י חַצְר֥וֹת בֵּית יְהוָֽה; v6's וְהוּא֩ הֶעֱבִ֨יר is a second verse-initial off-line continuation, an emphatic-subject tag of the same kind used at 32:30. Neither 33:4's waw-qatal opener nor 33:6's fronted-pronoun-plus-qatal tag introduces a new participant, setting, or time-frame, so neither breaks the scene; the chain is carried mainly by wayyiqtol with these two off-line continuations, not by an unbroken wayyiqtol run. The chain closes on וַיֶּ֣תַע מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה אֶת יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת רָ֔ע מִן הַ֨גּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הִשְׁמִ֣יד יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, ‘Manasseh seduced Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that they did more evil than did the nations whom Yahweh destroyed before the children of Israel’ (v9), a shared six-word relative clause differing from v2 only in one verb — הוֹרִ֣ישׁ ('cast out') giving way to הִשְׁמִ֣יד ('destroyed') — restating v2's verb-object shape at national scale. That inclusio, not any editorial paragraphing, is what binds vv1-9 into one unit. A PE follows v9 (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only), and the true closing edge is the actor shift at v10's וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה, ‘Yahweh spoke to Manasseh,’ where the subject moves from Manasseh to Yahweh in direct speech.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A bare vv1-2 accession-and-evaluation row, cut off from its catalog, would misrepresent the text: v3's וַיָּ֗שָׁב וַיִּ֨בֶן֙ is a plain wayyiqtol continuation, not one of the book's dating-clause or new-formula boundary types, so it simply illustrates the evil just named in v2 rather than opening a fresh unit.

boundary_rationale: V10's own actor shift, Yahweh replacing Manasseh as grammatical subject in the rejected-word formula, is this row's tier-1 opening warrant. A single WEB paragraph break sits inside this row, before v12, and another falls at the row's own opening edge, before v10; that opening-edge break is tier-4 markup only, alongside the PE trailing v9 (single-witness, tier-3) that the preceding row already carries as its own closing corroboration, and neither is promoted here to an affirmative warrant. Both halves report a single sin-judgment-repentance sequence the Chronicler treats as one theological arc elsewhere in the book. V10 opens the rejected-word formula וַיְדַבֵּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל מְנַשֶּׁ֥ה וְאֶל עַמּ֖וֹ וְלֹ֥א הִקְשִֽׁיבוּ, ‘Yahweh spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they didn’t listen.’, and v11 executes the judgment it threatens. V12 pivots on the distress-clause וּכְהָצֵ֣ר ל֔וֹ חִלָּ֕ה אֶת פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע מְאֹ֔ד מִלִּפְנֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו, ‘When he was in distress, he begged Yahweh his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.’, and the row closes on the recognition formula וַיֵּ֣דַע מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֥וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִֽים, ‘Then Manasseh knew that Yahweh was God.’ (v13), a settled verdict with nothing further until v14's fresh temporal clause. Keeping vv10-13 together preserves the judgment and its reversal as one cause-and-effect unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting before v12 (10-11 vs 12-13) has genuine tier-1 support, not ¶ alone: v12 opens with its own kaph-prefixed infinitive-construct protasis, וּכְהָצֵ֣ר, a time-frame transition independent of WEB's formatting. But the split still isolates the judgment from the very repentance it exists to provoke, and Manasseh's humbling-and-prayer sequence here (וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע ... וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל, vv12-13) realizes the same verb pair as Yahweh's own 7:14 conditions for restoration, וְיִכָּנְע֨וּ עַמִּ֜י ... וְיִֽתְפַּֽלְלוּ֙ וִֽיבַקְשׁ֣וּ פָנַ֔י, lexeme for lexeme — a programmatic fulfillment that only reads as one movement if vv10-13 stay together.

boundary_rationale: וְאַחֲרֵי כֵ֡ן בָּנָ֣ה חוֹמָ֣ה חִֽיצוֹנָ֣ה לְעִיר דָּוִ֡יד, ‘Now after this, he built an outer wall to David’s city’ (v14), is an explicit temporal transition of the same class as the book's other 'after this'-type time-frame openers -- confirmed comparanda at 20:1, 20:35, and 24:4, all clause-initial -- following directly on v13's settled recognition formula, so the topic-change to building and cultic restoration is clearly signaled rather than implied; 32:23's adjunct falls outside this class on form, per M8-2Chr-140, so this row and 140 read the phrase family consistently. The unit runs through the altar-restoration and sacrifice notices of vv15-16 and closes on the caveat אֲבָל֙ ע֣וֹד הָעָ֔ם זֹבְחִ֖ים בַּבָּמ֑וֹת רַ֖ק לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם, ‘Nevertheless the people still sacrificed in the high places, but only to Yahweh their God.’ (v17), which has no further development before v18's source-citation formula, וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁה֮, opens in an entirely different archival register.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v17's high-places caveat into the following source-citation unit (18-20) loses because v17 is still narrating Manasseh's own reign, not yet the 'rest of the acts' regesta formula that begins v18.

boundary_rationale: The row is framed by the reign-closing source-citation formula: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֣י מְנַשֶּׁה֮ וּתְפִלָּת֣וֹ אֶל אֱלֹהָיו֒, ‘Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God’ (v18), shifts register from narrated reform (v17) into archival citation, and v19 restates the citation with an alternate source label ('the history of Hozai'), a doubling that reads as the formula's own expansion rather than a second unit's opening. V20 closes on the death-and-succession pair וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב מְנַשֶּׁה֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֖הוּ בֵּית֑וֹ וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָמ֥וֹן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו, ‘So Manasseh slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house; and Amon his son reigned in his place.’, a formula type that recurs closing reigns elsewhere in this book. A PE follows v20, and WEB's next paragraph begins only at v21 with Amon's own age-formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating v20 as the opening half of Amon's account rather than the close of Manasseh's loses because the death-notice's subject and verb (Manasseh slept, was buried) belong entirely to the outgoing king; Amon's reign begins only with the age-formula at v21.

boundary_rationale: The age-formula pattern shared with every other reign-unit in this run supplies its opening line, בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה אָמ֣וֹן בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁתַּ֣יִם שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם, ‘Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign; and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.’ (v21). A PE, single-witness, tier-3, non-driving, follows the preceding row's own close at 33:20. The evaluation in vv22-23 measures Amon explicitly against his father, וַיַּ֤עַשׂ הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֑יו, ‘He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, as did Manasseh his father’ (v22), and וְלֹ֤א נִכְנַע֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כְּהִכָּנַ֖ע מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה אָבִ֑יו, ‘He didn’t humble himself before Yahweh, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself’ (v23), before the conspiracy report וַיִּקְשְׁר֤וּ עָלָיו֙ עֲבָדָ֔יו וַיְמִיתֻ֖הוּ בְּבֵיתֽוֹ, ‘His servants conspired against him, and put him to death in his own house.’ (v24). Vv24-25 do carry their own formulas — the same conspiracy shape closing Joash's report (הִתְקַשְּׁר֨וּ עָלָ֜יו עֲבָדָ֗יו, 24:25) and Amaziah's (וַיִּקְשְׁר֨וּ עָלָ֥יו קֶ֛שֶׁר, 25:27), and the people-of-the-land enthronement notice recurring for Jehoahaz (וַיַּמְלִיכֻ֥הוּ תַֽחַת אָבִ֖יו, 36:1) — but both remain inside this reign-report rather than opening a new one, since neither the conspiracy notice (v24) nor the enthronement notice (v25) IS an age formula or dating clause in itself -- unlike 34:1's age formula, identical in form to 33:1 and 33:21, which opens the next unit -- and every reign-unit in this run (33:1, 33:21, 34:1) is headed by one, which is why the report closes at v25 and the next unit opens only at 34:1; the report simply narrates its own king's death and successor within one unusually compact unit, closing on Josiah's enthronement at v25, with a PE following (single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v24 to isolate the conspiracy-and-succession notice is a genuinely stronger rival than 'no formula marks it' would suggest: v24's conspiracy formula and v25's people-of-the-land enthronement formula are both real, independently attested devices (24:25, 25:27; 36:1), not silence. But neither is followed by the age-formula or dating clause that opens every other reign-unit in this run, so they still function as this report's own closing notices rather than the head of a new one; the five verses hold together as one unusually compact reign-report.

boundary_rationale: Manasseh, Amon, and now Josiah share one age-formula shape at the head of their reigns: בֶּן שְׁמוֹנֶ֥ה שָׁנִ֖ים יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֑וֹ, ‘Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.’ (v1), paired with the positive evaluation וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה, ‘He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes’ (v2) — one of five uses of this evaluative clause, at the consonantal level, for a favorably-judged king (25:2, 26:4, 27:2, 29:2, 34:2) — reinforced here by the Davidic-conformity clause וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּדַרְכֵי֙ דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֔יו and closing on וְלֹא סָ֖ר יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול, ‘and didn’t turn away to the right hand or to the left,’ which, checked against a book-wide sweep, is unique to this verse as a royal evaluation -- 27:2 alone among the five carries different cantillation, since its own verse continues past the clause, while 25:2, 26:4, 29:2 and 34:2 all close the clause on an atnach; the five remain uninterrupted-string instances all the same, distinguishing them from 24:2's subject-interposed variant; the book's nearest evaluative departure-idiom for a favorably-judged king is the differently-worded וְלֹא סָ֣ר מִמֶּ֑נָּה of Jehoshaphat (20:32). V3 breaks from this with an explicit new dating clause ('in the eighth year... in the twelfth year'), so the row closes before the reform narrative's own chronology begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A vv1-7 row, on the model of Manasseh's undivided vv1-9, would flatten a real difference: Josiah's v3 supplies an explicit dated clause reintroducing the synchronism-style device, rather than simply continuing the evaluation in narrative apposition as Manasseh's v3 does.

boundary_rationale: A double-dated clause reintroduces the year-count device that v2's fixed idiom had just closed off: וּבִשְׁמוֹנֶ֨ה שָׁנִ֜ים לְמָלְכ֗וֹ וְהוּא֙ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ נַ֔עַר הֵחֵ֕ל לִדְר֕וֹשׁ לֵאלֹהֵ֖י דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑יו, ‘in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David his father’ (v3). Vv4-6 extend the purge geographically, from Judah/Jerusalem's Baal-altars to the northern cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and Naphtali, and the campaign closes on the return notice וַיָּ֖שָׁב לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם, ‘then returned to Jerusalem.’ (v7), with a SAMEKH following — a going-out-and-coming-back bracket that closes royal campaigns elsewhere in the book: 19:1's return-to-Jerusalem-in-peace notice closes the Ramoth-gilead campaign, and 20:27's return-to-Jerusalem-with-joy notice closes the Moabite-war campaign. V8's fresh eighteenth-year dating clause opens an unrelated administrative matter, so the boundary out is unusually sharp.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v7's return notice as transitional rather than terminal, folding it forward into v8's temple-repair commissioning, loses not because v8 is severed from the purge campaign — its own לְטַהֵ֥ר הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהַבָּ֑יִת repeats the identical infinitive opening the campaign at v3, הֵחֵל֙ לְטַהֵ֔ר, and the finite form appears again at v5, וַיְטַהֵ֥ר אֶת יְהוּדָ֖ה וְאֶת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם, a purification-verb chain running 34:3, 34:5, 34:8 — but because v8's clause is a subordinate back-reference summarizing a now-finished campaign under its own fresh eighteenth-year dating formula, which is what actually opens the new administrative unit, not a fresh topic severed from the old.

boundary_rationale: Eighteen years into the reign, a fresh dating formula redirects the narrative toward temple funding: וּבִשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁמוֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ לְמָלְכ֔וֹ לְטַהֵ֥ר הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהַבָּ֑יִת שָׁ֠לַח אֶת שָׁפָ֨ן, ‘Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had purged the land and the house, he sent Shaphan’ (v8), following directly on v7's return notice. Vv9-12 form a single administrative chain — money gathered by the Levite gatekeepers, handed to the overseeing workmen, then to carpenters and builders for stone and timber, with named overseers directing skilled Levites — and the row closes on the personnel register itself, וּמֵֽהַלְוִיִּ֔ם סוֹפְרִ֥ים וְשֹׁטְרִ֖ים וְשׁוֹעֲרִֽים, ‘Of the Levites, there were scribes, officials, and gatekeepers.’ (v13), a list-closing formula with nowhere further to extend. WEB opens a fresh paragraph only at v14, where the register gives way to the pivotal discovery notice, וּבְהוֹצִיאָ֣ם אֶת הַכֶּ֔סֶף.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the whole 'money' thread together through v14 loses because v14's clause pivots the narrative onto an entirely different axis — the law-book's discovery — which the register in vv8-13 gives no hint of.

boundary_rationale: Although WEB inserts a paragraph break before v16, vv14-18 form one causally chained event: Hilkiah's discovery, וּבְהוֹצִיאָ֣ם אֶת הַכֶּ֔סֶף הַמּוּבָ֖א בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מָצָא֙ חִלְקִיָּ֣הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֶת סֵ֥פֶר תּֽוֹרַת יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד מֹשֶֽׁה, ‘When they brought out the money that was brought into Yahweh’s house, Hilkiah the priest found the book of Yahweh’s law given by Moses.’ (v14), leads directly to his handing the book to Shaphan (v15), Shaphan's carrying it to the king with his own report (vv16-17), and the reading itself, וַיִּקְרָא ב֥וֹ שָׁפָ֖ן לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ, ‘Shaphan read from it to the king.’ (v18). The seam out sits at v18/v19, where the topic shifts from Shaphan's report-and-reading to the king's own emotional and administrative response; no new dating clause or archival formula interrupts vv14-18 itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The WEB ¶ before v16 (14-15 vs 16-18) has a scene-change in its favor (priest's chamber to throne room), but honoring it here severs the book's single unbroken hand-off chain — found, told, carried, reported, read — into two halves that neither closes on its own.

boundary_rationale: Grief, not reading, is the first note struck here: וַיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י הַתּוֹרָ֑ה וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת בְּגָדָֽיו, ‘When the king had heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.’ (v19), distinct from the reading that closed v18. V20 names the five commissioned officials and opens direct command speech, continuing through v21's rationale for urgency, כִּֽי גְדוֹלָ֤ה חֲמַת יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִתְּכָ֣ה בָ֔נוּ, ‘for great is Yahweh’s wrath that is poured out on us’. A PE follows v21, and v22 shifts to a new grammatical subject and location — ‘So Hilkiah and those whom the king had commanded went to Huldah the prophetess’ — compliance rather than command.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching v22's compliance notice to this row as the command's natural completion loses because v22 introduces a new subject (the delegation, not the king) and a new location (Huldah's quarter), matching the book's usual command-then-separate-compliance pattern rather than one continuous clause.

boundary_rationale: The delegation's errand, not the king's own words, supplies this row's first clause: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ חִלְקִיָּ֜הוּ וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶל חֻלְדָּ֨ה הַנְּבִיאָ֜ה, ‘So Hilkiah and those whom the king had commanded went to Huldah the prophetess’ (v22), and its summarized speech to her ('they spoke to her to that effect') is completed only by her reply, which opens with a first messenger formula relaying instructions to the delegation itself, כֹּה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִמְר֣וּ לָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַ֥ח אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי, ‘Yahweh, the God of Israel says: ‘Tell the man who sent you to me,’ (v23); v22 stays attached to what follows rather than standing alone, since its closing clause names no content of its own. The doom content proper opens only with v24's own independent messenger formula, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה, ‘Yahweh says, ‘Behold, I will bring evil on this place...’ — the book's sole consecutive-verse doubling of this messenger formula (eight total occurrences: 11:4, 12:5, 18:10, 20:15, 21:12, 34:23, 34:24, 34:26) — and runs through the finality clause וְתִתַּ֧ךְ חֲמָתִ֛י בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִכְבֶּֽה, ‘my wrath is poured out on this place, and it will not be quenched’ (v25), before v26's adversative וְאֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה, ‘But to the king of Judah,’ opens a second, contrasting address. WLC marks a SAMEKH after both v22 and v23 (single-witness, weak), sitting exactly at the relay-then-oracle doubling; neither drives the split, since the relay formula (v23) and the doom formula (v24) read as one messenger-speech complex — the first authorizing the second — rather than two separate oracles.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A 22-23/24-25 division at the relay-then-oracle doubling is the strongest rival, since v24 opens its own independent messenger formula heading the actual doom content — a real tier-1 seam, not mere silence — but it still fails: v23's relay formula is what authorizes v24's oracle to be delivered at all, so treating them as separate units would sever one commissioned speech act in two.

boundary_rationale: A sharp adversative pivot launches this row, וְאֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה הַשֹּׁלֵ֤חַ אֶתְכֶם֙ לִדְר֣וֹשׁ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה, ‘But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of Yahweh’ (v26), turning the oracle from the doom just pronounced on 'this place' to a personal word for Josiah grounded in his own tenderness of heart (v27). The unit closes on the compliance-and-return notice וַיָּשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דָּבָֽר, ‘They brought back this message to the king.’ (v28), after which WEB opens a fresh paragraph at v29 with the king's own summons of the elders — prophetic word giving way to royal initiative. A SAMEKH follows v26 (single-witness, weak), internal to this row rather than at either edge, so it neither drives nor undermines the boundaries argued here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this row back into 22-25 as one seven-verse Huldah unit loses the distinctiveness between the two addresses, though not on the ground of 'this place and its inhabitants' — that phrase (עַל הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וְעַל יוֹשְׁבָ֑יו / עַל הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ וְעַל יֹ֣שְׁבָ֔יו / עַל הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וְעַל יֹשְׁבָ֑יו) recurs at 34:24, 27, AND 28 alike and so cannot discriminate the two halves. The real edge is morphological: the doom oracle of vv24-25 never addresses Josiah directly, while from the tail of v26's הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמָֽעְתָּ, 'the words which you have heard,' through v27's second-person forms (לְבָ֨בְךָ֜ / בְּשָׁמְעֲךָ֤ / בְּגָדֶ֖יךָ) and v28's (אֹֽסִפְךָ֜ / אֲבֹתֶ֗יךָ / תִרְאֶ֣ינָה עֵינֶ֔יךָ), second-person forms run continuously — a genuine shift into direct royal address substantial enough to argue for two rows.

boundary_rationale: Royal initiative, not prophetic word, restarts the action here: וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֶּאֱסֹ֕ף אֶת כָּל זִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם, ‘Then the king sent and gathered together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.’ (v29), an assembly-summons device distinct from the prophetic-word register that just closed at v28 with a PE marked. V30 has the king read the covenant book publicly; v31 shifts to the covenant-ratification idiom וַיַּעֲמֹ֨ד הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ עַל עָמְד֗וֹ וַיִּכְרֹ֣ת אֶֽת הַבְּרִית֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֒, ‘The king stood in his place and made a covenant before Yahweh’, kept joined to the summons-and-reading rather than isolated, since both belong to one ceremonial event; v32 extends the covenant to the wider populace and closes on וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּבְרִ֥ית אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽם, ‘The inhabitants of Jerusalem did according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.’ V33 then shifts scope from Jerusalem/Benjamin to 'all the countries... of Israel' and from ceremony-report to a lifetime-fidelity formula, marking the row's close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the public reading (29-30) from the covenant-cutting act (31-32) is a real option — כרת ברית is a distinct legal-ritual idiom from the reading that precedes it — but the two remain one uninterrupted ceremony in the text, with no dating clause, ¶, or change of participants separating them.

boundary_rationale: This single verse pivots scope and register at once: וַיָּ֨סַר יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֜הוּ אֶת כָּל הַתּוֹעֵב֗וֹת מִֽכָּל הָאֲרָצוֹת֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒, ‘Josiah took away all the abominations out of all the countries that belonged to the children of Israel’, widens v32's local Jerusalem-and-Benjamin frame to the whole territory of Israel, and the verse closes on the lifetime-fidelity idiom כָּל יָמָ֕יו לֹ֣א סָ֔רוּ מֵֽאַחֲרֵ֕י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽם, ‘All his days they didn’t depart from following Yahweh, the God of their fathers.’ — a summary formula with no ceremonial content of its own, unlike the concrete assembly-and-covenant acts of vv29-32. A PE follows v33, matching this part's assigned close ahead of the distinct Passover cultic-action opening of the next unit (35:1, outside this part's range).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding v33 into the covenant-assembly row (29-33) as its natural conclusion loses because v33's own grammar and geography step outside the assembly just narrated — a nationwide summary rather than a further covenant act performed at Jerusalem.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a fresh royal-action heading rather than a continuation of the covenant-renewal material closing ch34: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ יֹאשִׁיָּ֧הוּ בִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם פֶּ֖סַח לַיהוָ֑ה, ‘Josiah kept a Passover to Yahweh in Jerusalem’ (v1, quoted in full; nothing is elided), which WEB likewise renders as a flat topic-opening declarative. From there an unbroken wayyiqtol chain runs through the priestly stationing at v2 (וַיַּעֲמֵ֥ד הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים עַל מִשְׁמְרוֹתָ֑ם וַֽיְחַזְּקֵ֔ם, ‘He set the priests in their offices and encouraged them’) into direct royal speech, opened by the tier-1 speech frame וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לַ֠לְוִיִּם, WEB's ‘He said to the Levites who taught all Israel’ (v3), instructing them to house the ark and organize by division; the speech itself closes on the Mosaic-authority tag לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כִּדְבַר יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַד מֹשֶֽׁה, ‘according to Yahweh’s word by Moses’ (v6, WEB's own wording; ‘by the hand of’ is a literal gloss of בְּיַד not present in WEB), with a PE tucked in right after it (single-witness, tier-3 only). Verse 7 breaks the pattern with a new subject-verb pairing, וַיָּ֣רֶם יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ, WEB's ‘Josiah gave to the children of the people’, shifting register from command to gift list, so the charge-unit closes at v6 rather than absorbing it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuine rival, under the INSET RULE's own two-part test, is a 35:1-2/35:3-6 split: v3's וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לַ֠לְוִיִּם supplies an opening speech frame and v7's וַיָּ֣רֶם יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ supplies a resumption after, which is exactly what the rule requires to isolate an inset. It still fails on host-unit integrity: the charge itself (vv3-6) has no narrative resumption of its own inside the span — nothing reports the Levites acting on the instruction before v7 moves to the king's own gifts — and vv1-2 supply the very occasion (the Passover, the priestly stationing) that the imperatives of vv3-6 presuppose, so the two halves read as one continuous inception notice rather than a host narrative plus a detachable inset.

boundary_rationale: A new register begins where the king's own gift is tallied, וַיָּ֣רֶם יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ, WEB's ‘Josiah gave to the children of the people’ (v7) — thirty thousand animals from the flock, three thousand cattle — followed by the identical tally shape applied to his officials, וְשָׂרָ֞יו לִנְדָבָ֥ה, WEB's ‘His princes gave a free will offering to the people’ (v8, naming Hilkiah, Zechariah, Jehiel), and again to the Levite chiefs at v9 — the consonantal line opens וכונניהו with qere וְ֠כָֽנַנְיָהוּ, followed by וּשְׁמַֽעְיָ֨הוּ and the rest of the named list; the ketiv/qere pair covers only the first name, and וּשְׁמַֽעְיָ֨הוּ is simply the next donor, Shemaiah, in the list with no ketiv counterpart of its own. Each tier repeats donor-then-livestock-count, so the three verses read as one triadic tally rather than three independent notices. A SAMEKH trails v7 (single-witness, tier-3) — squarely inside this list — but a mark of that weight cannot outrank the matching threefold form binding the king's gift to the two that follow it. The tally closes before v10 switches into a completion-formula register describing the priests and Levites taking their stations.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the SAMEKH after v7 as a hard break would peel the king’s gift away from the two parallel donor tiers sharing its exact list-form — a tier-3 mark overruling a matched internal pattern is the weaker call.

boundary_rationale: An establishment-formula opens this execution report, וַתִּכּ֖וֹן הָעֲבוֹדָ֑ה ... כְּמִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ, WEB's ‘So the service was prepared... according to the king’s commandment’ (v10), and its own scaled echo closes it, וַ֠תִּכּוֹן כָּל עֲבוֹדַ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה ... כְּמִצְוַ֖ת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ, WEB's ‘So all the service of Yahweh was prepared the same day... according to the commandment of King Josiah’ (v16) — the same root widened from ‘the service’ to ‘all the service of Yahweh’ and from the bare ‘king’ to ‘King Josiah’ by name.
