Between the two brackets the priests and Levites slaughter, sprinkle, portion, and roast the offerings (vv11-13, wayyiqtol-driven -- v11 in fact ends on a subject-plus-participle clause with no finite verb, and v13 has a fronted-object plain-qatal middle clause before the wayyiqtol resumes, so the report already tolerates a participial clause and a fronted-object qatal inside vv11-13, which strengthens rather than weakens the parenthesis reading of vv14-15's own qatal/verbless register against a 10-13/14-15 split), before the register shifts to qatal at v14's doubled הֵכִ֤ינוּ ... הֵכִ֣ינוּ and a verbless clause at v15 naming the singers' and gatekeepers' standing posts, וְהַמְשֹֽׁרֲרִ֨ים בְּנֵי אָסָ֜ף עַל מַעֲמָדָ֗ם — a parenthetical aside on staffing that v16's wayyiqtol resumes and completes, rather than a break in the report. Because v16 restates and completes v10's own verb rather than opening fresh material, it reads as the closing half of a matched inclusio, not the head of what follows; v17 shifts the acting subject away from the cultic staff to the wider populace, וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֛ים אֶת הַפֶּ֖סַח, WEB's ‘The children of Israel who were present kept the Passover’ — a scene change strong enough to open the next unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v16 as the opening line of the following national-observance summary is plausible on WEB's own paragraph break, which falls before v16, but the repeated root and shared 'commandment of the king' phrasing tie it back to v10 more tightly than forward to v17's population-focused clause; and the qatal/verbless staffing note in vv14-15 is best read as a parenthesis within this same execution report, not as a rival internal seam, since v16's wayyiqtol picks the report's own chain back up.

boundary_rationale: This unit's opening edge is the same one M8-2Chr-160 closes on: that row's completion-formula inclusio (וַתִּכּ֖וֹן הָעֲבוֹדָ֑ה v10 / וַ֠תִּכּוֹן כָּל עֲבוֹדַ֨ת יְהוָ֜ה v16) ends the cultic-execution report, and v17's shift to a new subject, וַיַּעֲשׂ֨וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֛ים אֶת הַפֶּ֖סַח, opens this national-observance unit rather than continuing that report. From there the claim widens into a superlative: וְלֹֽא נַעֲשָׂ֨ה פֶ֤סַח כָּמֹ֨הוּ֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל, ‘there was not made a Passover like it in Israel’ (v18), reaching back to Samuel's day, and the unit closes on the regnal date anchoring that same claim, בִּשְׁמוֹנֶ֤ה עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה לְמַלְכ֖וּת יֹאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ נַעֲשָׂ֖ה הַפֶּ֥סַח הַזֶּֽה, ‘in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign this Passover was kept’ (v19), whose demonstrative 'this Passover' reaches back to the whole celebration reported from v16's לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הַפֶּ֔סַח and v17's אֶת הַפֶּ֖סַח onward, not narrowly to v18's comparison alone. A SAMEKH sits between v18 and v19 (single-witness, tier-3) at exactly the point where the superlative claim meets its own date-stamp, but the mark falls inside one continuing sentence-pair rather than at a seam. The next verse opens an unrelated time-frame formula for Necho's campaign, which gives this unit its outer edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at the SAMEKH between v18 and v19 would strand the date-stamp from the very celebration it dates, since v19's demonstrative 'this Passover' reaches back to the whole report from v16 onward and points nowhere else for its referent.

boundary_rationale: A time-frame formula opens the unit and pivots away from the Passover material entirely: אַחֲרֵ֣י כָל זֹ֗את אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵכִ֤ין יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ֙, ‘After all this, when Josiah had prepared the temple’ (v20), introducing Necho's march on Carchemish and Josiah's decision to intercept him. The relative clause quoted here points back to the temple-service preparation summarized at 35:16, the opposite of a total pivot; the edge holds because the new finite verb launching Necho's campaign follows, not because the formula severs every backward connection. The action runs unbroken through the wounding and return to Jerusalem into the paired death-and-burial notice, וַיָּ֕מָת וַיִּקָּבֵ֖ר, ‘and he died and was buried’, and the mourning that follows, מִֽתְאַבְּלִ֖ים עַל יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ, ‘mourning for Josiah’ (v24), before closing on the elaboration of that same mourning into a fixed custom — Jeremiah's dirge, the singers' laments — ending on a written-record notice, וְהִנָּ֥ם כְּתוּבִ֖ים עַל הַקִּינֽוֹת, ‘behold, they are written among the laments’ (v25). A PE trails v24 (single-witness), sitting right at the join between the burial/mourning notice and the lament report, and it is a genuinely stronger rival seam than most marks in this part offer — but rather than sharing v24's subject, v25 in fact introduces two fresh named subjects of its own, יִרְמְיָהוּ֮ and כָֽל הַשָּׁרִ֣ים וְ֠הַשָּׁרוֹת; what ties the two verses is the repeated grief-object עַל יֹאשִׁיָּֽהוּ, closing v24 and recurring twice more in v25 (בְּקִינ֨וֹתֵיהֶ֤ם עַל יֹאשִׁיָּ֨הוּ֙), so the tier-3 mark still falls inside one continuing grieving report rather than at a seam. The following verse pivots the register entirely to bibliographic citation, giving this unit its far edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The PE after v24 could be read as closing the death narrative proper (vv20-24) apart from the lament report (v25), but v24's own closing clause already explicitly names the whole populace, Judah and Jerusalem, as mourners, so v25 does not fill a gap v24 leaves open; it instead adds named mourners, Jeremiah and then the singers, and a durative extension of the custom on top of the populace-wide grief v24 already reports, so severing it at the mark still strands half of one continuous grieving notice held together by the repeated grief-object.

boundary_rationale: Josiah’s reign closes on the Chronicler’s bibliographic tag, opening וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ, literally ‘and the remainder of the words of Josiah’ (v26), and running through the paired first-and-last citation, עַל סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִיהוּדָֽה, ‘[written] in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah’ (v27). The same ‘rest of the acts of X ... written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah’ shape recurs within this very part at 36:8 for Jehoiakim, so this is not a one-off flourish but a closing register this part repeats when a reign ends — distinct in form from the narrative report in vv20-25 (action and grief) and from v25’s own written-record notice, which names ‘the laments’ specifically rather than the royal chronicle generally. Two different citation traditions sit back to back in the text, and only the second is this unit’s own genre.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Absorbing this formula into the preceding death-and-lament report would blur a self-contained bibliographic genre into the narrative it closes, and 36:8’s matching formula shows this shape is a recurring unit-closer within this part, not an extension of v25’s lament notice.

boundary_rationale: Jehoahaz’s brief reign opens not with the age-formula alone but with a populace-installation clause first: וַיִּקְחוּ֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ אֶת יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז, ‘the people of the land took Jehoahaz’ (v1), then the standard age-notice, בֶּן שָׁל֧וֹשׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים שָׁנָ֖ה, ‘twenty-three years old’ (v2) — a three-month reign, the shortest recorded here. The report tracks Egypt’s deposition of him, the fine levied on the land, and Necho’s installation of a replacement brother, closing on Jehoahaz’s own removal, וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ מִצְרָֽיְמָה, ‘and he brought him to Egypt’ (v4), with a PE sitting just after it (single-witness). The Joahaz/Jehoahaz spelling alternation between v1's יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז and vv2/4's יוֹאָחָ֣ז / יוֹאָחָ֤ז is a genuine MT orthographic feature, not merely a translator's footnote choice (WEB's note only reports it); it still carries no weight here, since name-spelling is not one of the tier-1 device classes and the shift itself falls between v1 and v2, inside the span rather than at either edge. What closes this unit is the same age-formula device opening again at v5 for Jehoiakim — and again at v9 and v11 for Jehoiachin and Zedekiah — so the seam-out at v5 is the first of three repeats of one identical accession marker within this same chapter.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Grouping vv1-4 with Jehoiakim’s notice (vv5-8) into one ‘two short kings’ unit would erase the age-formula seam at v5, which recurs unaltered twice more later in this chapter.

boundary_rationale: The age-formula reopens for a new reign, בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙, ‘twenty-five years old’ (v5), followed at once by the evil-notice and then Nebuchadnezzar’s binding of Jehoiakim and the removal of temple vessels to Babylon (vv6-7). The unit closes on a double formula, both parts present intact: the citation heading וְיֶתֶר֩ דִּבְרֵ֨י יְהֽוֹיָקִ֜ים, ‘now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim’, running straight into the successor-installation clause וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו, ‘and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place’ (v8), trailed by a PE (single-witness) — echoing the same tier-1-formula-plus-tier-3-mark convergence already seen closing v4. Of the four reigns compressed into this chapter, only Jehoiakim’s retains the citation-and-succession pairing in full; Jehoiachin’s notice just below drops the citation half entirely (its own close is a bare deportation-and-succession clause at v10), which sharpens rather than blurs this unit’s edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit through v10 to absorb Jehoiachin’s installation would splice the citation formula closing Jehoiakim’s reign onto an unrelated age-formula opening a fresh one at v9.

boundary_rationale: A fresh age-formula opens Jehoiachin's own notice, בֶּן שְׁמוֹנֶ֤ה שָׁנִים֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין, ‘eight years old, Jehoiachin’ (v9) — וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ וַעֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֔ים, three months and ten days, a brief reign but not the chapter's shortest, since Jehoahaz's three months (36:2, argued in M8-2Chr-164) runs ten days shorter still — followed by the evil-notice and then his deportation with the temple's valuable vessels. The unit closes on a different installation device than v8's: not the succession formula וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו closing Jehoiakim's report, where the incoming king himself is subject, but the causative וַיַּמְלֵךְ֙ אֶת צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ אָחִ֔יו עַל יְהוּדָ֖ה וִֽירוּשָׁלִָֽם, ‘and he made Zedekiah his brother king’ (v10), where the appointee is an accusative object under an agent left unexpressed within its own clause -- although the verse has already named Nebuchadnezzar earlier in the same sentence, וְלִתְשׁוּבַ֣ת הַשָּׁנָ֗ה שָׁלַח֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֔ר… — the same construction, stem for stem, as v4's foreign king installing Eliakim, וַיַּמְלֵ֨ךְ מֶֽלֶךְ מִצְרַ֜יִם אֶת אֶלְיָקִ֣ים אָחִ֗יו עַל יְהוּדָה֙ וִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם, with a PE marked at its heel (single-witness). This reign carries no 'rest of his acts' citation at all — the deportation notice stands in its place — but that omission is a feature of the compressed regnal-report form here, not a weakening of the boundary itself: a sweep of the chapter's first three reign-units falsifies the generalization that the age-formula opening and causative-installation closing pair marks all three: unit 2 (Jehoiakim, vv5-8) closes on v8's Qal succession formula, not a causative clause; unit 2's own causative appointment (v4) stands mid-verse, not at the close; and unit 1 (Jehoahaz) opens on the causative v1, with the age-formula arriving only at v2, not at the head. The pairing holds in full only for this reign, vv9-10 (Jehoiachin); Zedekiah's own report (v11 on) closes differently, on no installation formula at all. This reign opens on the recurring age-formula and closes on a causative appointment clause whose only true parallel in the chapter is v4.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v10 as an appendix tacked onto Jehoiakim’s block (vv5-8) rather than the close of Jehoiachin’s own notice would ignore that v9 opens with the identical age-formula launching every other reign here.

boundary_rationale: Zedekiah's reign opens with the chapter's fourth and final age-formula, בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְאַחַ֛ת שָׁנָ֖ה צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ, ‘twenty-one years old, Zedekiah’ (v11), then narrates his refusal to humble himself before Jeremiah and his broken oath of loyalty to Nebuchadnezzar, the rebellion clause heading v13 in full, so the two additive particles stand at the head of consecutive verses, ‘he also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar’ (vv12-13). From there the indictment widens past the king to the priestly and popular leadership, entering for the first time under the matching particle, גַּ֠ם כָּל שָׂרֵ֨י הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְהָעָם֙ הִרְבּ֣וּ, ‘moreover all the chiefs of the priests and the people trespassed’ (v14), and closing on their desecration of the temple, וַֽיְטַמְּאוּ֙ אֶת בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִקְדִּ֖ישׁ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם, ‘they polluted the house of Yahweh which he had made holy in Jerusalem’ (v14). Whether v14 belongs here or opens the divine-response material that follows is a genuine fork, not a manufactured one: what ties it to vv11-13 is not repeated actors — the priests and people are new to the scene at v14 — but the additive particle chain running from v13's own head into v14, a particle this chapter uses only one more time, at v22 (three hits total), while v15 turns the subject to Yahweh's own initiative, so the corporate-guilt clause is kept as this unit's low point rather than promoted to the head of the next.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating v14 as the opening line of a guilt-then-response arc (vv14-16) is defensible given the tight causal link, but v14's own additive particle ties it backward to v13's matching particle rather than forward — the same subject-change from human to divine that would open a v14-16 unit already happens one verse later, at v15, not at v14 itself.

boundary_rationale: The acting subject turns from the corporate guilt just narrated to Yahweh's own repeated initiative, וַיִּשְׁלַ֡ח יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֧ם עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם בְּיַ֥ד מַלְאָכָ֖יו הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְשָׁל֑וֹחַ כִּֽי חָמַ֥ל עַל עַמּ֖וֹ וְעַל מְעוֹנֽוֹ, ‘Yahweh, the God of their fathers, sent to them by the hand of his messengers, rising up early and sending, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place’ (v15) — the doubled infinitive-absolute pairing (הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְשָׁל֑וֹחַ) casting the sending as a repeated, iterative act — met with mockery in a cumulative summary building to the point of no return, עַ֠ד עֲל֧וֹת חֲמַת יְהוָ֛ה בְּעַמּ֖וֹ עַד לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא, ‘until Yahweh's wrath arose against his people, until there was no remedy’ (v16, paralleled in 2Chr only at 21:18's לָחֳלִ֖י לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא, both marking a point of irreversible ruin). This two-verse hinge both explains everything narrated since v11 and licenses the invasion that follows; its far edge rests not on a change of grammatical subject — Yahweh remains the operative subject into v17, where וַיַּ֨עַל עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ כשדיים כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים brings the Chaldean king on stage only as the accusative object of Yahweh's own action, and הַכֹּ֖ל נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ still needs Yahweh as its giver — but on the shift from vv15-16's iterative, summarizing register (repeated sending, cumulative mockery) to v17's punctual narrative action (a single punctual invasion, executed and complete). That shift is real but is not one of the book's named tier-1 formula types, and it sits inside the exile-compression stretch already flagged as thin ground for confident calls; graded down accordingly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding vv15-16 forward into the Chaldean-invasion report (v17 on) as one cause-and-effect sweep has real appeal, and it is reinforced by the book's only other use of the compassion verb: כִּֽי חָמַ֥ל עַל עַמּ֖וֹ (v15) is answered by וְלֹ֥א חָמַ֛ל עַל בָּח֥וּר וּבְתוּלָ֖ה (v17), a positive-then-negative pair found nowhere else in 2Chr, straddling this exact seam — read as one deliberate antithesis, it would argue against splitting here at all. That pairing can also be composed across a genuine boundary, though, so it is weighed rather than decisive; what is judged the stronger case for keeping the split is the register shift itself, iterative divine patience versus a punctual invasion narrative, since no new grammatical agent actually enters at v17 to carry the break on its own.

boundary_rationale: The wrath just declared at v16's terminal עַד לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא, 'until there was no remedy' (its only other occurrence in the book, 21:18's לָחֳלִ֖י לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא, likewise seals off a moment past hope), is now executed: Yahweh — still the operative subject continuing from v15's וַיִּשְׁלַ֡ח יְהוָה֩ — וַיַּ֨עַל עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת מֶ֣לֶךְ כשדיים כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים, 'brought up against them the king of' the Chaldeans (v17), the gentilic itself the only genuinely new element here (ketiv כשדיים, qere כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים), since Nebuchadnezzar is already named four times earlier in this chapter (נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר 36:6, נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר 36:7, נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֔ר 36:10, נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּר֙ 36:13); the opening pivot is not a new agent entering but the shift from prophetic-messenger action (vv15-16) to military execution, sparing no age group. The report moves through the seizure of every treasury (v18) into the burning of the temple, city wall, and palaces, וַֽיִּשְׂרְפוּ֙ אֶת בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים, 'they burned the house of God', and וַֽיְנַתְּצ֔וּ אֵ֖ת חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם, '[they] broke down the wall of Jerusalem' (v19, plural verbs throughout, trailing a SAMEKH, single-witness), then a pivot to a singular subject at v20's וַיֶּ֛גֶל הַשְּׁאֵרִ֥ית, 'he carried away the remnant' -- וַֽיִּהְיוּ ל֤וֹ וּלְבָנָיו֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים, 'they were servants to him and his sons' is 3mp ('and they were'), referring to the deported remnant collectively, not singular: an independent sweep (5:8, 13:13, 20:25, 24:12, 24:14) confirms this verb form is plural throughout the book, and a plural verb cannot itself confirm the number of the earlier, grammatically unrelated 3ms verb of exile; the element that actually continues a singular referent into the clause is instead the singular pronominal suffix in the following word, 'to him', running עַד מְלֹ֖ךְ מַלְכ֥וּת פָּרָֽס, 'until the reign of the kingdom of Persia' (v20). V21's purpose infinitive, לְמַלֹּ֖אות שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה, 'to fulfill... seventy years', depends grammatically on v20's own finite וַיֶּ֛גֶל rather than standing free, so it cannot be detached from it; that dependency, not agent continuity, is what actually holds vv20-21 to what precedes. V21 is the strongest formal closer still available at this point in the stretch — not, as an unqualified superlative would claim, the strongest anywhere in it, since the source-citation series (וְיֶתֶר֩ דִּבְרֵ֨י יְהֽוֹיָקִ֜ים, its tenth and final member) already closed the same 36:1-21 material at v8 — and a fresh dating formula opens the Cyrus material immediately after v21, which is why the unit is capped here, even though it sits on ground the book strategy already flags as thin.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the destruction notices (vv17-19) from the exile-and-fulfillment notices (vv20-21) at the SAMEKH after v19 has a real tier-1 signal behind it that 'the same agent governs both halves' does not capture: v19's destruction verbs are all 3mp (וַֽיִּשְׂרְפוּ֙, וַֽיְנַתְּצ֔וּ, שָׂרְפ֣וּ) while v20 opens 3ms. It still fails: 36:21 contains two occurrences of the purpose infinitive. The verse-final one immediately follows and completes a finite qal perfect governed by 'all the days of its desolation' within v21 itself, an independent clause the row concedes elsewhere; the infinitive that actually rides grammatically on v20's finite verb is the verse-initial one, opening v21. A verse opening on a bare purpose infinitive cannot head a unit on its own, which defeats the 19/20 split without denying that v21 supplies its own independent clause.

boundary_rationale: A new regnal dating formula opens the book's final unit, וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֗ת לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס, ‘in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia’ (v22), explicitly framed as the fulfillment of Jeremiah's word, לִכְל֥וֹת דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ, ‘that Yahweh's word by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished’ — a near-verbatim echo of v21's own purpose clause, לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ, ‘to fulfill Yahweh's word by Jeremiah's mouth’. The echo is deliberate bracketing, not grounds for folding v22 backward into v21: each purpose-infinitive rides its own independent finite verb — v21's on v20's וַיֶּ֛גֶל, v22's own on הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה, ‘Yahweh stirred up’ — so the two verses supply parallel but syntactically distinct fulfillment-frames bracketing the exile's start and the return's start respectively. The notice pivots from third-person narration of Cyrus's proclamation into Cyrus's own first-person edict, closing on the protasis-apodosis מִֽי בָכֶ֣ם מִכָּל עַמּ֗וֹ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהָ֛יו עִמּ֖וֹ וְיָֽעַל, ‘whoever is among you of all his people, Yahweh his God be with him, and let him go up’ (v23) — a third-person apocopated jussive, וְיָֽעַל, not an imperative, distinguished from the wayyiqtol doubling pattern of v17's וַיַּ֨עַל by its simple conjunctive waw. A SAMEKH trails v22 (single-witness) between the narrated notice and Cyrus's quoted speech, span-internal rather than corroborating either outer edge; the PE keyed to v21 (single-witness), already carried in the refs, is what corroborates this unit's opening edge. The Ezra 1:1-3 overlap in this material is cross-book metadata under the book strategy's synoptic-discipline rule and plays no role in setting this boundary; the pair stands as its own closing unit regardless.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v22 as the tail of the preceding exile-and-fulfillment report (folding it into vv17-21) rather than the head of the Cyrus unit would strip the dating formula from the edict it introduces. It is not, as it might seem, blocked merely because v21 stands complete without v22: v21's own purpose clause, לְמַלֹּ֤אות דְּבַר יְהוָה֙ בְּפִ֣י יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ, is a bare infinitive construct with no finite verb of its own — riding on v20's וַיֶּ֛גֶל — and the verse's one truly independent clause, כָּל יְמֵ֤י הָשַּׁמָּה֙ שָׁבָ֔תָה, is not the fulfillment clause at all. What actually blocks the fold is v22's own new finite verb and new dating formula launching a fresh, independent notice rather than continuing v21's dependent purpose clause.
